set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 Birds are animals that, like mammals, maintain a constant body temperature, and their skins are covered in feathers. Birds lay eggs covered with a hard shell on land, and don’t have external ears.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A yeast ( Saccharomyces cerevisiae),  glucose and water are mixed in a test tube. 
 The diagrams show the test tube at the start and after one hour. 
  Which process causes this change?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (respiration) because:
 Yeast is a living organism that can respire both aerobically and anaerobically. The gas carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) is always produced as one of the waste products, the main point of the reaction being to release energy. The bubbles of gas seen after one hour are bubbles of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ).
 A  is incorrect because reproduction is the process by which more of the same kind of organism is made and doesn’t directly result in the release of carbon dioxide.
 C  is incorrect because growth is a permanent increase in size and dry mass caused by an increase in cell number or cell size (or both).
 D  is incorrect because sensitivity is the ability to detect or sense stimuli in the internal or external environment and to make appropriate responses.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The image below shows a house mouse, whose scientific name is  Mus musculus .
  Which genus does it belong to?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  ( Mus ) because:
 • In the binomial system of naming developed by Linnaeus, the first name of the two is the genus that the organism belongs to. It is always written with a capital letter
 • The second name is the name of its species and always has a small initial letter. Both should be  italic ised
 A  is incorrect because mammal is the class that the house mouse belongs to.
 B  is incorrect because musculus is the species name (it begins with a lower case m).
 D  is incorrect because a vertebrate is the phylum that the house mouse belongs to.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The salivary glands contain cells which are responsible for producing salivary amylase, a digestive enzyme.
 Which organelles would be present in large numbers in cells of the salivary glands?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  (mitochondria and ribosomes) because:
 • Salivary amylase is an  enzyme ; enzymes are made from  protein .  Ribosomes  are the site of  protein synthesis  in all cells
 • Production of proteins requires significant amounts of  energy  and therefore cells which manufacture digestive enzymes. that need to be made and then transported out of the cell would contain a lot of  mitochondria , as this is where respiration takes place
 A  and  B  are incorrect because although mitochondria and ribosomes would be required in large numbers, each cell only ever possesses one nucleus. 
 C  is incorrect because vacuoles are present in plant cells; salivary glands are animal cells.

 The other answers are incorrect because they do not show the correct structures present in bacterial cells.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which row of the table below correctly matches functions to some of the components in a root hair cell?
 |  
 | cell wall
 | cell membrane
 | mitochondria
 |
 | A
 |  support
 |  active transport
 |  energy release
 |
 | B
 |  energy release
 |  active transport
 |  nutrition
 |
 | C
 |  support
 |  active transport
 |  nutrition
 |
 | D
 |  active transport
 |  support
 |  energy release
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • The cell membrane is partially permeable and controls the movement of substances into the cell by osmosis, diffusion and active transport
 • The cell wall is fully permeable and therefore does not control the movement of any substances, all move through it
 • The cell wall (in plants) is made of cellulose, a polysaccharide that forms fibres which criss-cross over each other to form a very strong support for the cell
 • Mitochondria are where most energy is released in the cell (via respiration)
 The other rows are incorrect as they do not correctly describe the functions of the components of the root hair cell.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The image below shows two solutions separated by a partially permeable membrane.
  Which of the statements below would be true in relation to the image?
options: A. There is no net movement of water from W to X
B. There would be movement of water molecules from W to X
C. Osmosis of sugar molecules would occur from the dilute solution (W) to the concentrated solution (X)
D. Solution X is more dilute and therefore has a higher water potential than solution W
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (There would be movement of water molecules from W to X) because:
 • Osmosis is the  net  movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential (dilute solution) to a region of lower water potential (concentrated solution), through a partially permeable membrane
 • Net movement’ means ‘overall movement’ -  more  water molecules will move from solution W to solution X, but water molecules are able to move in either direction (they don’t choose to move from one solution to another, because they can’t tell if the solution they’re in is dilute or concentrated)
 A  is incorrect because the net movement of water would be from W (dilute solution) to X (concentrated solution).
 C  is incorrect because osmosis only refers to the movement of water molecules, not sugar molecules.
 D  is incorrect because solution X is more concentrated than W since there are more sugar molecules and less free water molecules in X.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A number of red blood cells were immersed in pure water before being observed under a microscope. There was a dramatic change in their appearance. 
 Which row of the table below correctly describes what happened to the red blood cells?
 |  
 | direction of water movement
 | from higher to lower solute concentration
 | from higher to lower water potential
 | effect
 |
 | A
 | in
 | ✓
 | X
 | cells burst
 |
 | B
 | in
 | X
 | ✓
 | cells burst
 |
 | C
 | out
 | ✓
 | X
 | cells shrink
 |
 | D
 | out
 | ✓
 | ✓
 | cells shrink
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Pure water has a solute concentration of zero and has the highest possible water potential
 • Water will therefore move  into red blood cells  by osmosis when they are placed in pure water
 • Water moves from  low to high solute concentration  and from  high to  low water potential  through a partially permeable membrane
 • This will cause the cells to swell and eventually  burst

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The drawing shows a food test being carried out in a laboratory.
  Which food test is being shown and which food group is being tested for?
options: B. DCPIP test for Vitamin C
C. Benedict's test for reducing sugars
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (Benedict's test for reducing sugars) because:
 The Benedict's test requires a heating step and a colour change is observed in a positive test.
 A  is incorrect because the test for protein (the Biuret test) does not require a heating step, even though a colour change is observed in a positive protein test. 
 B  is incorrect because the test for Vitamin C (using DCPIP) does not require a heating step, even though a colour change is observed in a positive protein test.  
 D  is incorrect because the emulsion test for fats (using ethanol and water) does not require a heating step. This would also be dangerous, with flammable ethanol near a naked flame.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A student decided to investigate the effect of pH on the activity of the enzyme lipase.
 Five different test tubes are set up. Each test tube contains a mixture of the enzyme lipase and its substrate, a lipid.
 Which condition should not be kept the same in each of the five test tubes?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.  (pH) because:
 If the condition being investigated is pH, then this is the  independent   variable  and should be different in each test tube to get a good range of results.
 A  is incorrect because the temperature is one factor that can affect enzyme activity and should not be changed if pH is being altered.
 B  is incorrect because the concentration of the enzyme is another factor that needs to be kept the same (not changed) to make the experiment fair as it can also affect enzyme activity.
 C  is incorrect because the volume of the lipid solution is one of the things that needs to be kept the same to make the experiment valid; the more lipid (substrate) there is, the longer it will take for the reaction to complete.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which of the following options is the best explanation for the role of chlorophyll in photosynthesis?
 Chlorophyll...
options: A. transfers light energy from the Sun because it has magnesium ions
B. transfers chemical potential energy from sunlight into organic molecules which can be used to synthesise carbohydrates such as glucose
C. transfers light energy from the Sun into chemical energy in inorganic molecules which can be used for growth
D. transfers light energy into chemical potential energy in glucose molecules which are used in the synthesis of other carbohydrates
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  (transfers light energy into chemical potential energy in glucose molecules which are used in the synthesis of other carbohydrates) because:
 • chlorophyll absorbs light energy (from the Sun or artificial light sources)
 • light energy is used to drive a reaction between water and carbon dioxide, producing glucose (a carbohydrate)
 • glucose can be converted into other carbohydrates, such as sucrose, starch and cellulose
 A  is incorrect because chlorophyll molecules do contain magnesium ions, but this doesn’t outline its role in photosynthesis.
 B  is incorrect because chlorophyll absorbs light energy, not chemical potential energy, to drive the synthesis of organic molecules such as glucose (light energy is transferred to chemical potential energy stored in the bonds of glucose molecules).
 C  is incorrect because chlorophyll absorbs energy from sunlight to drive reactions between inorganic molecules (carbon dioxide and water) to produce glucose (an organic

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The average number of chloroplasts found in four different types of cell from the leaf of a plant are shown in the bar chart below.
  What are the names of the four types of cell?
 |  
 | 1
 | 2
 | 3
 | 4
 |
 | A
 | spongy mesophyll cell
 | epidermal cell
 | palisade mesophyll cell
 | guard cell
 |
 | B
 | palisade mesophyll cell
 | guard cell
 | spongy mesophyll cell
 | epidermal cell
 |
 | C
 | epidermal cell
 | spongy mesophyll cell
 | palisade mesophyll cell
 | guard cell
 |
 | D
 | palisade mesophyll cell
 | spongy mesophyll cell
 | guard cell
 | epidermal cell
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 Palisade  mesophyll cells contain the  most  chloroplasts, followed by spongy mesophyll cells.  Guard   cells  contain a  small   number  of  chloroplasts  (far fewer than either mesophyll cell).
 Palisade mesophyll cells are found towards the top of the leaf and therefore have access to more sunlight hitting them than the cells of the spongy mesophyll; this is why they contain greater numbers of chloroplasts than spongy mesophyll cells.
 Guard cells have a smaller number of chloroplasts; they indirectly help control stomatal opening and closing.  
 Epidermal cells in the leaf do not contain chloroplasts. Cells in the upper epidermal layer need to allow light to penetrate the mesophyll layers below, and cells in the lower epidermal layer do not receive enough sunlight to photosynthesise.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram below shows a section through a leaf. 
 Which cell type would have the highest concentration of oxygen on a bright, sunny day?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 A  is a palisade mesophyll cell which is where most photosynthesis takes place (due to palisade mesophyll cells having the highest concentration of chloroplasts). The more photosynthesis occurring, the greater the amount of oxygen produced as a waste product. Some oxygen will be used up by each type of plant cell in the process of aerobic respiration, but the amounts are similar in each type of cell.
 B  is incorrect because it is part of the vascular bundle (xylem and phloem); these tissues do not contain chloroplasts.
 C  is incorrect because it is a spongy mesophyll cell which has fewer chloroplasts than the palisade cells (so photosynthesises less).
 D  is incorrect because it is an epidermal cell. Epidermal cells do not contain chloroplasts so do not photosynthesise.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram below shows part of the human digestive system. 
 In which structure is most of the water from food absorbed?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 Although  water  is also absorbed in the  colon  (large intestine),  most  absorption occurs in the  small intestine . This is because the absorption of  soluble  food molecules and salts (ions) from food occurs in the small intestine,  lowering the water potential  of the blood, drawing water in by osmosis.
 A  is incorrect because no absorption of water occurs in the oesophagus.
 B  is incorrect because no absorption of water occurs in the pancreas. Remember the pancreas is an accessory organ, and not part of the alimentary canal so no food passes through it.
 D  is incorrect because some absorption would occur in the large intestine, but the question asks where  most  absorption takes place.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which of the following descriptions are correctly matched to the different stages of food breakdown?
 |  
 | absorption
 | assimilation
 | egestion
 |
 | A
 | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream
 | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells
 | excretion of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus
 |
 | B
 | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream
 | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells
 | passing out of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus
 |
 | C
 | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells
 | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream
 | passing out of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus
 |
 | D
 | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells
 | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream
 | excretion of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 Absorption  is the movement of soluble food molecules and ions through the intestinal wall into the blood to be transported to the cells. Once it reaches the cells these food molecules and ions will cross the cell membrane during  assimilation  in order to become part of the cell. Any food that hasn't been digested or absorbed will move along the alimentary canal and leave the body through the anus during  egestion .
 A  is incorrect because egestion does not involve excretion. The waste products that leave the body during the process of excretion comes from metabolic reactions that occur  within cells . Waste products that leave the body during egestion was created  outside cells .
 C  is incorrect because the description of absorption and assimilation has been switched around.
 D  is incorrect because all three descriptions is incorrect for the reasons mentioned above.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A student collected some of the solution from the phloem in the stem of a plant. 
 Which of the following would be present in the liquid?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 Amino acids would be the only substance from the options given to move through the phloem (as well as sucrose).
 A  is incorrect because glucose is never transported through the phloem; however, sucrose (a disaccharide that contains one glucose molecule) is transported through the phloem.
 B  and  D  are incorrect because starch and cellulose are large biomolecules that are insoluble in water, therefore they cannot be moved around the plant.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which of the following processes is/are involved in the loss of water from the leaves of plants?
 • diffusion
 • osmosis
 • condensation
 • evaporation
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  (1 and 4) because:
 Water molecules evaporate from mesophyll cells, forming water vapour (a gas) which diffuses from an area of higher concentration in the air spaces inside the leaf to a lower concentration in the air outside the leaf (unless it’s very humid and the air is saturated with water!)
 A  is incorrect because diffusion is involved in the loss of water from a leaf, but condensation (change in the stage of gas to a liquid) is not.
 B  is incorrect because diffusion is only one of the processes involved in water loss from the leaves of a plant.
 C  Is incorrect because evaporation is involved in the loss of water from a leaf, but diffusion is also involved.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram below shows a vertical section through a human heart.
  Which row of the following table has the correct names for the structures labelled in the diagram?
 |  
 | X
 | Y
 | Z
 |
 | A
 | atrioventricular valve
 | semilunar valve
 | septum
 |
 | B
 | semilunar valve
 | atrioventricular valve
 | septum
 |
 | C
 | semilunar valve
 | semilunar valve
 | atrioventricular valve
 |
 | D
 | atrioventricular valve
 | atrioventricular valve
 | septum
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Semilunar  valves are found in the two arteries connected to the heart (the only arteries in the body to contain valves); they prevent the backflow of blood into the heart when it relaxes after contracting
 • The  atrioventricular  (AV) valves are located between the atria and the ventricles; they prevent the backflow of blood from the ventricles to the atria when the ventricles contract. The AV valve shown by  Y  in the question image is called the  bicuspid  or  mitral  valve
 • The  septum  separates the two sides of the heart; preventing the mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which row of the table below shows the correct chambers of the heart, from those with the thinnest walls to those with the thickest?
 |  
 | thinnest  →  thickest
 |
 | A
 | left ventricle
 | right ventricle
 | left atrium
 |
 | B
 | left atrium
 | left ventricle
 | right ventricle
 |
 | C
 | right ventricle
 | left atrium
 | left ventricle
 |
 | D
 | left atrium
 | right ventricle
 | left ventricle
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Ventricles  have much  thicker  muscle walls than atria because the  atria  are just passing the blood onto the ventricles whereas the ventricles have to generate enough force to push blood out of the heart
 • The  left ventricle  has a thicker muscle wall than the right ventricle as the right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs, which are right next to the heart, whereas the left ventricle is pumping blood to the entire body and so has to generate a higher pressure to pump it a greater distance

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following sequences show the correct path of oxygen as it enters the lungs?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.  (trachea → bronchus → bronchiole → alveolus) because:
 Air containing oxygen is inhaled through the mouth or nose, moving down the  trachea  which branches into the left bronchus and right bronchus (plural  bronchi ), the bronchi then divide into smaller branches (or airways) called  bronchioles  which eventually lead to a cluster of alveoli (singular alveolus).

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Students were discussing how to remember the difference between two groups of cells, ‘many, minute and motile’ or ‘few, fat and fixed’.
 What group of cells were they referring to?
options: C. Red and white blood cells
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A.  (Male and female gametes) because:
 • ‘Many, minute and motile’ refers to  sperm  cells. They are produced in very large numbers and are much smaller than the  ovum  (the egg) - they are much less energy intensive to produce which is why more of them can be made. They also have a  tail  to swim to the ovum
 • ‘Few, fat and fixed’ refers to an ovum (egg cell). Generally, only one egg is released each month in the  menstrual cycle . They are much larger than sperm cells and are unable to move independently, instead, they rely on the  ciliated  cells in the oviduct to waft them through to the  uterus
 A common misconception here is that these statements are referring to animal and plant cells, students often think of animal cells being smaller and motile and plant cells being large and fixed.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
To remain healthy, a person must be able to excrete a number of waste products produced as a result of metabolism.
 A list of excretory products is given below.
 Which of the following would be lost from both the kidneys  and  lungs?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  (water) because:
 Both the kidneys and the lungs are involved in the loss of water from the body. 
 B  is incorrect because carbon dioxide is not excreted by the kidneys. Carbon dioxide is mainly excreted by the lungs.
 C  is incorrect because glucose is not excreted (under normal conditions) by either the kidneys or the lungs. Excess glucose is transported to the liver to be converted into glycogen for storage.
 D  is incorrect because the lungs do not excrete urea, that is the role of the kidneys.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The image below shows a cell from the nervous system. The cell forms part of a reflex arc.
  An impulse moves along the neurone from Q to P. 
 What structures would be found at P and Q?
 |  
 | P
 | Q
 |
 | A
 | receptor
 | relay neurone
 |
 | B
 | relay neurone
 | receptor
 |
 | C
 | motor neurone 
 | relay neurone
 |
 | D
 | gland
 | relay neurone
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 The cell in the image above is a sensory neurone. If the impulse moves along the neurone from Q to P, then Q must be a receptor cell in a sense organ and P must be a relay neurone in the central nervous system (CNS).
 A  is incorrect because this answer would only be correct if the impulse travelled along the neurone from left to right (the question specifies it travels in the opposite direction).
 C  is incorrect because the relay neurone synapses with the motor neurone directly in a reflex arc; there is no neurone in between them.
 D  is incorrect because this would be correct if the cell shown was a motor neurone. Notice that the cell body is found strongly at one end of the motor neurone.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The image below shows the structures involved in a simple reflex arc. 
  Which of the following sequences correctly shows the order that an impulse passes through during a reflex action?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 Receptor cells (S) are found in sense organs. They pick up on the stimulus which generates an electrical impulse that travels along a sensory neurone (U) to the central nervous system (the brain or spinal cord) where it synapses with a relay neurone (V) which allows the impulse to pass rapidly from the sensory neurone to a motor neurone. Motor neurones synapse with effectors, in this case a muscle (T), stimulating it to contract and bring about a response.
 B  is incorrect because T is the effector (muscle) and U is the sensory neurone; the sensory neurone does not connect to the effector via a synapse.
 C  is incorrect because the receptor cells (S) are connected to sensory neurones (U) only.
 D  is incorrect because a reflex arc cannot begin with an effector!

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which of the following is a correct cause and effect?
 |  
 | deficiency
 | cause
 | effect
 |
 | A
 | iron
 | diet deficient in red meat, leafy green vegetables and liver
 | brittle bones (rickets)
 |
 | B
 | iron
 | lack of sunlight, fish and eggs
 | anaemia - tiredness and weakness due to not enough oxygen being delivered to tissues
 |
 | C
 | vitamin D
 | lack of sunlight
 | brittle bones (rickets)
 |
 | D
 | vitamin D
 | diet deficient in red meat, leafy green vegetables and liver
 | anaemia - tiredness and weakness due to not enough oxygen being delivered to tissues
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 A vitamin  D   deficiency  leads to  brittle   bones , as it is required for bones to be able to  absorb   calcium  ions in the  bloodstream . Calcium is the mineral which is needed to strengthen bones; the less calcium the weaker they are. Vitamin D can be  synthesized  in the body when  cholesterol  in skin cells is  converted  into  Vitamin D ; this reaction is driven by  UV  from sunlight.
 A  is incorrect because the effect is not linked to a deficiency in iron.
 B  is incorrect because the cause is incorrect.
 D  is incorrect because the deficiency does not match the cause or the effect.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram shows a human sperm cell. The sperm cell has many mitochondria in the mid section.
  How do the mitochondria help the sperm carry out its function?
options: A. They carry the genetic information from the male parent.
B. They release energy for movement.
C. They help the sperm enter the egg.
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.  (They release energy for movement) because:
 Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration which releases the energy needed to power the tail of the sperm so that it can make its journey to the ovum in the oviduct.
 A  is incorrect because the nucleus contains the genetic information from the male.
 C  is incorrect because the sperm cell has enzymes in the head (in the acrosome) to help it digest the outer layer of the egg so that it can release its nucleus into the egg.
 D  is incorrect because ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The statements below are about different hormones in the human body.
 • Produced by the pancreas.
 • Causes the voice to deepen at puberty.
 • Causes an egg to mature in the menstrual cycle.
 • Promotes the development of stronger muscles.
 Which of these statements are correct for testosterone?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.  (2 and 4) because:
 Testosterone is the male hormone that causes  secondary sexual characteristics  during  puberty . These include the development of stronger muscles and the voice to deepen.
 A  is incorrect because while it does cause the voice to deepen, testosterone is not produced by the pancreas (it’s produced in the testes).
 C  is incorrect because while it does promote the development of stronger muscles and is primarily thought of as a male hormone, women do produce small amounts of testosterone but it is not involved in the control of egg maturation in the ovaries.
 D  is incorrect because even though this is a correct statement, it is not the  only  correct statement (the question is asking you for all the statements).

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
HIV is an STI. The following statements are about changes that could occur in the body.
 • Reduced antibody production
 • Reduction in red blood cells
 • Reduction in white blood cells
 • Reduced volume of blood plasma
 Which of these statements would be correct for HIV?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.  (1 and 3) because:
 • HIV infects  lymphocytes  (a type of white blood cell) eventually leading to a reduction in their number. As the  lymphocytes  produce  antibodies  which enhance an immune response to infection, the reduction in antibody production eventually results in a reduced ability to fight infection (at this point a person has AIDS)
 • HIV is a sexually transmitted disease; that is the HIV virus is passed from one person to another via body fluids
 A  is incorrect because while HIV will reduce antibody production, it will not directly decrease the levels of red blood cells.
 B  is incorrect because neither of these statements would be correct for a direct effect of HIV.
 C  is incorrect because while HIV will reduce white blood cells it will not directly reduce the volume of plasma produced.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagrams show 3 different species of pollen grains as they appear under a microscope. The diagrams are all to the same scale.
  Which pollen grains are involved in insect pollination?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C.  (2 only) because:
 Pollen grains that are transferred by  insect pollinators  are larger and have a spiky surface to attach to insects.
 The pollen in picture 1 has a larger surface area with ‘wings’ and in picture 3 are small and light. These two features are more likely to be seen in wind pollinated seeds.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following diseases can be transmitted by contact with contaminated surfaces?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.  (Salmonella and athletes foot) because:
 Both these diseases are transmitted when a person comes into contact with a surface that contains these pathogens.
 A  is incorrect because malaria is transmitted by the bite of the female  Anopheles  mosquito.
 B  is incorrect because typhoid is transmitted by the consumption of water or food contaminated with the faeces of people infected with typhoid.
 C  is incorrect because influenza spreads by inhaling droplets in the air carrying the virus while dengue fever is spread by the bite of a specific species of mosquito ( Aedes aegypti ).

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which shows the correct size order of structures, starting with the smallest?
options: A. gene →  DNA strand →  chromosomes →  nucleus
B. DNA strand →  chromosomes →  gene → nucleus
C. chromosomes →  gene →  DNA strand →  nucleus
D. nucleus →  chromosomes →  DNA strand →  gene
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  (gene →  DNA strand →  chromosomes →  nucleus) because:
 A gene is the smallest structure of those listed; a gene is a section of a single DNA strand.  DNA coils itself around to form chromosomes; chromosomes are found in the nucleus which is the largest structure.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following statements is a correct definition of ‘adaptive features’?
options: A change in the environment that is an advantage to an organism.
B. An inherited feature that increases an organism's ability to survive and reproduce.
C. A change in phenotype that is caused by the environment.
D. An action that aids an organism's ability to survive.
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (An inherited feature that increases an organism's ability to survive and reproduce) because:
 Adaptive  features  are features that increase the chance of an organism surviving and reproducing in its environment.
 A  is incorrect because there may be changes in an environment that will give certain  phenotypes  an advantage, however, this is not an adaptive feature.
 C  is incorrect because a change in phenotype is not caused by the environment, but mutations in  genes  which can be inherited .
 D  is incorrect because this answer describes behavioural adaptations such as mating rituals.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
An island’s entire population of a species of butterfly are descended from just two parents. These were introduced from the mainland.
 Which of the following statements about this species of butterfly, compared with that of the mainland, is correct?
options: A. The population shows more genetic variety.
B. The population will adapt more slowly to environmental changes.
C. The population shows more phenotypic variation.
D. The population is less in danger of collapsing from disease.
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (the population will adapt more slowly to environmental changes) because:
 • The whole population has descended from just two parents, this will mean the population has very  little genetic diversity  (a small gene pool)
 • Reduced  variation  in a population means that they are less likely to survive any changes in the environment
 • Natural changes will occur due to  random mutations , but these must occur in gametes that form new individuals to possibly introduce variation into the population; such changes will be slow
 The other answers are incorrect because all of these statements refer to a population that has a large gene pool and a large genetic diversity.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram below shows part of the nitrogen cycle. 
  Which letter would represent denitrification?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 The process of denitrification removes nitrates from the soil, releasing it back into the atmosphere as nitrogen gas. This process occurs naturally by denitrifying bacteria in the soil, and it reduces soil fertility.
 A  is incorrect because this arrow shows decomposition of animals into ammonium compounds.
 B  is incorrect because this arrow refers to nitrification which is carried out by nitrifying bacteria.
 D  is incorrect because this arrow depicts nitrogen fixation by bacteria in root nodules and lightning.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The image below shows a pyramid of biomass for a food chain in a rainforest ecosystem.
  What would be an appropriate  pyramid of numbers  for this food chain?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 The first diagram shows a pyramid of biomass, although the trees are few in number, they are large organisms with a very high biomass. Remember that biomass is the biological mass of the organisms after water has been removed. The aphids have a small biomass; therefore a very large number are needed to support the next trophic level so in a pyramid of numbers this will be a much larger box than the producers. Remember that the producers are always at the bottom of a pyramid.  Pyramids of biomass are always pyramid shaped but pyramids of numbers may not be .
 A  &  D  are incorrect because there will only be a few trees supporting many of the next level in the chain. In a pyramid of numbers, when the producers are very large organisms, they will be represented by a smaller box.
 B  is incorrect because if there were only a very small number of aphids there would not be enough to support the next level in the chain.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following diagrams show a pyramid of biomass for a forest?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 Pyramids of biomass are always pyramid shaped, regardless of the habitat that they represent (unlike pyramids of number).
 Pyramids  A ,  B  and  D  are not pyramid shaped so, therefore, do not show a pyramid of biomass.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The graph shows the relationship between the number of lichens and the levels of sulfur dioxide pollution.
  Which of these statements best describe the graph?
options: A. Sulfur dioxide levels do not affect lichen growth.
B. As sulfur dioxide levels increase, the number of lichen decreases.
C. Lichens cannot survive if there is sulfur dioxide present.
D. As sulfur dioxide levels increase, so does the number of lichen.
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (as sulfur dioxide levels increase, the number of lichen decreases) because:
 The graph shows that as the levels of sulfur dioxide increase, the number of lichen species decreases.
 A  is incorrect because there  is  a correlation between sulfur dioxide levels and the number of lichens.
 C  is incorrect because some lichens are surviving even at relatively high levels of sulfur dioxide.
 D  is incorrect because sulfur dioxide levels increase and the levels of lichens do not increase.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A large quantity of non-selective herbicide is spread over a field. However, some of the herbicide washes into a nearby stream.
 What is the effect of the herbicide on the weeds in the field and on the plants in the stream?
 |  
 | weeds in field
 | plants in stream
 |
 | A
 | more growth
 | less growth
 |
 | B
 | less growth
 | more growth
 |
 | C
 | less growth
 | less growth
 |
 | D
 | more growth
 | more growth
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 A non-selective herbicide will likely kill  all  plants; both aquatic plants in the stream and weeds in the field. Even selective herbicides that only target unwanted plants like weeds can harm all plants when their concentration is high enough.
 Herbicides kill plants so any answer that refers to more growth will not be correct.
 Be careful – don’t confuse this with eutrophication, herbicides will kill plants not increase growth; that is the role of fertilisers.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Penicillin is produced in a fermenter by growing the fungus  Penicillium . 
 The graph below shows how the mass of living  Penicillium  fungus, and the concentration of penicillin, changed over time.
  Which day would be the best to harvest the penicillin at?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (5 days) because:
 At 5 days this would give you the highest  yield  of penicillin. Penicillin is produced in a  batch culture  so you would want to harvest with the highest yield possible. This is also the point at which the mass of living organisms has reduced.

D. The leaves have parallel veins.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  (the veins in the leaf are reticulated) because:
 Dicotyledonous plants have leaves that are usually large with a network of branching veins.
 B  and  D  are incorrect because both statements would apply to a monocotyledonous plant; flowers from monocots contain petals in multiples of 3 and their leaves have parallel veins.
 C  is incorrect because the method of pollination is not a distinguishing feature between monocots or dicots.

 A plant cell and an animal cell are observed under a light microscope.
 Which of the above structures would always be visible in a plant cell?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (1 & 3 only) because:
 • The  nucleus  is usually the  largest  subcellular structure and should easily be visible in a plant cell observed with a light microscope 
 • Ribosomes  are extremely small and cannot be seen with a light microscope - you need an electron microscope with higher magnification and resolution to see them
 • Plant cells contain  permanent   vacuoles  (which store solutions of salt and sugar)
 • Not every plant cell will have a  chloroplast  - they are largely found in the palisade and spongy mesophyll cells, as well as guard cells (all in the leaf)
 The other answers are incorrect because they do not correctly show the structures that would be visible with a light microscope. 
 Remember not every cell in a plant will photosynthesise - think of the cells of the roots underground, they don’t receive any light so couldn’t photosynthesise even if they did contain chloroplasts (which they don’t!).

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A student decided to investigate the effect of pH on the activity of the enzyme lipase.
 Five different test tubes are set up. Each test tube contains a mixture of the enzyme lipase and its substrate, a lipid.
 Which condition should not be kept the same in each of the five test tubes?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.  (pH) because:
 If the condition being investigated is pH, then this is the  independent   variable  and should be different in each test tube to get a good range of results.
 A  is incorrect because the temperature is one factor that can affect enzyme activity and should not be changed if pH is being altered.
 B  is incorrect because the concentration of the enzyme is another factor that needs to be kept the same (not changed) to make the experiment fair as it can also affect enzyme activity.
 C  is incorrect because the volume of the lipid solution is one of the things that needs to be kept the same to make the experiment valid; the more lipid (substrate) there is, the longer it will take for the reaction to complete.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Which of the following options is the best explanation for the role of chlorophyll in photosynthesis?
 Chlorophyll...
options: A. transfers light energy from the Sun because it has magnesium ions
B. transfers chemical potential energy from sunlight into organic molecules which can be used to synthesise carbohydrates such as glucose
C. transfers light energy from the Sun into chemical energy in inorganic molecules which can be used for growth
D. transfers light energy into chemical potential energy in glucose molecules which are used in the synthesis of other carbohydrates
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  (transfers light energy into chemical potential energy in glucose molecules which are used in the synthesis of other carbohydrates) because:
 • chlorophyll absorbs light energy (from the Sun or artificial light sources)
 • light energy is used to drive a reaction between water and carbon dioxide, producing glucose (a carbohydrate)
 • glucose can be converted into other carbohydrates, such as sucrose, starch and cellulose
 A  is incorrect because chlorophyll molecules do contain magnesium ions, but this doesn’t outline its role in photosynthesis.
 B  is incorrect because chlorophyll absorbs light energy, not chemical potential energy, to drive the synthesis of organic molecules such as glucose (light energy is transferred to chemical potential energy stored in the bonds of glucose molecules).
 C  is incorrect because chlorophyll absorbs energy from sunlight to drive reactions between inorganic molecules (carbon dioxide and water) to produce glucose (an organic

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram below shows how the rate of photosynthesis is affected by different conditions.
  What of the following correctly identifies the limiting factor for photosynthesis at the three points on the graph?
 |  
 | 1
 | 2
 | 3
 |
 | A
 | light intensity
 | light intensity
 | carbon dioxide concentration
 |
 | B
 | temperature
 | temperature
 | light intensity
 |
 | C
 | light intensity
 | temperature
 | carbon dioxide concentration
 |
 | D
 | light intensity
 | carbon dioxide concentration
 | temperature

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • At 1, the  rate  of photosynthesis has yet to level off (neither temperature nor concentration of carbon dioxide are limiting in this experiment) so light intensity is still the limiting factor
 • At 2, the  rate  of photosynthesis is  no longer increasing  even though the  light intensity is still increasing , so some other factor is limiting (in the table, we can see the temperature for experiment 2 is 20℃, so the temperature is the limiting factor)
 • At 3, the  rate  of photosynthesis is  no longer increasing  even though the light intensity is still increasing, so  some other factor is limiting  (in the table, we can see the carbon dioxide concentration is lower than other experiments, so carbon dioxide concentration is the limiting factor)
 A  is incorrect because  temperature  is the limiting factor for experiment 2, not light intensity.
 B  is incorrect because  light intensity  is the limiting factor in experiment 1, not temperature.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of the following is a correct explanation of the effect of root hairs on absorption?
options: A. Provide a large surface area, maximising the rate of absorption of water and ions by osmosis.
B. Provide a large surface area, maximising the rate of absorption of water by osmosis and ions by active transport.
C. Increase the surface area, maximising the uptake of water by osmosis and ions by diffusion.
D. Provide a surface area, increasing the rate of absorption of water and ions by active transport.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 Root hairs are extensions of the cytoplasm of root cells, increasing the surface area to maximise the absorption of water by osmosis and ions by active transport.
 A  is incorrect because ions are transported into the roots by active transport. Osmosis only applies to the movement of water.
 C  Is incorrect because ions are transported into the roots by active transport, not diffusion.
 D  Is incorrect because there is no indication that surface area is increased in this explanation, and osmosis should be mentioned in relation to the movement of water.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram below shows part of the human digestive system. 
 In which structure is most of the water from food absorbed?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 Although  water  is also absorbed in the  colon  (large intestine),  most  absorption occurs in the  small intestine . This is because the absorption of  soluble  food molecules and salts (ions) from food occurs in the small intestine,  lowering the water potential  of the blood, drawing water in by osmosis.
 A  is incorrect because no absorption of water occurs in the oesophagus.
 B  is incorrect because no absorption of water occurs in the pancreas. Remember the pancreas is an accessory organ, and not part of the alimentary canal so no food passes through it.
 D  is incorrect because some absorption would occur in the large intestine, but the question asks where  most  absorption takes place.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Which of the following descriptions are correctly matched to the different stages of food breakdown?
 |  
 | absorption
 | assimilation
 | egestion
 |
 | A
 | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream
 | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells
 | excretion of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus
 |
 | B
 | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream
 | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells
 | passing out of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus
 |
 | C
 | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells
 | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream
 | passing out of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus
 |
 | D
 | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells
 | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream
 | excretion of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus
 |
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 Absorption  is the movement of soluble food molecules and ions through the intestinal wall into the blood to be transported to the cells. Once it reaches the cells these food molecules and ions will cross the cell membrane during  assimilation  in order to become part of the cell. Any food that hasn't been digested or absorbed will move along the alimentary canal and leave the body through the anus during  egestion .
 A  is incorrect because egestion does not involve excretion. The waste products that leave the body during the process of excretion comes from metabolic reactions that occur  within cells . Waste products that leave the body during egestion was created  outside cells .
 C  is incorrect because the description of absorption and assimilation has been switched around.
 D  is incorrect because all three descriptions is incorrect for the reasons mentioned above.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of the following depicts the correct order of stages in the formation of a blood clot?
options: A. soluble fibrin → insoluble fibrinogen → blood clot
B. soluble fibrinogen → insoluble fibrin → blood clot
C. insoluble fibrin → soluble fibrinogen → blood clot
D. insoluble fibrinogen → soluble fibrin→ blood clot
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.  (soluble fibrinogen → insoluble fibrin → blood clot) because:
 • When a blood vessel is broken/ damaged , a series of reactions occur within the blood  plasma
 • This results in an enzyme becoming activated which converts  soluble   fibrinogen  (present in the blood plasma) into  insoluble   fibrin
 • Strands of insoluble fibrin trap red blood in a  mesh -like structure which forms a  clot  over the damaged area

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Which of the following processes is/are involved in the loss of water from the leaves of plants?
 • diffusion
 • osmosis
 • condensation
 • evaporation
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  (1 and 4) because:
 Water molecules evaporate from mesophyll cells, forming water vapour (a gas) which diffuses from an area of higher concentration in the air spaces inside the leaf to a lower concentration in the air outside the leaf (unless it’s very humid and the air is saturated with water!)
 A  is incorrect because diffusion is involved in the loss of water from a leaf, but condensation (change in the stage of gas to a liquid) is not.
 B  is incorrect because diffusion is only one of the processes involved in water loss from the leaves of a plant.
 C  Is incorrect because evaporation is involved in the loss of water from a leaf, but diffusion is also involved.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
When a tissue is transplanted from a female donor to a male recipient, it may be rejected.
 What is the main cause of this rejection?
options: A. The presence of an X chromosome
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.  (Antibody production) because:
 • Antibodies are produced in response to any foreign cell in the body, regardless of whether that cell is a pathogenic microorganism or a cell from another member of the same or different species
 • Don’t be distracted by the fact that the donor tissue is from a female and the recipient is a man – this has nothing to do with causing an immune response
 A  is incorrect because the presence of an X chromosome in the grafted cells is not what provokes an immune response; it is the antigens on the surface of the cells which do that.
 B  is incorrect because platelets are involved in blood clotting, not an immune response.
 C  is incorrect because antibiotics are given to a patient with a bacterial infection, they don’t usually affect other human cells, and are not made by the body so do not form part of the immune response.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The human body has a number of barriers to prevent infection by pathogens some of which are listed below.
 • Skin
 • Mucus
 • Hairs in the nose
 • Antibodies
 • Stomach acid
 Which of these are examples of mechanical barriers?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A.  (1 and 3) because:
 The skin and hairs in the nose forms a physical barrier that makes it more difficult for pathogens to enter the body.
 B  and  C  are incorrect because mucus (2) is an example of a chemical barrier while antibodies (4) are produced by lymphocytes in response to foreign antigens entering the body, they do not act as a barrier.
 D  is incorrect because stomach acid (5) is another example of a chemical barrier, not a mechanical one.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of the following sequences show the correct path of oxygen as it enters the lungs?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.  (trachea → bronchus → bronchiole → alveolus) because:
 Air containing oxygen is inhaled through the mouth or nose, moving down the  trachea  which branches into the left bronchus and right bronchus (plural  bronchi ), the bronchi then divide into smaller branches (or airways) called  bronchioles  which eventually lead to a cluster of alveoli (singular alveolus).

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Students were discussing how to remember the difference between two groups of cells, ‘many, minute and motile’ or ‘few, fat and fixed’.
 What group of cells were they referring to?
options: C. Red and white blood cells
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A.  (Male and female gametes) because:
 • ‘Many, minute and motile’ refers to  sperm  cells. They are produced in very large numbers and are much smaller than the  ovum  (the egg) - they are much less energy intensive to produce which is why more of them can be made. They also have a  tail  to swim to the ovum
 • ‘Few, fat and fixed’ refers to an ovum (egg cell). Generally, only one egg is released each month in the  menstrual cycle . They are much larger than sperm cells and are unable to move independently, instead, they rely on the  ciliated  cells in the oviduct to waft them through to the  uterus
 A common misconception here is that these statements are referring to animal and plant cells, students often think of animal cells being smaller and motile and plant cells being large and fixed.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Which of the following processes would release the most energy in a cell from one molecule of glucose?
 • Aerobic respiration in yeast
 • Aerobic respiration in animals
 • Aerobic respiration in plants
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  (all of the above) because:
 The process of aerobic respiration is essentially the same in all eukaryotic cells, so the theoretical energy released will be the same when one molecule of glucose is broken down in any of the above cells.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of the following organs are responsible for removing excretory products from the blood?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (kidneys and lungs) because:
 The kidneys remove urea, excess salts and water from the blood. The lungs remove carbon dioxide from the blood due to the concentration gradient set up between the air in the lungs and the carbon dioxide in the blood. This is maintained by breathing. 
 A  is incorrect because the bladder is not responsible for removing excretory products from the  blood , it removes it from the body.
 C  is incorrect because the liver is responsible for producing many of the excretory products, but it is not directly responsible for the excretion of these products.
 D  is incorrect because neither the bladder nor liver will remove excretory products from the blood for excretion as mentioned above.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The image below shows the structures involved in a simple reflex arc. 
  Which of the following sequences correctly shows the order that an impulse passes through during a reflex action?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 Receptor cells (S) are found in sense organs. They pick up on the stimulus which generates an electrical impulse that travels along a sensory neurone (U) to the central nervous system (the brain or spinal cord) where it synapses with a relay neurone (V) which allows the impulse to pass rapidly from the sensory neurone to a motor neurone. Motor neurones synapse with effectors, in this case a muscle (T), stimulating it to contract and bring about a response.
 B  is incorrect because T is the effector (muscle) and U is the sensory neurone; the sensory neurone does not connect to the effector via a synapse.
 C  is incorrect because the receptor cells (S) are connected to sensory neurones (U) only.
 D  is incorrect because a reflex arc cannot begin with an effector!

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The image below shows a cell from the nervous system. The cell forms part of a reflex arc.
  An impulse moves along the neurone from Q to P. 
 What structures would be found at P and Q?
 |  
 | P
 | Q
 |
 | A
 | receptor
 | relay neurone
 |
 | B
 | relay neurone
 | receptor
 |
 | C
 | motor neurone 
 | relay neurone
 |
 | D
 | gland
 | relay neurone
 |
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 The cell in the image above is a sensory neurone. If the impulse moves along the neurone from Q to P, then Q must be a receptor cell in a sense organ and P must be a relay neurone in the central nervous system (CNS).
 A  is incorrect because this answer would only be correct if the impulse travelled along the neurone from left to right (the question specifies it travels in the opposite direction).
 C  is incorrect because the relay neurone synapses with the motor neurone directly in a reflex arc; there is no neurone in between them.
 D  is incorrect because this would be correct if the cell shown was a motor neurone. Notice that the cell body is found strongly at one end of the motor neurone.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The data in the graph shows the effect of an antibiotic on the population of bacteria in the blood.
  What can be concluded from the data in the graph?
options: Antibiotics take 10 days to kill all bacteria.
B. Antibiotics cause a reduction in division of bacteria.
C. Antibiotics are effective against viral and bacterial infections.
D. Before the start of the antibiotic treatment the bacterial population was increasing.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 The bacterial population is increasing before the patient starts to take antibiotics. This can be seen in the graph.
 A  is incorrect because from the graph the bacteria population has decreased to 0 by 6.5 days after starting the treatment with antibiotics.
 B  is incorrect because you can’t see how the antibiotic works on the bacteria from the graph.
 C  is incorrect because antibiotics are not effective against viruses - the graph only shows the effect on bacterial populations.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The statements below are about different hormones in the human body.
 • Produced by the pancreas.
 • Causes the voice to deepen at puberty.
 • Causes an egg to mature in the menstrual cycle.
 • Promotes the development of stronger muscles.
 Which of these statements are correct for testosterone?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.  (2 and 4) because:
 Testosterone is the male hormone that causes  secondary sexual characteristics  during  puberty . These include the development of stronger muscles and the voice to deepen.
 A  is incorrect because while it does cause the voice to deepen, testosterone is not produced by the pancreas (it’s produced in the testes).
 C  is incorrect because while it does promote the development of stronger muscles and is primarily thought of as a male hormone, women do produce small amounts of testosterone but it is not involved in the control of egg maturation in the ovaries.
 D  is incorrect because even though this is a correct statement, it is not the  only  correct statement (the question is asking you for all the statements).

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagrams show 3 different species of pollen grains as they appear under a microscope. The diagrams are all to the same scale.
  Which pollen grains are involved in insect pollination?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C.  (2 only) because:
 Pollen grains that are transferred by  insect pollinators  are larger and have a spiky surface to attach to insects.
 The pollen in picture 1 has a larger surface area with ‘wings’ and in picture 3 are small and light. These two features are more likely to be seen in wind pollinated seeds.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
ABO blood groups are an inherited characteristic.
 What would the blood group of the offspring be when two parents have the genotypes I A I A  and I A I O ?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  (group A) because:
 • Blood group inheritance is an example of  codominance
 • There are three possible alleles that can be inherited; but an individual can only have a maximum of two alleles in their genotype
 • Alleles I A  and I B   are dominant over I O , so because one parent is homozygous for blood group A, all of the offspring will inherit the  I A  allele, meaning all the offspring will be in group A (as the partner has a heterozygous genotype with the recessive I O  allele

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The graph below shows the number of deaths from MRSA per 100 000 people in a population of over-65’s from 2005 to 2012.
  Which of the following statements are possible explanations for the trend shown in the graph?
options: A. More effective antibiotics are being used to treat infected people.
B. A decrease in the size of the population of over-65 year olds.
C. Over-65 year olds are immune to MRSA infection.
D. Antibiotics do not affect viruses.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 It is most likely that the decrease in number of deaths from MRSA over time is a result of new or different antibiotics being used that are effective at treating MRSA infections; as a result, the death rate will fall.
 B  is incorrect because a decrease in the population would not affect the death rate.
 C  is incorrect because over-65’s are still dying from MRSA infection so this cannot be true or likely.
 D  is incorrect because, while this is a true statement, it has nothing to do with the data shown.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram shows the menstrual cycle. This is a 28 day cycle.
  Which time range in the cycle is the woman most likely to get pregnant?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C.  (Days 13 - 16) because:
 • Ovulation  happens after the LH surge which occurs around day 14 (if day 1 is the first day of a period in a new cycle) 
 • Sperm  will survive in a woman's body for 2 -3 days so once the egg is released there may be sperm in the fallopian tube to fertilise the egg
  A  is incorrect because around this time the egg has not been released from the ovary.
 B  is incorrect because there is no egg released (it will be maturing at this point) and any sperm present at this time are unlikely to survive until the egg is released roughly 4 days later.
 D  is incorrect because the egg will have died by day 20 so there will be no egg for the sperm to fertilise.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Two individuals are crossed. One is homozygous dominant (TT), the other heterozygous.
 What will the genotypes of the offspring be?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (50% TT, 50% Tt) because:
 • The parents have the genotypes TT (homozygous) and Tt (heterozygous)
 • The gametes produced by the homozygous dominant individual will all contain the allele ‘T’
 • The possible gametes for the heterozygous parent will contain either ‘T’ or ‘t’

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of the following statements is a correct definition of ‘adaptive features’?
options: A change in the environment that is an advantage to an organism.
B. An inherited feature that increases an organism's ability to survive and reproduce.
C. A change in phenotype that is caused by the environment.
D. An action that aids an organism's ability to survive.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (An inherited feature that increases an organism's ability to survive and reproduce) because:
 Adaptive  features  are features that increase the chance of an organism surviving and reproducing in its environment.
 A  is incorrect because there may be changes in an environment that will give certain  phenotypes  an advantage, however, this is not an adaptive feature.
 C  is incorrect because a change in phenotype is not caused by the environment, but mutations in  genes  which can be inherited .
 D  is incorrect because this answer describes behavioural adaptations such as mating rituals.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of these is  not  a feature of a hydrophyte?
options: B. Large air spaces in the tissues.
C. Leaves rolled up and covered with hairs.
D. Leaves with stomata on the upper surface.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (leaves rolled up and covered with hairs) because:
 • Hydrophytes  are plants that live in  wet  or  aquatic  environments
 • Leaves rolled up and covered with hairs is an  adaptation  of xerophytes (plants that live in very dry environments such as sand dunes)
 The other answers are incorrect because all the other features listed are features of hydrophytes:
 • They have a reduced root and xylem system as they are living in an aquatic environment so have a plentiful supply of water
 • They have large air spaces in the tissues for gas exchange
 • They have stomata on their upper surface as they are often floating in water, so stomata on the upper surface of the leaf are easier for gas exchange

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The inheritance of Huntington's disease is determined by a single gene. This gene has a dominant allele and a recessive allele. The allele for Huntington’s is dominant to the allele for non-sufferers of the condition.
 The diagram shows the inheritance of Huntington’s in a family.
  What is the probability that the next child from the same parents will have Huntington’s?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (50%) because:
 • The parent without Huntington’s (non-Huntington’s) must be homozygous recessive (hh)
 • The parent with Huntington’s must be heterozygous (Hh) as they have one child without the disease and the sufferer must have passed on a recessive allele
 The Punnett square for this will be:
 |  
 | H
 | h
 |
 | h
 | Hh
 | hh
 |
 | h
 | Hh
 | hh
 |
 This shows a 50% chance of any child from this cross being a sufferer of the disease.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The image below shows a pyramid of biomass for a food chain in a rainforest ecosystem.
  What would be an appropriate  pyramid of numbers  for this food chain?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 The first diagram shows a pyramid of biomass, although the trees are few in number, they are large organisms with a very high biomass. Remember that biomass is the biological mass of the organisms after water has been removed. The aphids have a small biomass; therefore a very large number are needed to support the next trophic level so in a pyramid of numbers this will be a much larger box than the producers. Remember that the producers are always at the bottom of a pyramid.  Pyramids of biomass are always pyramid shaped but pyramids of numbers may not be .
 A  &  D  are incorrect because there will only be a few trees supporting many of the next level in the chain. In a pyramid of numbers, when the producers are very large organisms, they will be represented by a smaller box.
 B  is incorrect because if there were only a very small number of aphids there would not be enough to support the next level in the chain.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which letter shows the path of the energy from the sun?
options: A. chemical energy in sugars → stored in plants → trapped in chlorophyll
B. trapped in chlorophyll → chemical energy in sugars → stored in plants
C. stored in plants → chemical energy in sugars →  trapped in chlorophyll
D. stored in plants → trapped in chlorophyll →  chemical energy in sugars
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Energy from the sun is trapped by  chlorophyll , the pigment found in chloroplasts. Light energy is then used to drive the synthesis of carbohydrates such as glucose (a  sugar ); in this sense an energy transfer occurs from light to chemical potential energy within the bonds of carbohydrate molecules
 • The sugars produced in photosynthesis are then  stored  as more complex molecules such as starch in the plant

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The following statements refer to conservation techniques.
 • Artificial insemination will decrease the need for male and female organisms to be present in the same area
 • The offspring produced during artificial insemination will have less genetic variation than their parents
 • In vitro fertilisation will produce large numbers of offspring without the need for gametes to fuse
 • These techniques will increase the resilience of a species and decrease their risk of extinction
 Which of these statements are  false ?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (2 and 3 only) because:
 Artificial insemination is a technique whereby the genetic material carried by the gametes combine and is therefore used to maintain or increase the genetic variation within a species, which makes statement 2 false. In vitro fertilisation involves the fusion of gametes outside the body (usually in a petri dish), so statement 3 is not correct.
 A ,  C  and  D  are all incorrect because statements 1 and 4 are  true  regarding conservation techniques.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: What is the role of ligase enzymes in genetic engineering?
options: A. To insert plasmids into bacteria.
B. To join human DNA with plasmid DNA.
D. To cut open plasmid DNA.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (to join human DNA with plasmid DNA) because:
 • The  enzyme  that can join complementary  sticky ends  created by the activity of restriction enzymes on plasmid and human DNA is called  ligase
 • ‘Sticky ends’ can complement base-pair with each other, but ligase joins the sugar-phosphate backbones of adjacent DNA molecules together
 A  is incorrect because ligase enzyme is not used when plasmids are taken up by the bacteria.
 C  is incorrect because the human gene is isolated using  restriction enzymes  that cut the DNA at specific base sequences.
 D  is incorrect because  restriction enzymes  are used to cut the plasmid open to create  sticky ends.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Penicillin is produced in a fermenter by growing the fungus  Penicillium . 
 The graph below shows how the mass of living  Penicillium  fungus, and the concentration of penicillin, changed over time.
  Which day would be the best to harvest the penicillin at?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (5 days) because:
 At 5 days this would give you the highest  yield  of penicillin. Penicillin is produced in a  batch culture  so you would want to harvest with the highest yield possible. This is also the point at which the mass of living organisms has reduced.

set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
During the fermentation of yeast, enzymes that break down sugar release carbon dioxide gas. The volume of carbon dioxide released can be used to measure how fast these enzymes are working. 
 A student investigates if fermentation works faster at two different temperatures: 25°C or 30°C. They measured the volume of carbon dioxide released in 15 minutes. Fig. 1 shows the apparatus she uses.
  Fig. 1
 The student used a gas syringe, as shown in Fig. 1 to collect and measure the volume of carbon dioxide released. They could have measured the volume of carbon dioxide by collecting the gas over water in a measuring cylinder. 
 Use the information provided in Fig. 1 to suggest why it is better to use a gas syringe.
set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
It is better to use a gas syringe because...
 • (It allows for) more accurate/precise measurement (of the volume/amount of gas);  [1 mark]
 Allow  'gas could dissolve in water / less gas can escape'   Ignore  'gives exact measurement of gas release'
 [Total: 1 mark]
 The volume of carbon dioxide released would be small so the graduations on a measuring cylinder would be more appropriate for collecting large volumes of gas. A gas syringe would allow for more precise measurements due to the smaller intervals between markings.

set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
Fig. 1  shows the path of light entering the front part of the eye of a person with normal vision, whilst looking at a close object.
  Fig. 1
 As people get older (typically 40+), their lenses lose flexibility and can't spring back into a round shape when looking at close objects.
 Explain what effect a less flexible lens would have on the path of light.
set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
The effect a less flexible lens would have on the path of light is as follows...
 Any  three  from the following:
 • The light is refracted by a smaller amount / narrower angle;  [1 mark]
 • As the lens is thin / stretched;  [1 mark]
 • Images / light rays are brought into focus behind the retina;  [1 mark]
 • So (close objects) appear blurred/fuzzy;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 3 marks]
 To help you answer this question, think of the lens and path of light as being similar to when looking at a distant object but as the person is looking at a near object, the amount of light refraction is not sufficient. This condition is known as presbyopia and can be corrected by wearing reading glasses.

set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
The nephron consists of several different structures such as the Bowman's capsule and glomerulus.
 Describe and explain how the structure of the glomerulus and Bowman's capsule help to remove urea from the bloodstream.
set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
The structure of the Bowman's capsule and glomerulus and how it facilitates the removal of urea from the bloodstream can be explained as follows...
 Any  four  of the following:
 • The glomerulus consists of a knot/network of capillaries;  [1 mark]
 • The glomerulus sits inside the cup-shaped Bowman's capsule;  [1 mark]
 • The capillaries (of the glomerulus) are narrow which increase the pressure of the blood (moving through them);  [1 mark]
 • The Bowman's capsule and glomerulus let small molecules (such as urea) pass into the tubules (of the nephron);  [1 mark]
 • During the process of  ultra filtration;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 4 marks]
 It is very important to be able to relate the structure of the parts of the nephron to its function so make sure you familiarise yourself with this.

set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
Fig. 1 shows a dwarf sunflower and a tall sunflower,  Helianthus annuus .
 The height of the dwarf sunflower is 0.45 m and the height of the tall sunflower is 4.5 m.
  Fig. 1
 Dwarf plants like the one in Fig. 1 have mutant alleles.
 Define the term  allele .
set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
The term allele can be defined as...
 • A version of a  gene ;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 1 mark]
 This question covers core knowledge but is taken from a paper 4 (extended content) paper.

 • Not all nutrients in the organisms are eaten / digested / a

set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
CGRP is a protein found in the human brain. High levels of CGRP has been linked to the occurrence of migraines in sufferers. A possible treatment under investigation involves injecting mice with human CGRP.
 Explain how the immune system of mice would respond to the CGRP injection.
set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
The immune system of mice would respond in the following ways to the CGRP injection...
 • Antigens on CGRP proteins would be recognised as foreign (by mice lymphocytes);  [1 mark]
 • Lymphocytes would produce antibodies against CGRP;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 2 marks]
 Remember that the immune response would occur in response to the presence of any foreign antigen, even if that antigen does not form part of a pathogen. Human CGRP proteins would trigger a similar immune response in mice than an infection with a pathogen would.

set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
A person leaves a room and runs very fast for 200m. When the person stops running, his breathing rate and his heart rate remain high for several minutes.
 Explain why the person’s breathing rate and heart rate remain high.
set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
The person's breathing rate and heart rate remain high because:
 Any  four  from the following:
 • Takes time for...;  [1 mark]
 • ...oxygen debt (to be repaid);  [1 mark]
 • More oxygen needed;  [1 mark]
 • Lactic acid / lactate;  [1 mark]
 • Builds up in muscles / needs to be cleared away;  [1 mark]
 • Lactic acid is broken down / respired; [1 mark]
 [Total: 4 marks]
 When lactic acid is broken down in the liver it reacts with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water, which can both be easily removed from the body.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which name can be given to a group of organisms that have similar morphological features and can reproduce successfully to produce fertile offspring?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  (species) because:
 Members of the same species usually look similar or share similar features, and crucially, can reproduce to produce offspring that can in turn go on to produce fertile offspring themselves. 
 A  is incorrect because a kingdom is an extremely large group containing different phyla. For example, animals make up one kingdom, plants make up another. 
 B  is incorrect because a genus is a group containing several different species with similar characteristics and evolutionary history. 
 C  is incorrect because a family is a taxonomic classification between order and genus; a family contains many different genera.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Some of the processes carried out by living organisms are illustrated in the diagram below.
