set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (respiration, respiration, nutrition) because:
 Process  W  shows oxygen being absorbed by the green plant (oxygen is only needed for aerobic respiration),  X  shows the rabbit respiring (carbon dioxide is being released to the atmosphere) and  Y  shows the plant being consumed by the rabbit (which demonstrates nutrition).
 Watch out - you might think process  W  is photosynthesis as it's being carried out by a green plant, but oxygen is being consumed, not carbon dioxide. Remember that plants respire too.

Use the key to identify the group to which fish belong.

 Fur present...

 mammals

 Smooth skin...

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is group  C  because:
 Fish do not have fur, lay eggs without shells, reproduce in water, and have scales.
 Group A would be birds, as birds lay eggs with hard shells.
 Group B would be reptiles, as reptiles lay their eggs on land.
 Group D would be amphibians, as they have smooth skin.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following terms would be correct to describe a leaf, a root and stem?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (organ) because:
 All three structures in the question are organs. An organ is a group of two or more tissues working together to carry out a particular function.
 A  is incorrect because each of the leaves, stems and roots are made up of thousands of different cells all working together. 
 B  is incorrect because the  leaf  is made from  palisade  &  spongy  mesophyll tissue,  epidermal  tissue and  vascular  tissue functioning together to allow a plant to photosynthesise. The  roots  and  stem  are made from  vascular  (transport)  tissue  which work together to transport substances around the plant.
 D  is incorrect because together plants have two organ systems. The  shoot organ system  in a plant is made from leaves, stems, buds, fruits and flowers. The  root organ system  of most plants are all the parts that are underground.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which row of the table below correctly describes a spongy mesophyll cell?

 | contains chloroplasts for photosynthesis
 | loses water by transpiration
 | ideal surface area for gas exchange

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 Spongy mesophyll cells contain chloroplasts for photosynthesis and have a relatively large surface area for gas exchange with the air spaces in the leaf. They also lose water by transpiration; water evaporates from the surfaces of the spongy cells, diffusing into the air spaces and out of the stomata.
 The other answers are incorrect because they do not correctly describe a spongy mesophyll cell.
 The diagram below shows the structure of the leaf and the position of the spongy mesophyll cells within the leaf.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Eukaryotic cells contain mitochondria (a mitochondrion is shown below).
  Which diagram below correctly shows the position of mitochondria in a plant cell?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 Mitochondria are usually slightly smaller than chloroplasts and are found within the cytoplasm. Mitochondria have a highly folded internal membrane, whereas chloroplasts look like they contain stacks of pancakes (sometimes!).
 B  is incorrect because mitochondria are not found within the cell wall; in fact, no organelles are found within the cell wall. 
 C  is incorrect because mitochondria are not found within the vacuole.
 D  is incorrect because this cell is an animal cell. You can tell this because of the absence of a cell wall and vacuole.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: What causes the diffusion of carbon dioxide out of a living cell?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (Random movement of molecules) because:
 Molecules like carbon dioxide must be able to move to be able to diffuse. Individual molecules move about randomly, but overall net movement of a gas occurs from a region of high concentration to a region of low concentration.
 A  is incorrect because active transport requires protein molecules embedded within a membrane using energy released via respiration to move molecules deliberately into the cell (usually against a concentration gradient).
 C  is incorrect because respiration as a chemical process produces the waste gas carbon dioxide, but the reaction isn’t responsible for the movement of the gas.
 D  is incorrect because photosynthesis is a chemical process that requires carbon dioxide, and although a plant cell photosynthesising lowers the concentration of carbon dioxide inside the cell, it doesn’t cause the movement of carbon dioxide out of the cell.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the structures below is best adapted for diffusion?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  (ileum) because:
 The ileum is part of the small intestine where most food absorption occurs. The wall of the ileum is heavily folded; these finger-like folds are called villi (singular villus) which are externally covered by highly folded cells called microvilli. 
 B  and  C  are incorrect because the bronchioles and atria are not adapted for diffusion at all due to their thick walls.
 D  is incorrect because even though a capillary is adapted for diffusion, it is not the best adapted from the listed structures. The ileum will collectively have a larger surface area for diffusion compared to one capillary.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which statement is false?
options: A. Fatty acids are a type of lipid
C. A triglyceride consists of three fatty acids and one glycerol molecule
D. Amino acids each have a side group (R) that distinguishes them from other amino acids
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The false statement is  A  (Fatty acids are a type of lipid) because:
 Fatty acids are part of a lipid molecule, so cannot be a type of lipid.
 All the other statements about biological molecules are true.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following best describes what an enzyme is?
options: A catalyst that speeds up reactions in cells, being used up in the process
B. A protein that speeds up reactions in cells, being used up in the process
C. A carbohydrate that functions as a biological catalyst
D. A protein that functions as a biological catalyst
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.  (A protein that functions as a biological catalyst) because:
 Enzymes are  proteins  (formed from chains of amino acids) which  increase  the  rate  of chemical  reactions  without being changed by it. This makes them catalysts, and because they are found in living organisms they are  ‘biological catalysts ’ (many catalysts in chemistry are metals which are obviously not biological!)
 A  and  B  are incorrect because enzymes, as catalysts, are not used up in the process of speeding up reactions.
 C  is incorrect because enzymes are made from protein, not carbohydrates.

 Which food contains reducing sugar and Vitamin C but  not  protein or starch?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • A positive Benedict’s test is the reagent changing colour from blue to brick-red/orange when heated (or yellow or green if a small amount of sugar is present in a sample)
 • DCPIP is a reagent that can be used to indicate the presence of Vitamin C within a sample; it is a blue solution when oxidised. When mixed with Vitamin C DCPIP is reduced, becoming colourless
 A  is incorrect because this food sample contains sugar, protein and Vitamin C. 
 C  is incorrect because this food sample does not contain starch only. 
 D  is incorrect because this food sample contains sugar, starch and Vitamin C.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A student sets up an experiment to measure the rate of oxygen production of an aquatic plant when it is photosynthesising.
 The student repeated the experiment several times to calculate the average amount of oxygen collected.
 Which two factors should be kept constant during the student’s experiment?
options: A. The size of the funnel and beaker.
B. The size of the aquatic plant and time exposed to light.
C. The size of the aquatic plant and the amount of water in the beaker.
D. The size of the aquatic plant and the amount of gas in the measuring cylinder.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (the size of the aquatic plant and time exposed to light.) because:
 • A smaller plant would photosynthesise less than a larger plant, affecting the amount of gas produced each time
 • The time of exposure to  light  is also a control variable as light is necessary for photosynthesis to occur, so each time the experiment is run the plants should be exposed to the same amount of light
 A  is incorrect because neither the beaker nor the funnel will affect the rate of photosynthesis.
 C  is incorrect because water is already in excess, the exact amount is not important as long as there is water in the measuring cylinder to be displaced by any gas produced by the plant and readings are taken before and after each experiment.
 D  is incorrect because the amount of gas in the measuring cylinder is the dependent variable, not a control variable.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
An experiment is set up with four test tubes as shown in the diagram below. 
 All four test tubes are left in sunlight for 6 hours. 
 Which test tube would contain the least amount of dissolved carbon dioxide after 6 hours?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • The test tube contains pondweed, which in the presence of light can  photosynthesise . As a result, carbon dioxide levels in the water will decrease
 • A carbon dioxide diffusion gradient is set up between the water and the leaves  as photosynthesis occurs, resulting in  diffusion  of carbon dioxide  into  the leaf for photosynthesis
 A  is incorrect because there is nothing in the test tube photosynthesising or respiring, so the concentration of carbon dioxide in the water will not change.
 B  is incorrect because although the  pondweed  in the test tube will be  photosynthesising  and therefore decreasing the carbon dioxide concentration of the water, the  snail  will be  respiring  and so releasing carbon dioxide. There will be more carbon dioxide than in test tube  C .
 D  is incorrect because the test tube contains a snail which will be  respiring  and therefore releasing carbon dioxide into the water, increasing the overall amount.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following best describes the function of vitamin D in a human?
options: A. Vitamin D forms an essential part of collagen protein which is the main component of skin, hair and nails.
B. Vitamin D is needed for strong bones and teeth and a deficiency may lead to osteoporosis later in life.
C. Vitamin D assists with the absorption of calcium and is therefore needed to build strong bones and teeth.
D. Vitamin D is an important component of haemoglobin which is needed for the transport of oxygen to the cells.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (Vitamin D assists with the absorption of calcium and is therefore needed to build strong bones and teeth.) because:
 Vitamin D facilitates the absorption of calcium into bones and teeth, which is required to provide strength to these parts. Without sufficient vitamin D intake, a child may develop rickets where the bones develop poorly.
 A  is incorrect because vitamin C is needed to make collagen, not vitamin D.
 B  is incorrect because even though vitamin D is needed for strong bones and teeth, a deficiency will not lead to osteoporosis later in life. That is a characteristic of a calcium deficiency.
 D  is incorrect because iron is an important component of haemoglobin and therefore plays a role in the transport of oxygen in the body.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following is  not  an example of physical digestion?
options: A. Breaking food up into smaller pieces by chewing it.
B. Starch being broken down into glucose molecules.
C. Food being churned when the muscles in the stomach lining contracts.
D. Bile breaking large fat droplets up into smaller ones during emulsification.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (Starch being broken down into glucose molecules.) because:
 The digestion of starch involves enzymes that break large insoluble starch molecules up into smaller soluble glucose molecules. Whenever enzymes are involved then it is an example of chemical digestion, not physical digestion.
 A ,  B  and  D  are incorrect because these are all examples of physical digestion where large food particles are mechanically broken down into smaller particles. This is done to increase the surface area on which the digestive enzymes can work during chemical digestion to change large insoluble molecules into smaller soluble ones.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram below shows four different types of human teeth. 
  Which teeth would be used to grind and chew food?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  (1 and 2) because:
 1  is a  premolar  tooth and  2  is a  molar  tooth. Premolars and molars have  larger , flatter  surfaces  with ridges at the edges for  chewing  and grinding up food.
 B  is incorrect because  3  is an  incisor , which is chisel shaped for  biting  and cutting.
 C  is incorrect because  1  (premolar) is also responsible for chewing and grinding of food.
 D  is incorrect because  3  is an  incisor , which is for  biting  and cutting while  4  is a  canine , which is pointed for tearing,  holding  and biting.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:

 • D  has the lowest total surface area (number of leaves × average surface area of one leaf) and also the lowest density of stomata per mm 2 , with each stoma being fairly small in diameter

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which row of the table below shows substances transported through the phloem and xylem, and the direction of transport, correctly?

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • The phloem carries sucrose (and amino acids) in all directions from sources (which depending on the time of year could be leaves or storage organs like roots) to sinks (other areas of the plant where the amino acids and sucrose will be used or stored)
 • The xylem transports water (and mineral ions) in one direction up the plant, from the roots to the leaves, driven by the pulling force generated by transpiration in the leaves
 A  is incorrect because transport in the xylem is unidirectional.
 B  is incorrect because the direction of transport in the phloem and the xylem is the wrong way around.
 D  is incorrect because transport in the phloem occurs in both directions.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following statements would be incorrect for most of the veins in the human body?
options: A. They carry blood at low pressure.
D. They return blood to the heart.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C.  (They have a pulse) because:
 Veins do not have a pulse. A person’s pulse is a measurement of heart rate based upon compression of an artery to feel expansion and contraction of arterial vessels as blood is forced through.
 A  is incorrect because veins return blood to the heart which has passed through the capillary network, and against the force of gravity, so blood pressure in the veins is low.
 B  is incorrect because almost all veins have valves to prevent the backflow of blood.
 D  is incorrect because veins are the blood vessels that connect the capillary network in the tissues of the body with the heart.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The human body has a number of barriers to prevent infection by pathogens some of which are listed below.
 • Skin
 • Mucus
 • Hairs in the nose
 • Antibodies
 • Stomach acid
 Which of these are examples of mechanical barriers?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A.  (1 and 3) because:
 The skin and hairs in the nose forms a physical barrier that makes it more difficult for pathogens to enter the body.
 B  and  C  are incorrect because mucus (2) is an example of a chemical barrier while antibodies (4) are produced by lymphocytes in response to foreign antigens entering the body, they do not act as a barrier.
 D  is incorrect because stomach acid (5) is another example of a chemical barrier, not a mechanical one.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: What is a pathogen?
options: B. A phagocyte that engulfs bacteria
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C.  (A disease-causing organism) because:
 A pathogen is a microorganism that infects another organism where it replicates / multiplies and causes disease.
 A  is incorrect because a transmissible disease is caused by a pathogen that can spread from one organism to another (e.g. Covid-19 is a transmissible disease caused by the pathogenic SARS-CoV-2 virus).
 B  is incorrect because phagocytes are part of the immune system responsible for destroying pathogens that have entered the body.
 D  is incorrect because not all bacteria (or microorganisms for that matter) are pathogenic. The human digestive system and skin, contains huge numbers of beneficial bacteria that help prevent infection (by competing with pathogens for resources).

  Which sample is inspired air and which sample is expired air?

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • Atmospheric air contains around 20 – 21%  oxygen , of which we only  absorb    around 4 – 5% , breathing out air containing around 16% oxygen
 • Normal  carbon dioxide  content of air is around  0.04%  and, as carbon dioxide diffuses into the alveoli from the blood, we breathe out air containing around  4%  carbon dioxide
 • The percentage of nitrogen in inspired and expired air is around 79 – 80%  and does not change as nitrogen is not able to be utilized by the body in the form of nitrogen gas

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A student investigated respiration in yeast. They set up the experiment as shown in the diagram below.

The correct answer is  C  because:
 The independent variable, the temperature of water, is what is changed during an experiment. The dependent variable, the number of bubbles, is what is measured and  depends  on the independent variable.
 The other answers are incorrect because the time and the volume of water are  control variables  and are something that needs to be kept the same throughout the experiment.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following organs are responsible for removing excretory products from the blood?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (kidneys and lungs) because:
 The kidneys remove urea, excess salts and water from the blood. The lungs remove carbon dioxide from the blood due to the concentration gradient set up between the air in the lungs and the carbon dioxide in the blood. This is maintained by breathing. 
 A  is incorrect because the bladder is not responsible for removing excretory products from the  blood , it removes it from the body.
 C  is incorrect because the liver is responsible for producing many of the excretory products, but it is not directly responsible for the excretion of these products.
 D  is incorrect because neither the bladder nor liver will remove excretory products from the blood for excretion as mentioned above.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which of the following statements are reasons for the evolution of reflex arcs in the mammalian nervous system?
 • To prevent harm or damage to an organism.
 • To provide a rapid response to dangerous situations.
 • To allow a degree of choice to an organism about response.
 • To allow certain stimuli to be ignored/eliminated.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (1 and 2 are correct) because:
 • Statement 1  (to prevent harm or damage to an organism) is correct because an automatic, rapid response to a dangerous stimulus cuts the reaction time and allows less damage to be sustained before a response takes place
 • Statement 2  (to provide a rapid response to dangerous situations) is correct, linked to the explanation for  Statement 1
 Statement 3  (to allow a degree of choice to an organism about response) is incorrect because reflexes are involuntary - they take place with no choice of conscious thought. 
 Statement 4  (to allow certain stimuli to be ignored/eliminated) is incorrect because a dangerous stimulus cannot be ignored, nor can one be eliminated; that would be outside an organism's ability to control events!

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Penicillin is an antibiotic that prevents bacteria growing by stopping them from forming cell walls.
 Why does penicillin not affect viruses?
options: A. Viruses do not have cell walls.
B. Viruses do not contain cytoplasm.
C. Viruses become resistant to penicillin.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 Viruses are technically not living cells, this means that they are not affected by antibiotics. Viruses do not have cell walls or carry out cellular functions. Antibiotics work by disrupting cell chemical reactions or the production of cell walls.
 B  is incorrect because viruses do not contain cytoplasm, and antibiotics don’t affect cytoplasm.
 C  is incorrect because penicillin does not work on viruses.
 D  is incorrect because this is correct as viruses use the host cell to reproduce rapidly. It is not relevant to why penicillin will not work on viruses, however.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
During birth the following processes happen:
 • Breaking of the amniotic sac
 • Contraction of the muscles in the uterine wall
 • Cutting of the umbilical cord
 In which order do these processes usually occur?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.  (2 → 1 → 3) because:
 • Birth begins when the muscles in the wall of the uterus start  contracting . This is the start of labour
 • At first the contractions of the muscles stretch the cervix. This is the point that the amniotic sac breaks
 • After a few hours, when the cervix is wide enough the head of the baby will pass through and the contractions will push the baby out through the vagina
 • Once the baby is born it will start to breathe for itself and no longer need to get its oxygen from the  placenta  via the umbilical cord. The umbilical cord is cut just above the point it joins the baby (forming the belly button)

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram shows the female reproductive system.
  After ejaculation, which pathway will the male gamete take to fuse with the egg?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A.  (Vagina →  cervix   → uterus  → oviduct) because:
 Ejaculation  takes place in the vagina; from there sperm travels through the cervix, into the uterus and then to the oviduct where (if it has been released) an egg can be fertilised. 
 B  and  D  are incorrect because they would both be correct paths of an egg that was not fertilised by a sperm cell.
 C  is incorrect because the sperm will need to go through the cervix before it can enter the uterus.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
In 1945, Sir Alexander Fleming warned about the evolution of antibiotic resistance in bacteria. There is currently an antibiotic resistance crisis.
 Which of the following actions would worsen the situation?
 • Patients not completing the course of prescribed antibiotics.
 • The use of antibiotics for serious bacterial infections only.
 • The careful selection of antibiotics to match the bacterial strain.
 • Treating viral infections with broad-spectrum antibiotics.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (1 and 4) because:
 When an individual fails to complete an antibiotic course their body is less likely to clear the bacterial infection so there is more opportunity for resistance to evolve in the bacterial population. Antibiotics should never be used to treat viral infections as they are ineffective against viruses.
 A  is incorrect because antibiotics are vital for patient survival when they are suffering from serious bacterial infections.
 B  is incorrect because 4 has not been included in the answer.
 D  is incorrect because both 2 and 3 represent ways in which antibiotics should be used in order to minimise antibiotic resistance.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Males and females have a unique set of chromosomes. 
 What is the correct combination of male and female chromosomes?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (males XY, females XX) because:
 The male sex chromosomes are inherited as an X and a Y chromosomes - the X from the mother and the Y from the father, giving a male the chromosomes XY. A female inherits an X from the mother and another X from the father, giving the chromosomes XX as a female.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Albinism is a condition where the pigment melanin does not get produced in the skin, hair and eyes. This is an inherited condition that is caused by a recessive allele.
 If both parents have albinism what are the chances of the offspring being an albino child?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  (100%) because:
 • If both parents have the condition then they will both have the same  genotype :  homozygous recessive
 • Both parents only have (two) copies of the recessive allele; therefore the gametes formed by  meiosis  in each parent will always contain a recessive allele, therefore the only possible genotype for any offspring from these parents will be homozygous recessive
 Note - in genetics it is key to know your definitions!
 • Gene  - section of the chromosome that codes for a particular characteristic
 • Allele  - alternative version of a gene
 • Genotype  -  the genetic make-up of an organism in terms of the alleles present
 • Phenotype  - the observable features (physical characteristics) of an organism
 • Homozygous  - having two identical alleles for the same gene
 • Heterozygous  - has two different alleles for a particular gene

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: What is a mutation?
options: A process used in genetic engineering.
B. A type of continuous variation.
C. A condition caused by a dominant allele.
D. A change in a gene.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  (a change in a gene) because:
 • The definition of a mutation is the change in the base sequence of DNA (which is a more detailed way of saying a change in a gene)
 • This is how we get different versions of the same genes known as  alleles
 • Mutations   are the basis of  genetic variation
 A  is incorrect because  genetic engineering  is a process that involves inserting a  gene  into an organism (from another)
 B  is incorrect because  continuous variation  is a type of variation that has a range of  phenotypes  often due to both genetic and environmental factors.
 C  is incorrect because a  dominant allele  is a version of a gene that will always be expressed in the  phenotype  of an organism.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram below illustrates part of the carbon cycle. 
  Which process is shown by the arrow labelled Y?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (respiration) because:
 Decomposers release energy from their food (dead matter) by  respiration . Essentially the source of food for a decomposer is a dead plant / animal and their consumption of dead matter leads to the recycling of nutrients back into the environment. They respire as they do this, releasing carbon dioxide.
 A  is incorrect because photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. This is shown by the arrow from carbon dioxide in the atmosphere to green plants.
 B  is incorrect because feeding is to take in food, this process is shown by the arrows from green plants to decomposers and green plants to animals.
 D  is incorrect because combustion releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. This is shown by the arrow from fossil fuels to carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The image shows a food web. 
  Which organism, from the food web, feeds on the greatest variety of organisms?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (crabs) because:
 Crabs feed on mussels, lugworms and limpets. This gives them the largest range of food sources (3 in all) in this food web. This would mean that they have the greatest chance of survival if one of their food sources decreased in number.
 A  is incorrect because whelks only have one source of food, mussels.
 C  is incorrect because limpets only have one source of food, sea lettuce.
 D  is incorrect because mussels only have one source of food, small invertebrates.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The graph below shows the growth of the human population globally since 1630.
  Which of the following options represents the longest time period taken for the population of humans to double?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (200 years) because:
 Between 1630 and 1830 the population increased from 500 million to 1000 million. This is the longest time period represented on the graph for the population to double. After 1830 there was rapid growth of the human population, the time for the population to double was significantly less.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of these statements correctly describes genetic engineering?
options: A. Only breeding from crop plants that are resistant to pests.
B. Altering the DNA in crop plants so that they are resistant to herbicides.
C. Using yeast to produce ethanol.
D. Production of insulin in the pancreas.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (altering the DNA in crop plants so that they are resistant to herbicides) because:
 Genetic engineering  is the process of altering  DNA  to include new  genes  or sequences of  DNA.  This will give the modified organism new characteristics that may increase yield or increase resistance to chemicals.
 A  is incorrect because this process describes  selective breeding .   Selective breeding is the use of organisms with a particular characteristic in breeding so that the offspring have the trait that you desire.
 C  is incorrect because this process describes  fermentation . This is a natural process that has been exploited for centuries to produce bread and beer.
 D  is incorrect because this is a natural process that occurs normally in healthy individuals.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following is a correct example of a population?
options: All the animals in a forest.
B. All the goldfish in a pond.
C. All the species of animals in Europe.
D. All the people born in Scotland over a 150-year period.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 The definition of a population is 'the same species living in the same habitat at the same time'.
 A  is incorrect because this answer refers to ‘all the animals’, it is highly unlikely all of the animals in a forest belong to the same species, so this is not a definition of a population.
 C  is incorrect because this refers to more than one species so is not the definition of population.
 D  is incorrect because while this refers to a number of organisms of the same species this is not at the same time as over 150 years, some of the people will have died and other will have been born.

set-3/paper-3-theory-core.stem:
Water is important for living organisms as many substances are able to dissolve in it.
 Give  two  examples of the importance of water as a solvent in living organisms.
set-3/paper-3-theory-core.explanation:
The importance of water as a solvent in living organisms includes...
 Any  two  of the following:
 • Dissolved substances can be easily transported around organisms  OR  a named example e.g. xylem transporting water and mineral ions / phloem transporting sucrose and amino acids / blood transporting dissolved food molecules;  [1 mark]
 • Digested food molecules in the alimentary canal dissolve in water to be absorbed into the blood (for transport to cells);  [1 mark]
 • Toxic substances/urea / substances in excess can dissolve in water to be (easily) excreted in urine;  [1 mark]
 • Ensures that metabolic reactions can occur (in solution) within cells;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 2 marks]
 Make sure to familiarise yourself with the importance of water as a solvent in living organisms as this is a question you may come across in an exam paper.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which name can be given to a group of organisms that have similar morphological features and can reproduce successfully to produce fertile offspring?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  (species) because:
 Members of the same species usually look similar or share similar features, and crucially, can reproduce to produce offspring that can in turn go on to produce fertile offspring themselves. 
 A  is incorrect because a kingdom is an extremely large group containing different phyla. For example, animals make up one kingdom, plants make up another. 
 B  is incorrect because a genus is a group containing several different species with similar characteristics and evolutionary history. 
 C  is incorrect because a family is a taxonomic classification between order and genus; a family contains many different genera.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The image below shows a leaf from a plant.
  Identify the plant to which the leaf belongs using the dichotomous key below.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  ( F. americana ) because:
 The leaf shown is not in one piece, the start of the question states ‘the diagram shows a leaf’ which means a single leaf. Therefore this leaf is in more than one piece. The leaf edge is smooth.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Use the key to identify the group to which fish belong.

 Fur present...

 mammals

 group  A

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is group  C  because:
 Fish do not have fur, lay eggs without shells, reproduce in water, and have scales.
 Group A would be birds, as birds lay eggs with hard shells.
 Group B would be reptiles, as reptiles lay their eggs on land.
 Group D would be amphibians, as they have smooth skin.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of the following terms would be correct to describe a leaf, a root and stem?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (organ) because:
 All three structures in the question are organs. An organ is a group of two or more tissues working together to carry out a particular function.
 A  is incorrect because each of the leaves, stems and roots are made up of thousands of different cells all working together. 
 B  is incorrect because the  leaf  is made from  palisade  &  spongy  mesophyll tissue,  epidermal  tissue and  vascular  tissue functioning together to allow a plant to photosynthesise. The  roots  and  stem  are made from  vascular  (transport)  tissue  which work together to transport substances around the plant.
 D  is incorrect because together plants have two organ systems. The  shoot organ system  in a plant is made from leaves, stems, buds, fruits and flowers. The  root organ system  of most plants are all the parts that are underground.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Which row of the table below correctly describes a spongy mesophyll cell?
 |  
 | contains chloroplasts for photosynthesis
 | loses water by transpiration
 | ideal surface area for gas exchange
 |

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 Spongy mesophyll cells contain chloroplasts for photosynthesis and have a relatively large surface area for gas exchange with the air spaces in the leaf. They also lose water by transpiration; water evaporates from the surfaces of the spongy cells, diffusing into the air spaces and out of the stomata.
 The other answers are incorrect because they do not correctly describe a spongy mesophyll cell.
 The diagram below shows the structure of the leaf and the position of the spongy mesophyll cells within the leaf.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Eukaryotic cells contain mitochondria (a mitochondrion is shown below).
  Which diagram below correctly shows the position of mitochondria in a plant cell?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 Mitochondria are usually slightly smaller than chloroplasts and are found within the cytoplasm. Mitochondria have a highly folded internal membrane, whereas chloroplasts look like they contain stacks of pancakes (sometimes!).
 B  is incorrect because mitochondria are not found within the cell wall; in fact, no organelles are found within the cell wall. 
 C  is incorrect because mitochondria are not found within the vacuole.
 D  is incorrect because this cell is an animal cell. You can tell this because of the absence of a cell wall and vacuole.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A number of red blood cells were immersed in pure water before being observed under a microscope. There was a dramatic change in their appearance. 
 Which row of the table below correctly describes what happened to the red blood cells?

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Pure water has a solute concentration of zero and has the highest possible water potential
 • Water will therefore move  into red blood cells  by osmosis when they are placed in pure water
 • Water moves from  low to high solute concentration  and from  high to  low water potential  through a partially permeable membrane
 • This will cause the cells to swell and eventually  burst

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Plants take in various essential substances through their roots.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • Water always moves across cell membranes by osmosis
 • Oxygen is a gas and will move by diffusion down a concentration gradient
 • Minerals are taken up against their concentration gradients across the membrane of root hair cells

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which drawing represents the general structure of an amino acid molecule that would be found in Nature?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 An amino acid always has a H- atom, an -NH 2  group and a -COOH group around a central carbon atom.
 A  is incorrect because there are two central carbon atoms showing. 
 B  is incorrect because the group on the right is missing an oxygen atom (-COH as opposed to -COOH).
 C  is incorrect because it has a methyl group (-CH 3 ) where a single hydrogen atom should be.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The effect of pH on the rate of reaction of three different enzymes is shown in the graph below.
  What does the graph show?
options: A. Each enzyme works best over a narrow temperature range.
B. Most enzymes work best around a neutral pH.
C. Enzymes work better in acidic conditions.
D. Each enzyme works best at a different pH.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.  (Each enzyme works best at a different pH) because:
 For enzyme 1, the rate of reaction is quickest at pH 1.5, making this its optimum pH. For enzyme 2, the rate of reaction is quickest at pH 7, making this its optimum pH. And for enzyme 3, the rate of reaction is quickest at pH 14, making this its optimum pH.
 A  is incorrect because the graph gives no information about temperature. 
 B  is incorrect because only enzyme 2 works best in neutral conditions.
 C  is incorrect because only enzyme 1 works best in acidic conditions.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The table below shows the elements and basic units used by cells to make large biological molecules.

 Which row of the table is correct?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 Amino acids are the basic building blocks of protein molecules (the order of amino acids needed to build a protein is determined by the sequence of DNA bases in genes). Amino acids always contain the elements carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen.
 B  is incorrect because glycerol is one of the basic units of fats (a type of lipid) but lipids do not contain nitrogen. 
 C  is incorrect because glycerol is one of the basic units of fats (a type of lipid) but lipids do contain oxygen, not nitrogen.
 D  is incorrect because bases are the building blocks of DNA, and they contain the three main elements listed in the table as well as nitrogen and phosphorus.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A student sets up an experiment to measure the rate of oxygen production of an aquatic plant when it is photosynthesising.
 The student repeated the experiment several times to calculate the average amount of oxygen collected.
 Which two factors should be kept constant during the student’s experiment?
options: A. The size of the funnel and beaker.
B. The size of the aquatic plant and time exposed to light.
C. The size of the aquatic plant and the amount of water in the beaker.
D. The size of the aquatic plant and the amount of gas in the measuring cylinder.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (the size of the aquatic plant and time exposed to light.) because:
 • A smaller plant would photosynthesise less than a larger plant, affecting the amount of gas produced each time
 • The time of exposure to  light  is also a control variable as light is necessary for photosynthesis to occur, so each time the experiment is run the plants should be exposed to the same amount of light
 A  is incorrect because neither the beaker nor the funnel will affect the rate of photosynthesis.
 C  is incorrect because water is already in excess, the exact amount is not important as long as there is water in the measuring cylinder to be displaced by any gas produced by the plant and readings are taken before and after each experiment.
 D  is incorrect because the amount of gas in the measuring cylinder is the dependent variable, not a control variable.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The pH of an enzyme controlled reaction is decreased by a pH of 2. 
 How does this affect the rate of the reaction?
options: A. It has no effect on the rate.
B. It always decreases the rate.
C. It always increases the rate.
D. It may increase or decrease the rate .
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.  (It may increase or decrease the rate) because:
 • Whether the  rate  of enzyme activity increases or decreases  depends  on what the  optimum  pH for the enzyme is. In mammals, it would depend if the enzyme acts inside cells, or if it were a digestive enzyme
 • If the increase in pH takes the pH away from the optimum in either direction, then the rate will slow down
 • If the increase in pH moves the pH towards the optimum, then the rate will increase
 The other answers are incorrect because they do not correctly state how changing the pH will affect the rate of reaction.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Which of the following correctly identifies some of the molecules produced from the glucose synthesised by photosynthesis?
 |  
 | 1
 | 2
 | 3
 |
 | A
 | cellulose for storage
 | fats and oils for  energy storage
 | starch to build cell walls
 |
 | B
 | cellulose to build cell walls
 | fats and oils for energy storage
 | starch for storage
 |
 | C
 | sucrose to be transported around the plant
 | fats and oils for energy storage
 | cellulose for storage
 |
 | D
 | sucrose to be transported around the plant
 | starch to build cell walls
 | cellulose for storage
 |
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Glucose is converted into cellulose which is needed to form cell walls
 • Glucose is converted into starch for storage within the cell, as starch is insoluble and therefore doesn’t influence water levels in the cells (glucose is soluble and can affect osmosis)
 • Glucose is also converted to fats and oils for energy storage in seeds
 A  and  D  are incorrect because cellulose is not used for storage and starch is not used to build cell walls.
 C  is incorrect because glucose is converted into sucrose to be transported around the plant (via the phloem), but cellulose is not used for storage.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A student ate a meal which contained a type of biomolecule,  X .
 The digestion of biomolecule  X  started in the mouth, and finished in the duodenum.
 What is the product of the digestion of biomolecule  X ?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (Glucose) because:
 Starch , a large biomolecule, is made from many molecules of  glucose  molecules bonded together.  Salivary   amylase , an enzyme produced by the salivary glands, acts on starch and breaks it down into  maltose  (a disaccharide).  Amylase  is also produced by the  pancreas , to help digest any remaining starch in the small intestine. Maltose is broken down by the enzyme  maltase  (which is found in the lining of the small intestine), producing  glucose  molecules.
 A  and  B  are incorrect because amino acids are the product of protein digestion, which begins in the stomach, not the mouth.
 D  is incorrect because starch was the starting molecule in this process (starch is a polymer of glucose molecules).

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram below shows four different types of human teeth. 
  Which teeth would be used to grind and chew food?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  (1 and 2) because:
 1  is a  premolar  tooth and  2  is a  molar  tooth. Premolars and molars have  larger , flatter  surfaces  with ridges at the edges for  chewing  and grinding up food.
 B  is incorrect because  3  is an  incisor , which is chisel shaped for  biting  and cutting.
 C  is incorrect because  1  (premolar) is also responsible for chewing and grinding of food.
 D  is incorrect because  3  is an  incisor , which is for  biting  and cutting while  4  is a  canine , which is pointed for tearing,  holding  and biting.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A student collected some of the solution from the phloem in the stem of a plant. 
 Which of the following would be present in the liquid?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 Amino acids would be the only substance from the options given to move through the phloem (as well as sucrose).
 A  is incorrect because glucose is never transported through the phloem; however, sucrose (a disaccharide that contains one glucose molecule) is transported through the phloem.
 B  and  D  are incorrect because starch and cellulose are large biomolecules that are insoluble in water, therefore they cannot be moved around the plant.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of the following statements would be incorrect for most of the veins in the human body?
options: A. They carry blood at low pressure.
D. They return blood to the heart.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C.  (They have a pulse) because:
 Veins do not have a pulse. A person’s pulse is a measurement of heart rate based upon compression of an artery to feel expansion and contraction of arterial vessels as blood is forced through.
 A  is incorrect because veins return blood to the heart which has passed through the capillary network, and against the force of gravity, so blood pressure in the veins is low.
 B  is incorrect because almost all veins have valves to prevent the backflow of blood.
 D  is incorrect because veins are the blood vessels that connect the capillary network in the tissues of the body with the heart.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of the following diseases can be transmitted by contact with contaminated surfaces?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.  (Salmonella and athletes foot) because:
 Both these diseases are transmitted when a person comes into contact with a surface that contains these pathogens.
 A  is incorrect because malaria is transmitted by the bite of the female  Anopheles  mosquito.
 B  is incorrect because typhoid is transmitted by the consumption of water or food contaminated with the faeces of people infected with typhoid.
 C  is incorrect because influenza spreads by inhaling droplets in the air carrying the virus while dengue fever is spread by the bite of a specific species of mosquito ( Aedes aegypti ).

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Four different stages in one heartbeat are shown in the diagram below.
  Which of the following depicts a correct order of stages?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.  (X → Z → W → Y) because:
 • Stage  X  – blood enters the atria
 • Stage  Z  – the walls of the atria contract and blood moves into the ventricles
 • Stage  W  – the walls of the ventricles contract and blood is pushed up through the valves into the arteries
 • Stage  Y  – the arteries carry blood away from the heart and more blood is carried towards the heart in the veins

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Passive and active immunity have which of the following features in common?
 • They are always long-term.
 • They always involve the activity of memory cells.
 • They involve antibodies.
 • They can be acquired by vaccination.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.  (3 only) because:
 • Both active and passive immunity involve antibodies being present to help the immune system (particularly phagocytes) fight an infectious pathogen causing disease
 • In active immunity, the antibodies are acquired by having memory cells present in the body (as a result of prior infection with the pathogen or vaccination) which can make them, whereas in passive immunity the antibodies are acquired directly from another person either through an infusion of blood plasma,  or passed from mother to baby via breast milk
 A  is incorrect because long-term effects and the activity of memory cells only apply in cases of active immunity.
 C  is incorrect because memory cells are not involved in passive immunity.
 D  is incorrect because only active immunity is developed by vaccination.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram below shows a cross-section through an alveolus and a capillary.
  Why does oxygen move from P to Q?
options: A. The concentration of carbon dioxide is lower in the alveolus than in the blood.
B. The concentration of oxygen in the blood is lower than in the air in the capillary.
C. Oxygen must replace carbon dioxide.
D. The concentration of oxygen in the blood is lower than the air in the alveolus.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.  (The concentration of oxygen in the blood is lower than the air in the alveolus) because:
 Blood is deoxygenated when it enters the lung capillaries, therefore there is an oxygen concentration gradient between P and Q. There is a  higher   concentration of oxygen in the air in the alveolus than in the   blood , leading to  diffusion  of oxygen into the blood.
 A  is incorrect because the movement of oxygen is not affected by the concentration gradient for carbon dioxide
 B  is incorrect because there is no air in the capillary; the air is in the alveolus.
 C  is incorrect because the movement of each gas (carbon dioxide and oxygen) is dependent on the concentration gradient of each individual gas, not on the concentration of the other gas.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

 Respiration occurs in  ALL  plant cells  ALL  the time, regardless of where in the plant they are. Light only affects the rate of photosynthesis in plant cells, and obviously being underground root hair cells do not photosynthesise (but that’s irrelevant here).

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Which row of the table below correctly displays the correct roles of the following organs in processing waste in the human body?

 | kidneys

 | lungs

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Urea is one of the substances forced out of the blood in the kidneys; this occurs in the glomerulus (capillary network) where urea passes into the Bowman’s capsule at the start of a kidney tubule (nephron) and is not reabsorbed back into the bloodstream
 • Excess amino acids are broken down primarily by the liver, the nitrogen part (called an amine group) is converted into urea and then secreted back into the bloodstream. The remaining part of the amino acid can be converted into a number of substances that can be used in respiration or stored
 • The lungs are responsible for excreting carbon dioxide; there is a diffusion gradient between blood passing through the lungs from the heart which contains carbon dioxide that has diffused into the blood from respiring tissues, and the air in the lungs
 A  is incorrect because the liver does not excrete amino acids; it breaks them down into a number of substances of which urea is a waste product which is t

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Which of the following processes require, and are dependent on, the activity of enzymes?
 • aerobic respiration
 • glucose → lactic acid
 • osmosis
 • anaerobic respiration in yeast
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (1, 2 and 4) because:
 • Enzymes are proteins that act as biological catalysts, speeding up reaction times
 • All cellular reactions in living cells are catalyzed by enzymes such as respiration and the breakdown of glucose to lactic acid
 Osmosis is not a reaction, it is the diffusion of water from high to lower water potential through a partially permeable membrane, and therefore it does not require the action of an enzyme to occur.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of the following substances would be reabsorbed by the kidneys?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (salts and glucose) because:
 The kidneys reabsorb all the glucose that enters the tubules (by active transport in selective reabsorption) and some salts, depending on the concentration of salts in the blood and how much water needs to be reabsorbed.
 Urea is not reabsorbed back into the bloodstream from the kidney tubules, and glycogen would not be present in the filtrate in the first place (it is a relatively large molecule and isn’t usually present in the blood).

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Which of the following statements about glucagon are  false ?
 • Glucagon reverses the effect of the hormone glycogen
 • Glucagon is produced in the pancreas
 • Glucagon is secreted when blood glucose levels fall
 • Glucagon stimulates liver and muscle cells to convert glucose into stored glycogen
 • Glucagon is a polysaccharide
 • Glucagon is usually secreted soon after ingestion of carbohydrate-rich food
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (the  false  statements are 1, 4, 5 and 6) because:
 To deal with the statements in turn:
 • Glucagon reverses the effect of the hormone glycogen - FALSE - glycogen is not a hormone; glucagon reverses the effects of the hormone  insulin
 • Glucagon is produced in the pancreas - TRUE
 • Glucagon is secreted when blood glucose levels fall - TRUE
 • Glucagon stimulates liver and muscle cells to convert glucose into stored glycogen - FALSE; glucagon has the opposite effect to release glucose from stored glycogen in the liver and muscles
 • Glucagon is a polysaccharide - FALSE - glucagon, like most hormones, is a protein
 • Glucagon is usually secreted soon after ingestion of carbohydrate-rich food - FALSE, this is when insulin is usually secreted

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Penicillin is an antibiotic that prevents bacteria growing by stopping them from forming cell walls.
 Why does penicillin not affect viruses?
options: A. Viruses do not have cell walls.
B. Viruses do not contain cytoplasm.
C. Viruses become resistant to penicillin.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 Viruses are technically not living cells, this means that they are not affected by antibiotics. Viruses do not have cell walls or carry out cellular functions. Antibiotics work by disrupting cell chemical reactions or the production of cell walls.
 B  is incorrect because viruses do not contain cytoplasm, and antibiotics don’t affect cytoplasm.
 C  is incorrect because penicillin does not work on viruses.
 D  is incorrect because this is correct as viruses use the host cell to reproduce rapidly. It is not relevant to why penicillin will not work on viruses, however.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
During birth the following processes happen:
 • Breaking of the amniotic sac
 • Contraction of the muscles in the uterine wall
 • Cutting of the umbilical cord
 In which order do these processes usually occur?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.  (2 → 1 → 3) because:
 • Birth begins when the muscles in the wall of the uterus start  contracting . This is the start of labour
 • At first the contractions of the muscles stretch the cervix. This is the point that the amniotic sac breaks
 • After a few hours, when the cervix is wide enough the head of the baby will pass through and the contractions will push the baby out through the vagina
 • Once the baby is born it will start to breathe for itself and no longer need to get its oxygen from the  placenta  via the umbilical cord. The umbilical cord is cut just above the point it joins the baby (forming the belly button)

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of the following statements would  not  be a correct example of negative feedback?
options: An increase in core body temperature when cold.
C. The release of a neurotransmitter at a synapse.
D. The control of blood glucose levels.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 The release of a neurotransmitter at a synapse is not an example of negative feedback. Negative feedback mechanisms are the responses that occur in the body when a factor/system moves away from the normal range in which it should fall.
 A  is incorrect because maintenance of a core body temperature within a narrow range is a key example of negative feedback.
 B  is incorrect because vasoconstriction (constriction of arterioles in the skin) is part of a negative feedback response to a decrease in body temperature and is an action to reduce heat loss.
 D  is incorrect because the hormones insulin and glucagon act to maintain blood glucose levels within a narrow range, another key example of negative feedback.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which organ is involved in the metabolic breakdown of oral medication?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (liver) because:
 The liver is the primary site for drug metabolism.
 A  is incorrect because although the stomach is involved in the digestion of some oral medications it does not fully metabolise the drug.
 C  and  D  are incorrect because the brain and kidneys are not the primary sites of drug metabolism.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
In 1945, Sir Alexander Fleming warned about the evolution of antibiotic resistance in bacteria. There is currently an antibiotic resistance crisis.
 Which of the following actions would worsen the situation?
 • Patients not completing the course of prescribed antibiotics.
 • The use of antibiotics for serious bacterial infections only.
 • The careful selection of antibiotics to match the bacterial strain.
 • Treating viral infections with broad-spectrum antibiotics.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (1 and 4) because:
 When an individual fails to complete an antibiotic course their body is less likely to clear the bacterial infection so there is more opportunity for resistance to evolve in the bacterial population. Antibiotics should never be used to treat viral infections as they are ineffective against viruses.
 A  is incorrect because antibiotics are vital for patient survival when they are suffering from serious bacterial infections.
 B  is incorrect because 4 has not been included in the answer.
 D  is incorrect because both 2 and 3 represent ways in which antibiotics should be used in order to minimise antibiotic resistance.

 • Fertilisation hasn’t taken place as the  pollen tube  has not connected with the  ovum  and there is no pollen grain nucleus visible in the  ovary

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
There are a number of hormones that control fertility in women.
 Which one of these maintains the lining during pregnancy?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.  (Progesterone) because:
 • Progesterone is produced by the  corpus luteum  after ovulation. This maintains the lining of the  uterus  until the  placenta  can be developed and continue the production of progesterone until birth
 • If no fertilisation occurs, the corpus luteum breaks down which leads to a fall in progesterone so that the lining of the uterus is no longer maintained and is lost (a period)
 A  is incorrect because oestrogen stimulates the thickening of the uterus lining in the menstrual cycle.
 C  is incorrect because FSH stimulates the development of a follicle in the ovary.
 D  is incorrect because testosterone is a male sex hormone and has no role in the menstrual cycle.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Albinism is a condition where the pigment melanin does not get produced in the skin, hair and eyes. This is an inherited condition that is caused by a recessive allele.
 If both parents have albinism what are the chances of the offspring being an albino child?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  (100%) because:
 • If both parents have the condition then they will both have the same  genotype :  homozygous recessive
 • Both parents only have (two) copies of the recessive allele; therefore the gametes formed by  meiosis  in each parent will always contain a recessive allele, therefore the only possible genotype for any offspring from these parents will be homozygous recessive
 Note - in genetics it is key to know your definitions!
 • Gene  - section of the chromosome that codes for a particular characteristic
 • Allele  - alternative version of a gene
 • Genotype  -  the genetic make-up of an organism in terms of the alleles present
 • Phenotype  - the observable features (physical characteristics) of an organism
 • Homozygous  - having two identical alleles for the same gene
 • Heterozygous  - has two different alleles for a particular gene

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The image shows a food web. 
  Which organism, from the food web, feeds on the greatest variety of organisms?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (crabs) because:
 Crabs feed on mussels, lugworms and limpets. This gives them the largest range of food sources (3 in all) in this food web. This would mean that they have the greatest chance of survival if one of their food sources decreased in number.
 A  is incorrect because whelks only have one source of food, mussels.
 C  is incorrect because limpets only have one source of food, sea lettuce.
 D  is incorrect because mussels only have one source of food, small invertebrates.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The graph below shows the growth of the human population globally since 1630.
  Which of the following options represents the longest time period taken for the population of humans to double?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (200 years) because:
 Between 1630 and 1830 the population increased from 500 million to 1000 million. This is the longest time period represented on the graph for the population to double. After 1830 there was rapid growth of the human population, the time for the population to double was significantly less.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of the following is the correct definition for a sustainable resource?
options: A resource that can be replaced.
B. A resource that is running out.
C. Making sure that needs are met for future generations.
D. A resource that can be replenished as quickly as it is used.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  (a resource that can be replenished as quickly as it is used) because:
 A sustainable resource is a resource that can be replaced (almost) as quickly as it is used. This means that it will not run out. An example of this would be planting a tree to replace one that is chopped down.
 A  is incorrect because this statement only refers to resource replacement and not that it can be replaced as quickly as it is used.
 B  is incorrect because this statement only refers to resources, and does not take into account the needs of the future populations.
 C  is incorrect because sustainability is about protecting both the environment and resources for now and the future.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of these statements correctly describes genetic engineering?
options: A. Only breeding from crop plants that are resistant to pests.
B. Altering the DNA in crop plants so that they are resistant to herbicides.
C. Using yeast to produce ethanol.
D. Production of insulin in the pancreas.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (altering the DNA in crop plants so that they are resistant to herbicides) because:
 Genetic engineering  is the process of altering  DNA  to include new  genes  or sequences of  DNA.  This will give the modified organism new characteristics that may increase yield or increase resistance to chemicals.
 A  is incorrect because this process describes  selective breeding .   Selective breeding is the use of organisms with a particular characteristic in breeding so that the offspring have the trait that you desire.
 C  is incorrect because this process describes  fermentation . This is a natural process that has been exploited for centuries to produce bread and beer.
 D  is incorrect because this is a natural process that occurs normally in healthy individuals.

 One of the students states that salivary amylase must be responsible for digesting starch in the small intestine. The student is incorrect.
 Use the results in  Table 1  to explain why.
set-4/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
The student is incorrect because...

(i) The function of a red blood cell is:
 • (To) transport oxygen;  [1 mark]
 (ii) Ways in which a red blood cell is adapted to its function are:
 Any  two  from the following:
 • Contains haemoglobin;  [1 mark]
 • Biconcave (disc shape) / large surface area to volume ratio;  [1 mark]
 • No nucleus / (named) organelle;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 3 marks]

set-4/paper-4-theory-extended.stem: Compare natural selection with artificial selection.
set-4/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
A comparison of natural selection with artificial selection is...
 • Natural selection occurs naturally due to selection pressures within the environment  whereas  artificial selection is carried out by humans (selecting organisms with the most suitable characteristics);  [1 mark]
 • Natural selection results in populations with features/characteristics better adapted to the environment  whereas  artificial selection results in populations (more) useful to humans;  [1 mark]
 • Natural selection takes many generations / a long time to occur  whereas  artificial selection takes fewer generations / less time to occur;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 3 marks]

set-4/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
There are many threats to wildlife in the Galapagos.
 Describe ways in which endangered species can be conserved.
set-4/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
Endangered species can be conserved in the following ways...
 Any  five  of the following:
 • Monitoring/studying population(s)/individual(s);  [1 mark]
 • Protecting/restoring habitats;  [1 mark]
 • Preventing pollution (of habitats);  [1 mark]
 • Removal of alien/new species;  [1 mark]
 • Preventing colonisation by alien species;  [1 mark]
 • Introducing hunting bans / preventing poaching;  [1 mark]
 • Implementing government legislation/law to protect species;  [1 mark]
 • Create exclusion zones / reserves / conservation areas (so that habitats are not disturbed by people);  [1 mark]
 • Introduce specific times when / areas where hunting is not allowed;  [1 mark]
 • International agreements to limit trade (of endangered species / parts of endangered species);  [1 mark]
 • Removal (of endangered organisms) to zoos/botanical gardens/wildlife parks;  [1 mark]
 • Initiate captive breeding / breeding programme (in situ or ex situ);  [1 mark]
 • (Storage of endangered species in) seed ban

set-4/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a condition that commonly occurs in women of reproductive age. It is characterised by hormonal imbalances that affect the menstrual cycle of women with this condition.
 Fig. 1 compares the levels of FSH and LH in a normal menstrual cycle with the levels seen in the cycle of a woman with PCOS.
  Fig. 1
 Use the information in Fig. 1 to explain the effect that PCOS would have on the ovaries of a woman.
set-4/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
The effect that PCOS would have on the ovaries of a woman would include...
 Any  three  of the following:
 • Low FSH levels  SO  an egg will not mature;  [1 mark]
 • Low FSH  SO  oestrogen will not be released;  [1 mark]
 • No oestrogen  SO  LH will not be released;  [1 mark]
 • Low LH / no LH increase  SO  no ovulation / no egg will be released (from ovary);  [1 mark]
 Where capitalised SO is present the statements on both sides of SO are required for a mark to be awarded.
 [Total: 3 marks]
 Note that this is an explain question, so each effect on the ovaries needs to be linked to its hormonal cause for a mark to be awarded.

set-4/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
The stomach produces gastric juice which contains hydrochloric acid.
 Explain the importance of hydrochloric acid in the stomach.
set-4/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
Hydrochloric acid is important in the stomach because...
 • It kills bacteria in food because the low pH denatures their enzymes;  [1 mark]
 • This means they cannot carry out any cell reactions to maintain life;  [1 mark]
 • It ensures that the pH (in the stomach) is at an optimum for the working of pepsin;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 3 marks]

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which class of vertebrate typically gives birth to live young?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  (mammals) because:
 Mammals are generally the only group of vertebrates to give birth to live young.
 B, C  and  D  are all incorrect because all other vertebrate classes tend to lay eggs.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following orders would be correct showing the size of structures from biggest to smallest?
options: A. chromosome → red blood cell → stomach → gene → nucleus
B. stomach → red blood cell → gene → chromosome
C. stomach → red blood cell → nucleus → chromosome →  gene
D. gene → chromosome → red blood cell → stomach
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (stomach → red blood cell → nucleus → chromosome →  gene) because:
 • Genes are the smallest structures shown; genes are ‘coding’ sections of DNA
 • A chromosome is formed from a relatively long piece of double-stranded DNA; chromosomes are found inside the nucleus of cells and therefore must logically be smaller than a single cell
 • Red blood cells do not contain nuclei, but they are bigger than them
 • The stomach is an organ and so logically is the biggest structure listed
 The other answers are incorrect because they do not show the correct size order of the structures.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which row shows the three main elements from the Period Table that are present in most molecules in living organisms?
 | A
 | carbon
 | oxygen
 | nitrogen
 |
 | B
 | hydrogen
 | carbon
 | oxygen
 |
 | C
 | oxygen
 | sulfur
 | carbon
 |
 | D
 | hydrogen
 | carbon
 | nitrogen
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (hydrogen, carbon, oxygen) because:
 These three elements are the main constituents of carbohydrates and lipids; all proteins also contain them, along with other elements.
 Nitrogen, sulfur, phosphorus (not shown in the table) and trace elements are all important for life but are not found in most molecules in living organisms.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Four statements about large biological molecules are given below:
 • Proteins are made from a number of different amino acids.
 • Both glycogen and starch are made from simple sugar base units.
 • Fats are made from glycerol and fatty acids.
 • Oils are made from glycerol only. 
 Which of the four statements above is/are  false ?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 The question asks which of the statements given is  false . Statements 1, 2 and 3 are all true.
 Statement 4 is false because oils (like fats, a type of lipid) are made from glycerol and fatty acids. 
 Around 20 different amino acids are used to build protein molecules in almost all living cells. The basic structure of each amino acid is largely the same, with one variable region differing to produce a variety of amino acids. Glycogen and starch, as well as cellulose, are all polymers of glucose.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram below shows part of an organism (ciliated epithelium). 
  What term would correctly describe the level of organisation of the structure in the diagram above?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  (cell) because:
 The image shows a ciliated epithelial cell. These cells can be found lining the trachea and parts of the lungs. Cells are the basic functional units of all living organisms on Earth. 
 B  is incorrect because organelle is a term used to describe subcellular structures within cells, such as mitochondria and chloroplasts.
 C  is incorrect because an organ is formed from two or more tissues working together. Tissues are made from groups of similar cells.
 D  is incorrect because an organ system is made from organs working together to perform a particular function.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which row of the table below correctly matches a structure to its level of organisation within an organism?
