set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • The phloem is a transport tissue in plants formed from a number of cell types; including conducting cells (responsible for moving sugars around the plant) and structural and support cells
 • The small intestine is an organ because it is made from a number of different tissues; including muscular tissue, epithelial tissue and nervous tissue
 • The digestive system is made from a number of organs involved in the breakdown of large insoluble molecules into small soluble molecules
 B  is incorrect because blood is a tissue, RBCs are one of the cells in the blood; the xylem is a tissue not an organ, and the stomach is an organ.
 C  is incorrect because the small intestine is an organ and the spermatozoa are cells.
 D  is incorrect because root hair cells are not tissue, the heart is an organ part of the circulatory system.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: How does a water vapour molecule move out of the air space of a leaf into the atmosphere on a dry day?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (Diffusion) because:
 Water vapour is just water molecules in the gaseous state; in the leaf water vapour forms when water molecules evaporate from the surface of spongy mesophyll. All gas molecules move by diffusion – the movement of molecules and ions from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration down a concentration gradient as a result of random movement.
 A  is incorrect because active transport requires protein molecules embedded within a membrane using energy released via respiration to move molecules deliberately into the cell (usually against a concentration gradient).
 C  is incorrect because evaporation occurs at the surface of spongy mesophyll cells in the leaf, liquid water changes state to water vapour (a gas). 
 D  is incorrect because transpiration is the loss of water vapour from plant leaves by evaporation of water at the surfaces of the mesophyll cells followed by diffusion of water vapour through the stomata.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Three statements about the role of water in mammals are given below:
 • Water forms a major part of the cytoplasm, allowing substances to dissolve and participate in metabolic reactions within the cell
 • Substances, such as urea and excess salts, are able to dissolve in water making them easier to remove from the body in urine
 • Allows substances to be transported around the body in the blood
 Which of the statements above are true?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (All of the statements) because:
 Water is known as the universal solvent for living organisms as a very large number of substances are able to dissolve in it. Those substances that are not able to dissolve in water are usually packaged in substances that can.
 • Water is the main constituent of the cytoplasm - remember this is the jelly-like solution that is enclosed within the cell membrane
 • The kidneys are responsible for filtering the blood and removing urea and excess salts by forming urine. Water plays a large role in this function
 • Blood plasma is the yellowish liquid that holds the blood cells in suspension; it is mainly water in which proteins, hormones, antibodies, soluble food molecules and ions (amongst other substances) dissolve to be transported around the body

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram below shows a palisade mesophyll cell found in the leaves of plants.
 In which region of the cell would starch be stored?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 It represents the chloroplasts which are the organelles where photosynthesis occurs. They contain chlorophyll which absorb light energy.
 A  is incorrect because this is the nucleus where genetic information is stored.
 B  is incorrect because this is the vacuole, which contains a solution of sugars and salts and helps the cell maintain its shape.
 C  is incorrect because this is the cell wall which contains the polymer cellulose which provides structural support to the cell.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: A  decrease  in which of the following factors would normally cause the transpiration rate to  increase ?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 The less humid (drier) the atmosphere, the higher the diffusion gradient between the inside of the leaf and the outside (through the stomatal pore).
 A  is incorrect because a decrease in stomatal density means less transpiration (as the leaves have fewer stomata).
 B  is incorrect because a reduction in light intensity causes stomata to close, reducing the rate of transpiration.
 C  is incorrect because a reduction in temperature means the water vapour molecules move more slowly, so they would diffuse out of the stomata at a lower rate.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: What is a feature of all catalysts?
options: A. They are made from protein
B. They are not changed by the reaction
C. They are broken down in the reaction
D. They are altered by the rate of the reaction
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.  (They are not changed by the reaction) because:
 A feature of all catalysts is that they remain  unchanged  at the end of a reaction, and can go on to catalyse subsequent reactions.
 A  is incorrect because although enzymes, as biological catalysts, are made from proteins, other catalysts not found in living organisms are not made of proteins (many metals can act as catalysts in certain chemical reactions for example).
 C  and  D  are incorrect because catalysts are not changed by the chemical reactions they speed up.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Two test tubes are set up with two similar leaves inside them, as shown in the diagram below.
 One test tube is exposed to light, while the other is kept in the dark.
   
 The test tubes are left for 4 hours.
 What colour will the hydrogencarbonate indicator solution be in each test tube?
 |  
 | dark
 | light
 |
 | A
 | purple
 | yellow
 |
 | B
 | colourless
 | yellow
 |
 | C
 | purple
 | colourless
 |
 | D
 | yellow
 | purple
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 In the presence of  low  levels of  carbon dioxide  hydrogencarbonate  indicator  changes colour from red to  purple , whereas in high levels of carbon dioxide hydrogencarbonate indicator changes colour from red to  yellow . 
 The leaf in the test tube on the left is able to  photosynthesise  as it is exposed to  light , so carbon dioxide is absorbed from the air surrounding the leaf, lowering the level of carbon dioxide so that the indicator turns  purple . Even though the plant leaf will be respiring, the rate of respiration will probably be lower than the rate of photosynthesis. 
 The leaf in the test tube on the right is not exposed to light and so will not photosynthesise (it is in the dark). However, it will  respire ,  producing carbon dioxide . Levels of carbon dioxide in the air surrounding the leaf increase, turning the indicator yellow.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: The glucose molecules formed during photosynthesis have which form of energy stored within them?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (Chemical) because:
 When glucose is made in photosynthesis, light energy is transferred to chemical potential energy in the chemical (covalent) bonds that hold the atoms in a glucose molecule together.
 A  is incorrect because light energy is essential to drive the reactions of photosynthesis (reacting carbon dioxide and water together to form glucose).
 B  is incorrect because photosynthesis is an endothermic reaction. Heat energy is released when an exothermic reaction occurs.
 D  is incorrect because mechanical energy is the sum of kinetic and potential energy in an object used to do work (a machine), not the stored energy found in glucose molecules.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram below shows the organs of the digestive system, including the alimentary canal and accessory organs.
  Where are most of the digestive lipase enzymes made in the body?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (4 only) because:
 Structure  4  is the  pancreas  which produces the majority of  lipases  involved in digestion.
 A  is incorrect because the  stomach  (2) only produces  proteases  for protein digestion.
 C  is incorrect because the  liver  (3) produces  bile  which aids lipid digestion (by emulsifying lipids to increase their surface area) but it does not produce lipases.
 D  is incorrect because the  mouth  (1) contains salivary glands which secrete  salivary   amylase  to digest carbohydrates. No lipases are made here.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The image below shows two molecules before and after chemical digestion by enzymes in the alimentary canal. 
  Which letter(s) identify the product(s) of complete starch digestion?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 The product of complete starch digestion is glucose, a simple sugar, as shown by H.  
 A  is incorrect because G represents glycerol and F represents fatty acid chains; these are the products of lipid (fat and oil) digestion.
 C  is incorrect because E represents maltose molecules. Maltose is a disaccharide made from two molecules of glucose chemically bonded together. Maltose is the product of starch digestion by amylase. 
 D  is incorrect because E is maltose and H is glucose. Only glucose is the final product of complete starch digestion.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which of the following is an effect of a cholera infection?
 • Loss of salts from the blood
 • Loss of water from the blood
 • Blockage of the small intestine
 • Persistent diarrhoea
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.  (1, 2 and 4) because:
 Blockage of the small intestine (3) is the only effect listed above not caused by a cholera infection.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram below shows a potted plant and the same plant 48 hours later.
  What has caused the plant’s appearance to change?
options: A. Water loss by translocation is greater than water uptake.
B. Water evaporating from the leaves by translocation.
C. Water loss by transpiration is greater than water uptake.
D. Water loss from the leaves by osmosis.
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • After 48 hours the leaves have  wilted , you can see them drooping in the image
 • Wilting is a sign that a plant has  insufficient water  – it has lost more water by transpiration than it has taken up and therefore water has moved out of cells, causing them to become flaccid
 A  &  B  are incorrect because translocation is the term used to describe the movement of sucrose and amino acids in the phloem.
 D  is incorrect because water loss occurs by evaporation of water from mesophyll cells inside the leaf and then diffusion of this water vapour through the stomata. Osmosis describes the movement of water between solutions separated by partially permeable membranes.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following is a correct explanation of the effect of root hairs on absorption?
options: A. Provide a large surface area, maximising the rate of absorption of water and ions by osmosis.
B. Provide a large surface area, maximising the rate of absorption of water by osmosis and ions by active transport.
C. Increase the surface area, maximising the uptake of water by osmosis and ions by diffusion.
D. Provide a surface area, increasing the rate of absorption of water and ions by active transport.
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 Root hairs are extensions of the cytoplasm of root cells, increasing the surface area to maximise the absorption of water by osmosis and ions by active transport.
 A  is incorrect because ions are transported into the roots by active transport. Osmosis only applies to the movement of water.
 C  Is incorrect because ions are transported into the roots by active transport, not diffusion.
 D  Is incorrect because there is no indication that surface area is increased in this explanation, and osmosis should be mentioned in relation to the movement of water.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The image below shows the structure of the human urinary system.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • W  is the renal artery, which is formed from one of the main branches off of the aorta, delivering blood to the kidneys
 • The body has two ureters; one connecting each kidney to the bladder, therefore represented by  Y  on the image. Ureters transport urine to the bladder
 • The urethra is the tube through which urine passes out of the bladder (and eventually the body), represented by  Z  in the image

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The image below shows a cross-section of a blood vessel taken from an arm.

 • The direction of blood flow can be determined by looking at the valves –  these are pocket valves which the blood can push through from  T to S  but if the blood flows backwards it will get trapped in the pockets of the valve, which is then forced shut

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which of the following diseases listed below are  not  caused by infectious pathogens?
 • Coronary Heart Disease
 • Cholera
 • AIDS
 • Scurvy
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.  (1 and 4) because:
 Coronary heart disease ( CHD ) and  scurvy  are lifestyle diseases not caused by pathogenic infection.
 A ,  C  and  D  are incorrect because cholera (2) is caused by the bacterium  Vibrio cholerae , and AIDS (3) is Acquired Immunodeficiency Disease which is caused by late-stage infection of the HIV virus.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram below shows a cross-section through an alveolus and a capillary.
  Why does oxygen move from P to Q?
options: A. The concentration of carbon dioxide is lower in the alveolus than in the blood.
B. The concentration of oxygen in the blood is lower than in the air in the capillary.
C. Oxygen must replace carbon dioxide.
D. The concentration of oxygen in the blood is lower than the air in the alveolus.
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.  (The concentration of oxygen in the blood is lower than the air in the alveolus) because:
 Blood is deoxygenated when it enters the lung capillaries, therefore there is an oxygen concentration gradient between P and Q. There is a  higher   concentration of oxygen in the air in the alveolus than in the   blood , leading to  diffusion  of oxygen into the blood.
 A  is incorrect because the movement of oxygen is not affected by the concentration gradient for carbon dioxide
 B  is incorrect because there is no air in the capillary; the air is in the alveolus.
 C  is incorrect because the movement of each gas (carbon dioxide and oxygen) is dependent on the concentration gradient of each individual gas, not on the concentration of the other gas.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram below shows an experiment set up by a teacher to demonstrate how an investigation into anaerobic respiration in yeast cells can be carried out.
  Predict what would happen to the coloured liquid in the glass tube.
options: C. Moves rapidly to the right
D. Moves slowly to the right
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (moves to the left) because:
 As the yeast respires anaerobically, it produces carbon dioxide gas which would be released into the tube, increasing the pressure inside the tube and pushing the drop of coloured liquid to the left.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which organ is involved in the metabolic breakdown of oral medication?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (liver) because:
 The liver is the primary site for drug metabolism.
 A  is incorrect because although the stomach is involved in the digestion of some oral medications it does not fully metabolise the drug.
 C  and  D  are incorrect because the brain and kidneys are not the primary sites of drug metabolism.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A group of students set up an experiment to investigate growth responses in plants. 
 In one of the experiments, they placed a plant shoot in a box with a small window allowing light to fall on one side of the shoot only.
 Which of the following options correctly describes and explains what happened in the student’s experiment?
 |  
 | response
 | cause
 | effect
 |
 | A
 | positive phototropism
 | more auxin on side of shoot exposed to light
 | slower growth on shaded side of shoot
 |
 | B
 | positive phototropism
 | more auxin on shaded side of shoot
 | slower growth on side of shoot exposed to light
 |
 | C
 | negative gravitropism
 | even distribution of auxins
 | equal rates of growth
 |
 | D
 | positive phototropism
 | less auxin on shaded side of shoot
 | faster growth on side of shoot exposed to light
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • We can divide the shoot into two halves; the side in the light and the side in the shade. Auxins accumulate on the shaded side of a shoot strongly exposed to light from one direction (in this case through the window of a box)
 • In the shoots, auxin promotes cell growth and elongation; if the shaded side has more auxin than the side exposed to the light then it will grow at a faster rate and the shoot exhibits positive phototropism, growing towards the light source
 A  is incorrect because auxin would accumulate on the shaded side (as auxins diffuse away from light) and the shaded side would grow at a faster rate.
 C  is incorrect because although shoots do show negative gravitropism, this factor does not impact the shoots growth response to light. Auxins are strongly affected by light so would not be evenly distributed and there would not therefore be even growth.
 D  is incorrect because there would be more auxin on the shaded side of the shoot a

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The image below shows a simple reflex arc. 
  Which of the following sequences correctly shows the order of cells that an impulse passes through during a reflex action? 
 |  
 | first  →  last
 |
 | A
 | Z   →    X   →    Y 
 |
 | B
 | X   →   Y    →   Z
 |
 | C
 | Y  →     X   →    Z
 |
 | D
 | Z   →    Y   →    X
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • Receptor cells are found in sense organs. They pick up on the stimulus which generates an electrical impulse that is then sent along a sensory neurone (Z) to the coordinator (the brain or spinal cord)
 • The impulse is then passed to a relay neurone (X) which is a short neurone found inside the coordinator and connects sensory neurones to motor neurones
 • The impulse is then passed on to a motor neurone (Y) which connects to an effector, in this case a muscle, stimulating it to contract and bring about a response
 B  is incorrect because a reflex action cannot start with the relay neurone (X).
 C  is incorrect because the order of neurones is back-to-front from effector (muscle) to receptor, only effectors can carry out a response when signalled by an impulse from a motor neurone (Y) which requires impulses originating from the receptor.
 D  is incorrect because impulses pass along neurones in sequential order, an impulse cannot jump from a sensor

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following is the correct word equation for aerobic respiration in plants?
options: A. glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water
B. carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen
C. glucose + water → carbon dioxide + oxygen
D. glucose + carbon dioxide → water + oxygen
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  (glucose + oxygen →  carbon dioxide + water) because:
 • Plants, like all living organisms, respire to release energy (not shown in the above equations), therefore the process of aerobic respiration is the same in plants as it is in other organisms
 • Plants also photosynthesise, but only when conditions allow it to (such as when light is available and the temperature is appropriate)
 B  is incorrect because this is the equation for photosynthesis in plants. Photosynthesis is not the reverse reaction of respiration, although the reactants and products are the opposite way around in each reaction.  
 C  and  D  are incorrect because the reactants and products have been mixed up.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which description of the liver below is correct?
options: A. The liver is a cell, containing several tissues, which forms part of the digestive system.
B. The liver is an organ, containing several systems, which forms part of the digestive tissue
C. The liver is an organ, containing several tissues, which forms part of the digestive system.
D. The liver is a cell, containing several systems, which forms part of the digestive system.
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (The liver is an organ, containing several tissues, which forms part of the digestive system) because:
 The  liver  is an organ composed of several different tissue types. It plays a vital role in digestion by producing bile which neutralises acidic gastric juice from the stomach.
 • An  organ  is a structure made up of a group of tissues working together to perform a specific function
 • A  tissue  is a group of cells with similar structures working together to perform a shared function
 • An  organ   system  is a group of organs with related functions working together to perform body functions
 The other answers are incorrect because they do not correctly define what the liver is.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Some amphibians, such as frogs, can use their skin as a gas exchange surface.
 What are the most likely characteristics of the surface of the skin in these amphibians?
 |  
 | surface area
 | type of skin
 |
 | A
 | small
 | thick
 |
 | B
 | large
 | thick
 |
 | C
 | small
 | thin
 |
 | D
 | large
 | thin
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 This is because gas exchange surface have the following requirements:
 • A  large surface area  so that as much diffusion as possible can happen in the shortest amount of time
 • They are  thin  (normally only one cell thick), so that  diffusion distances are short
 A ,  B  and  C  are incorrect because thick skin would increase the distance over which gases had to be exchanged, reducing the rate of diffusion. A smaller surface area would provide less area for diffusion to occur. 
 To maximise diffusion efficiency gas exchange surfaces must also:
 • be able to  maintain a diffusion gradient  so that diffusion continually happens
 • be able to maintain a good supply of air containing oxygen

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Compared to the composition of atmospheric air, the air exhaled by a man contains:
options: A. more water vapour, more carbon dioxide.
B. more water vapour, less carbon dioxide.
C. less water vapour, more carbon dioxide.
D. less water vapour, less carbon dioxide.
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A.  (more water vapour, more carbon dioxide) because: 
 • Carbon dioxide  and  water  are products of  respiration  in cells which are transferred to the blood (due to diffusion / osmosis). Both can be  excreted  from the body by the lungs when we breathe out
 • This means that air exhaled by a human will contain more water vapour and more carbon dioxide than atmospheric air

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which of the following is a reason yeast is used to make bread?
 Yeast is used to make bread because...
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (it produces carbon dioxide) because:
 Yeast  produces carbon dioxide and ethanol (alcohol) during fermentation, and it is bubbles of carbon dioxide gas that makes the bread rise as it gets trapped in the dough.
 A  is incorrect because while yeast fermentation does result in the production of  ethanol , it is the production of the  carbon dioxide  that makes the bread rise.
 B  is incorrect because  lactic acid  is a product of  anaerobic  respiration in  animals  and some bacteria.
 D  is incorrect because fermentation is  anaerobic , meaning that it doesn’t require oxygen, and as a type of respiration does not produce oxygen. The process that produces oxygen is  photosynthesis  in plants and algae.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The graph below shows the results of an investigation into how the rate of respiration of an organism is affected by changing the temperature.
  Which of the following statements would explain the difference between the rate of respiration at 10 °C and that at 30 °C?
options: A. Enzyme activity is higher at 30 °C because more frequent collisions are occurring than at 10 °C.
B. Enzyme activity at 30 °C is lower because the bonds holding an enzyme together are altered at higher temperatures.
C. Enzyme activity is at its optimum at 30 °C, meaning the rate is at its highest.
D. Enzyme activity is lower at 10 °C because the enzymes are denatured and therefore unable to bind to their substrates.
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  (enzyme activity is higher at 30 °C because more frequent collisions are occurring than at 10 °C) because:
 Increasing the temperature of an enzyme to its optimum increases the rate of the chemical reaction it catalyses as enzymes and substrates will have more kinetic energy and therefore will collide successfully more often.
 B  is incorrect because the graph shows the rate of the enzyme’s activity increasing up to 40°C, so the bonds holding the structure together cannot have been altered.
 C  is incorrect because the optimum for the enzyme is somewhere between 30°C and 50°C.
 D  is incorrect because enzymes are denatured at temperatures above their optimum, not at low temperatures.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Fruit flies can have orange or red eyes.
 If two orange flies are crossed, all of the offspring will have orange eyes.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:

 • Dominant characteristics will show even if a recessive allele is present in the genotype (for example in an heterozygous individual)
 • Organisms that are orange-eyed must be recessive as when crossed offspring always have orange-eyes
 • In order for there to be a mixture of red and orange-eyed individuals the red-eyed flies must have been heterozygous

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
When growing millet, farmers choose seeds from high-yielding plants.
 Which of the following is this an example of?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (artificial selection) because:
 • Selecting plants for their desirable characteristics is  selective breeding
 • This is an example of  artificial selection  carried out by humans
 A  is incorrect because  evolution  is the change in adaptive features of a population over time as the result of  natural selection.
 B  is incorrect because  adaptations  are an inherited feature that helps an organism to survive and reproduce in its environment.
 D  is incorrect because  natural selection  is the process by which organisms best suited to their environment (better adapted) are more likely to survive and reproduce.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of these two gases both contribute to climate change?
options: D. Carbon dioxide and sulfur dioxide
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (carbon dioxide and methane) because:
 The two main gases that cause climate change are  carbon dioxide and methane.  Increasing amounts of carbon dioxide are being released by combustion, with reduced amounts removed by trees for photosynthesis as a result of deforestation. Methane is released by industrial processes as well as farming.
 A  is incorrect because oxygen is not a greenhouse gas.
 B  and  D  are incorrect because sulfur dioxide causes acid rain, this doesn’t contribute to climate change.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following is an example of a community?
options: All the populations of all species in a forest.
B. All the goldfish in a pond.
C. All the wheat and corn in a field.
D. All the plants in a forest.
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  (all the populations of all species in a forest) because:
 The definition of a community is all of the populations of all of the different species in a habitat.
 B  is incorrect because this answer refers to one species, all the goldfish in a pond.
 C  is incorrect because this refers to only two species. There will be more than two species in that habitat.
 D  is incorrect because this answer only refers to the producers in the forest and doesn’t consider all the populations within that habitat.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: What is the name of the enzyme used to produce clear apple juice?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  (pectinase) because:
 Pectin  is found in fruit juices. It is a  polysaccharide  that is responsible for holding cells together, but it makes fruit juice cloudy.  Pectinase  is the enzyme that breaks down  pectin  so that the juice is clear.
 A  is incorrect because  lipase  breaks down lipids into fatty acids and glycerol.
 B  is incorrect because  amylase  breaks down starch into  maltose .
 C  is incorrect because  protease  breaks down proteins into  amino acids.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The following statements refer to plastic pollution.
 • Animals will often try to eat the plastic or become entangled in it
 • It breaks down into micro particles that wash away into nearby rivers
 • As plastic breaks down, it releases toxins into the surrounding environment
 • It enters the food chain when filter feeders such as mussels ingest micro particles
 Which of these statements applies to both marine and terrestrial (land) habitats?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (1 and 3 only) because:
 Statements 1 and 3 can apply to both marine and terrestrial habitats. Animals on land and in the ocean may mistake plastic pollution for food and try to eat it, while many others may become entangled in discarded plastic packaging. Plastic will release toxins into both marine and terrestrial habitats as it breaks down, much to the detriment of the organisms that live there.
 A  is incorrect because statement 2 will mainly apply to marine environments. While plastic may break down on land, the tiny particles that wash away into rivers will end up doing the most damage in marine habitats.
 B  is incorrect because both statements 2 and 4 will apply to marine habitats. The clue in statement 4 is the mention of mussels, which lives in the ocean.
 D  is incorrect because statement 1 can also apply to both marine and terrestrial habitats.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which class of vertebrate typically gives birth to live young?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  (mammals) because:
 Mammals are generally the only group of vertebrates to give birth to live young.
 B, C  and  D  are all incorrect because all other vertebrate classes tend to lay eggs.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The image below shows two solutions separated by a partially permeable membrane.
  Which of the statements below would be true in relation to the image?
options: A. There is no net movement of water from W to X
B. There would be movement of water molecules from W to X
C. Osmosis of sugar molecules would occur from the dilute solution (W) to the concentrated solution (X)
D. Solution X is more dilute and therefore has a higher water potential than solution W
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (There would be movement of water molecules from W to X) because:
 • Osmosis is the  net  movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential (dilute solution) to a region of lower water potential (concentrated solution), through a partially permeable membrane
 • Net movement’ means ‘overall movement’ -  more  water molecules will move from solution W to solution X, but water molecules are able to move in either direction (they don’t choose to move from one solution to another, because they can’t tell if the solution they’re in is dilute or concentrated)
 A  is incorrect because the net movement of water would be from W (dilute solution) to X (concentrated solution).
 C  is incorrect because osmosis only refers to the movement of water molecules, not sugar molecules.
 D  is incorrect because solution X is more concentrated than W since there are more sugar molecules and less free water molecules in X.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Four statements about large biological molecules are given below: 
 • Proteins are made from a number of different amino acids.
 • Both glycogen and starch are made from simple sugar base units.
 • Fats are made from glycerol and fatty acids.
 • Oils are made from glycerol only. 
 Which of the four statements above is/are  false ?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 The question asks which of the statements given is  false . Statements 1, 2 and 3 are all true.
 Statement 4 is false because oils (like fats, a type of lipid) are made from glycerol and fatty acids. 
 Around 20 different amino acids are used to build protein molecules in almost all living cells. The basic structure of each amino acid is largely the same, with one variable region differing to produce a variety of amino acids. Glycogen and starch, as well as cellulose, are all polymers of glucose.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram below shows part of an organism (ciliated epithelium). 
  What term would correctly describe the level of organisation of the structure in the diagram above?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  (cell) because:
 The image shows a ciliated epithelial cell. These cells can be found lining the trachea and parts of the lungs. Cells are the basic functional units of all living organisms on Earth. 
 B  is incorrect because organelle is a term used to describe subcellular structures within cells, such as mitochondria and chloroplasts.
 C  is incorrect because an organ is formed from two or more tissues working together. Tissues are made from groups of similar cells.
 D  is incorrect because an organ system is made from organs working together to perform a particular function.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:

 6 molecules of carbon dioxide react with 6 molecules of water to form 1 molecule of glucose and 6 molecules of oxygen.

 B  is incorrect because this option has 1 molecule of carbon dioxide reacting with 6 molecules of water to form 1 molecule of glucose and 6 molecules of oxygen which is not balanced.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: A  decrease  in which of the following factors would normally cause the transpiration rate to  increase ?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 The less humid (drier) the atmosphere, the higher the diffusion gradient between the inside of the leaf and the outside (through the stomatal pore).
 A  is incorrect because a decrease in stomatal density means less transpiration (as the leaves have fewer stomata).
 B  is incorrect because a reduction in light intensity causes stomata to close, reducing the rate of transpiration.
 C  is incorrect because a reduction in temperature means the water vapour molecules move more slowly, so they would diffuse out of the stomata at a lower rate.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: What is a feature of all catalysts?
options: A. They are made from protein
B. They are not changed by the reaction
C. They are broken down in the reaction
D. They are altered by the rate of the reaction
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.  (They are not changed by the reaction) because:
 A feature of all catalysts is that they remain  unchanged  at the end of a reaction, and can go on to catalyse subsequent reactions.
 A  is incorrect because although enzymes, as biological catalysts, are made from proteins, other catalysts not found in living organisms are not made of proteins (many metals can act as catalysts in certain chemical reactions for example).
 C  and  D  are incorrect because catalysts are not changed by the chemical reactions they speed up.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which environmental factor is most likely to be responsible for a plant to wilt?
options: C. A decrease in the amount of available water.
D. A decrease in wind speed.
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 If a plant does not get enough water, it becomes limp and wilts. This is because water has left the cells and they have become flaccid, providing less support to the overall structure of the leaf. If a cell does not contain enough water there is no pressure pushing outwards against the cell wall and the cells will all shrink a little.
 A  is incorrect because a decrease in light intensity would just reduce the rate of photosynthesis, not cause the plant to wilt.
 B  is incorrect because an increase in humidity would reduce transpiration from the plant, meaning it would retain more water.
 D  is incorrect because a decrease in wind speed would reduce transpiration from the plant, meaning it would retain more water.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:

 A  is incorrect because G represents glycerol and F represents fatty acid chains; these are the products of lipid (fat and oil) digestion.
 C  is incorrect because E represents maltose molecules. Maltose is a disaccharide made from two molecules of glucose chemically bonded together. Maltose is the product of starch digestion by amylase.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
What happens when a person is vaccinated against measles? 
 |  
 | type of immunity
 | production of memory cells?

 | yes

 | passive
 | no
 |
 | C
 | active
 | yes
 |

 | active

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Active immunity is  acquired  when a person makes their own  antibodies  and  memory   cells  that protect against a pathogen. Memory cells can last in the body for years. Remember  lymphocytes  are the white blood cells that make antibodies, and some of these develop into memory cells
 • You can develop  active immunity  by having a  disease  and getting over it, or by being  vaccinated  with weakened pathogens
 A  and  B  are incorrect because passive immunity only develops when a person is given antibodies from someone else.
 D  is incorrect because memory cells are produced as a result of vaccination meaning that if you’re infected with the pathogen in future, your body can make antibodies against that pathogen before it has a chance to make you sick.

 • During  exhalation  the  volume  of the thorax needs to get  smaller  so that  pressure  inside will  increase  relative to the pressure of atmospheric air, forcing air out of the lungs. This means that the ribs must move down, contraction of the internal intercostal muscles aids this process

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
During vigorous exercise, such as cycling uphill, lactic acid builds up in the muscles.
 How is this lactic acid removed during recovery?
options: A. excretion of lactic acid by the kidneys
B. anaerobic respiration of lactic acid in the muscles
C. aerobic respiration of lactic acid in the liver
D. excretion of lactic acid by the lungs
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (aerobic respiration of lactic acid in the liver) because:
 • Lactic acid builds up in skeletal muscle cells during vigorous exercise
 • It is mainly excreted into the blood, and when the blood passes through the liver lactic acid is taken up by liver cells where it reacts with oxygen, forming carbon dioxide and water (and releasing energy)
 • As lactic acid is therefore being broken down with oxygen (and energy is being released), this is an example of aerobic respiration
 A  is incorrect because the kidneys can also break down lactic acid (using oxygen to form carbon dioxide and water) but they do not excrete lactic acid.
 B  is incorrect because anaerobic respiration in the muscles produces lactic acid.
 D  is incorrect because lactic acid is not excreted by the lungs (the carbon dioxide produced in aerobic respiration is).

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Which of the following diseases listed below are  not  caused by infectious pathogens? 
 • Coronary Heart Disease
 • Cholera
 • AIDS
 • Scurvy
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.  (1 and 4) because:
 Coronary heart disease ( CHD ) and  scurvy  are lifestyle diseases not caused by pathogenic infection.
 A ,  C  and  D  are incorrect because cholera (2) is caused by the bacterium  Vibrio cholerae , and AIDS (3) is Acquired Immunodeficiency Disease which is caused by late-stage infection of the HIV virus.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Four statements are given below. 
 • Neurotransmitters are released from vesicles.
 • An impulse is generated in the postsynaptic neurone.
 • An impulse arrives at the end of a neurone.
 • Neurotransmitters diffuse across the synaptic cleft.
 Which of the following options correctly describes the sequence of events that occurs at a synapse?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • See the key concept link for the series of events that occur when an impulse arrives at the end of a neurone
 • D  is the only possible correct answer as the other three options begin with either the neurotransmitter being released (before an impulse has arrived at the end of the presynaptic neurone) or with an impulse in the postsynaptic neurone
 • Remember that ‘pre’ means before and ‘post’ means after

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of the following gives the most accurate definition of a drug?
options: B. A substance taken into the body that modifies or affects chemical reactions.
C. A plant extract that kills bacteria.
D. A substance that produces side effects as well as therapeutic effects.
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (a substance taken into the body that modifies or affects chemical reactions) because:
 Drugs always have their effect at a chemical level, by affecting chemical reactions in cells, tissues and organs. 
 A  is incorrect because not all drugs are addictive or harmful; many have beneficial effects, though most would be harmful if taken at an excessive level (an 'overdose').
 C  is incorrect because not all drugs are plant extracts (some come from fungi and some are manufactured in a laboratory), and not all of them kill bacteria. 
 D  is incorrect because not all drugs produce side effects, though many do.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The table below shows some advantages and disadvantages of sexual and asexual reproduction.
 Which row is correct?
 |  
 | advantages of sexual reproduction
 | advantage of asexual reproduction
 |
 | A
 | less population growth
 | only one parent needed
 |
 | B
 | more energy efficient
 | gametes can be transferred by the environment
 |
 | C
 | no transfer of gametes
 | does not compete with parent for nutrients
 |
 | D
 | more genetic variation
 | faster
 |
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • More  genetic variation  within a population / species means that the population / species is more likely to survive any changes in the environment due to  natural selection . They may also be able to survive moving to new environments
 • Asexual reproduction  is faster as it only involves one parent, there is no need to find a suitable partner for reproduction
 A  is incorrect because while only one parent needed is an advantage of asexual reproduction, less population growth is not an advantage of sexual reproduction.
 B  and  C  are incorrect because none of these statements are scientifically correct.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The image below shows a simple reflex arc. 
  Which of the following sequences correctly shows the order of cells that an impulse passes through during a reflex action? 
 |  
 | first  →  last
 |
 | A
 | Z   →    X   →    Y 
 |
 | B
 | X   →   Y    →   Z
 |
 | C
 | Y  →     X   →    Z
 |
 | D
 | Z   →    Y   →    X
 |
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • Receptor cells are found in sense organs. They pick up on the stimulus which generates an electrical impulse that is then sent along a sensory neurone (Z) to the coordinator (the brain or spinal cord)
 • The impulse is then passed to a relay neurone (X) which is a short neurone found inside the coordinator and connects sensory neurones to motor neurones
 • The impulse is then passed on to a motor neurone (Y) which connects to an effector, in this case a muscle, stimulating it to contract and bring about a response
 B  is incorrect because a reflex action cannot start with the relay neurone (X).
 C  is incorrect because the order of neurones is back-to-front from effector (muscle) to receptor, only effectors can carry out a response when signalled by an impulse from a motor neurone (Y) which requires impulses originating from the receptor.
 D  is incorrect because impulses pass along neurones in sequential order, an impulse cannot jump from a sensor

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram shows the inheritance of ABO blood groups in the family. 
  What could be Jignasha’s genotype?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  (I B I O ) because:
 • Blood group inheritance is an example of  codominance
 • There are three possible alleles for the blood group (but remember a person can inherit a maximum of two alleles per gene)
 • Alleles I A  and I B   are dominant groups over I O
 • Jignasha has two children with a man who has the A blood group phenotype
 • Jignasha’s son is blood group B, meaning that Jignasha must have at least one I B  allele, as the son's father would not have this allele (the father must be I A I O )
 • Jignasha’s daughter’s genotype is not shown, but she has one daughter who is blood type O and one who is blood type A. The child who is blood group O must be I O I O  so the allele for I O  must have come from Jignasha making her I B I O
 It is very important to read and make use of all the information in the question, for example to realise that Jignasha is a female.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Some amphibians, such as frogs, can use their skin as a gas exchange surface. 
 What are the most likely characteristics of the surface of the skin in these amphibians?
 |  
 | surface area
 | type of skin
 |
 | A
 | small
 | thick
 |
 | B
 | large
 | thick
 |
 | C
 | small
 | thin
 |
 | D
 | large
 | thin
 |
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 This is because gas exchange surface have the following requirements:
 • A  large surface area  so that as much diffusion as possible can happen in the shortest amount of time
 • They are  thin  (normally only one cell thick), so that  diffusion distances are short
 A ,  B  and  C  are incorrect because thick skin would increase the distance over which gases had to be exchanged, reducing the rate of diffusion. A smaller surface area would provide less area for diffusion to occur. 
 To maximise diffusion efficiency gas exchange surfaces must also:
 • be able to  maintain a diffusion gradient  so that diffusion continually happens
 • be able to maintain a good supply of air containing oxygen

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram below shows the process of sexual reproduction. 
  Which of the processes are shown by stages  Q  and  R ?
 |  
 | Q
 | R
 |
 | A
 | meiosis
 | mitosis
 |
 | B
 | mitosis
 | mitosis
 |
 | C
 | meiosis
 | meiosis
 |
 | D
 | mitosis
 | meiosis
 |
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • The production of  gametes  involves meiosis
 • Meiosis results in the production of cells with a  haploid number  of chromosomes and with genetic variation (the daughter cells contain a unique combination of alleles compared to the parent cell)
 • Mitosis  produces genetically identical cells with a  diploid number  of chromosomes. This is used for  somatic  (body cell) division in growth and repair; so once the  gametes  have fused to form a  zygote  mitotic cell divisions allow the zygote to form an embryo and then a foetus
 The other answers are incorrect as they have not identified the correct stage for mitosis and meiosis.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A woman who has blood group A and a man who has blood group B have four children, each with a different blood group A, B, AB and O. 
 What variation does this show?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  (Discontinuous and genetic only) because:
 • Blood groups are controlled by a  genetic variation
 • This is an example of  discontinuous variation , there are distinct groups
 • These differences are due to differences in the  genetic code
 B  and  C  are incorrect because the blood group characteristic is not an example of  continuous variation,  there are only four possible blood groups with no intermediates in between.
 D  is incorrect because  discontinuous variation  is only under the influence of genetic factors, the environment doesn’t influence the phenotype.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of the following is  not  a feature of natural selection?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  (selection by humans) because:
 • Within populations there will always be  variation
 • Natural selection is the ‘favouring’ of a characteristic giving an individual a survival advantage over others: individuals with these characteristics are better adapted to the  environment  (remember the environment determines what is ‘favoured’ or ‘selected’) and therefore these individuals are more likely to  survive  and  reproduce
 • Variation increases the capability of a  population  to survive and cope with environmental change
 • Artificial selection  is carried out by humans selecting specific traits and deciding which individuals in a population (of livestock animals or plant crops) are able to breed. This is not a feature of natural selection
 All the other answers are incorrect because they are features of natural selection:
 • Production of a large number of offspring will mean that there will be a larger range of phenotypes from the inheritance of random muta

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram below shows part of the nitrogen cycle. 
  Which letter would represent denitrification?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 The process of denitrification removes nitrates from the soil, releasing it back into the atmosphere as nitrogen gas. This process occurs naturally by denitrifying bacteria in the soil, and it reduces soil fertility.
 A  is incorrect because this arrow shows decomposition of animals into ammonium compounds.
 B  is incorrect because this arrow refers to nitrification which is carried out by nitrifying bacteria.
 D  is incorrect because this arrow depicts nitrogen fixation by bacteria in root nodules and lightning.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
When growing millet, farmers choose seeds from high-yielding plants.
 Which of the following is this an example of?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (artificial selection) because:
 • Selecting plants for their desirable characteristics is  selective breeding
 • This is an example of  artificial selection  carried out by humans
 A  is incorrect because  evolution  is the change in adaptive features of a population over time as the result of  natural selection.
 B  is incorrect because  adaptations  are an inherited feature that helps an organism to survive and reproduce in its environment.
 D  is incorrect because  natural selection  is the process by which organisms best suited to their environment (better adapted) are more likely to survive and reproduce.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of these two gases both contribute to climate change?
options: D. Carbon dioxide and sulfur dioxide
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (carbon dioxide and methane) because:
 The two main gases that cause climate change are  carbon dioxide and methane.  Increasing amounts of carbon dioxide are being released by combustion, with reduced amounts removed by trees for photosynthesis as a result of deforestation. Methane is released by industrial processes as well as farming.
 A  is incorrect because oxygen is not a greenhouse gas.
 B  and  D  are incorrect because sulfur dioxide causes acid rain, this doesn’t contribute to climate change.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Rapid growth of algae on the surface of the water can occur as a result of nitrates entering a reservoir of water. 
 This causes the following changes in the reservoir:
 • An increase in aerobic respiration by decomposers.
 • A decrease in the concentration of dissolved oxygen in the water.
 • Fish and other aquatic animals die.
 • Producers die and decomposition increases.
 In which order do these changes occur?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  (4 → 1 → 2 → 3) because:
 • The first step in eutrophication is the blocking of the light to producers from the algae
 • This will cause the producers to die and as a result decomposer numbers will increase, increasing the rate of aerobic respiration occurring in the water
 • The reduced level of oxygen as a result of increased aerobic respiration will cause other organisms to die
 Nitrates will encourage rapid and dense growth of algae already present in the water, only answers  C  and  D  could possibly be correct as these are the only answers that start with the death of the producers due to the lack of light.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of these is  not  a correct use of genetic modification?
options: D. To modify crops to provide additional vitamins
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  (cloning) because:
 Cloning  is a process which aims to make an identical copy of the original organism being cloned. Within cloning there is no  genetic modification  of the organism.
 B ,  C  and  D  are incorrect because these are the uses and advantages of genetic modification of organisms.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: What is the name of the enzyme used to produce clear apple juice?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  (pectinase) because:
 Pectin  is found in fruit juices. It is a  polysaccharide  that is responsible for holding cells together, but it makes fruit juice cloudy.  Pectinase  is the enzyme that breaks down  pectin  so that the juice is clear.
 A  is incorrect because  lipase  breaks down lipids into fatty acids and glycerol.
 B  is incorrect because  amylase  breaks down starch into  maltose .
 C  is incorrect because  protease  breaks down proteins into  amino acids.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The graph shows how the world population of humans has increased from 1650 until the year 2000. 
  Which stage in this sigmoidal population curve is shown by point X?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 The exponential (log) phase in a population growth curve is when there is rapid growth of a population. 
 A  is incorrect because the stationary phase on the graph would show neither an increase nor a decrease in numbers in the population.
 B  is incorrect because the lag phase is when the population is growing slowly and adjusting to new conditions.
 D  is incorrect because the death phase on a graph would show the decline of the population with the line decreasing. This is not yet seen in the human population.

set-6/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:

 (i)
 State the two groups of flowering plants.
 [1]
 (ii)
 Explain how to distinguish between the two groups.
 [3]
set-6/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
(i) The two groups of flowering plants are...
 • Monocotyledons  and  dicotyledons;  [1 mark]
 Answer can be in either order
 (ii) To distinguish between the two groups...
 Any  three  of the following from:
 • Flowers from monocotyledons contain petals in multiples of 3;  [1 mark]
 • Flowers from dicotyledons contain petals in multiples of 4 or 5;  [1 mark]
 • Leaves from monocotyledons have parallel leaf veins;  [1 mark]
 • Leaves from dicotyledons have reticulated/branched leaf veins;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 4 marks]

set-6/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
Fig. 1 illustrates the results of two enzyme-controlled reactions involving two different types of enzyme.
  Fig. 1
 From these reactions, determine what conclusion can be drawn about the function of enzymes.
set-6/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
The conclusion that can be drawn about the function of enzymes is...
 • Enzymes can break down/degrade molecules;  [1 mark]
 • Enzymes can build-up/synthesise molecules;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 2 marks]
 It is important to remember that enzymes can either put substrates together to build up molecules (anabolism) or they can break down substrates to break molecules into smaller/simpler molecules (catabolism). You would not be awarded any marks if you had just said that enzymes can make DNA or nucleotides, this was just used as an example.

set-6/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
Fig. 1 shows a photomicrograph of a section of a root.
  Fig. 1
 Structure  J  is a xylem vessel.
 The xylem vessels conduct water from the roots to the stems.
 State the features of xylem vessels that enable them to conduct water.
set-6/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
The features of xylem vessels that enable them to conduct water are:
 Any  three  from the following:
 • (Xylem vessels contains) no cytoplasm / (named organelle) / they are hollow;  [1 mark]
 • (They have) lignin (in their walls);  [1 mark]
 • (The cell walls) are waterproof / water impermeable / does not allow water through;  [1 mark]
 • (There is secondary) thickening of the cell wall;  [1 mark]
 • (Xylem consists of) long / elongated (cells / vessels / tubes);  [1 mark]
 • (The vessels have bordered) pits (for water movement between vessels);  [1 mark]
 • (There are) no end / cross walls (between cells) / end plates to connect vessels (end to end);  [1 mark]

set-6/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
Organ 1 is…

 • (The diaphragm) relaxes and moves up/becomes dome-shaped;  [1 mark]

set-6/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
The kidneys excrete excess water in urine.
 The main component of urine is water.
 State  two  other substances that are excreted by healthy kidneys.
set-6/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
Two  other substances that are excreted by healthy kidneys are:
 Any  two  from the following:
 • Urea;  [1 mark]
 • Salt(s) / (named) ions / (named) minerals;  [1 mark]
 • Any other valid and correct substance e.g. hormones;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 2 marks]
 Make sure you read all the question information carefully; it can be tempting to put water here as part of your answer but this has already been included for you in the question.

set-6/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
Some animals are farmed intensively.
 Describe the negative impacts to an ecosystem of intensive livestock production.
set-6/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
The negative impacts to an ecosystem of intensive livestock production are:
 Any  four  from the following:
 • Habitat loss / deforestation;  [1 mark]
 • Loss of biodiversity / extinction (of species);  [1 mark]
 • Death of (wild) organisms / disruption of food web;  [1 mark]
 • Enhanced greenhouse effect / global warming;  [1 mark]
 • More carbon dioxide / methane;  [1 mark]
 • Pollution from urine / faeces;  [1 mark]
 • Pollution from farm machinery;  [1 mark]
 • Disease spreads (to wild populations);  [1 mark]
 • Ref. to antibiotic resistance / inappropriate use of antibiotics;  [1 mark]
 Allow references to reductions in animal welfare. 
 [Total: 4 marks]
 The most common error in this question is to describe the effects of intensive  arable  farming, when the question only requires you to focus on intensive  livestock  farming. Careful reading of the question will avert this error.

  Fig.1

 Care was taken to avoid petroleum jelly getting onto the cut end of the shoot.
  Fig. 2
 (i)
 Suggest why a species with a thin waxy cuticle was chosen for this experiment.
 [2]
 (ii)
 Explain why the shoot with ten leaves was cut from the branch under water and not in air. 
 [2]
 (iii)
 Explain the purpose of petroleum jelly being smeared on the areas shown in Fig. 2.
 [1]
 (iv)
 Explain why the students should avoid petroleum jelly getting onto the cut end of the shoot as shown in Fig. 2.
 [2]
set-6/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.explanation:
(i) A species with a thin waxy cuticle was chosen for this experiment because:
 • (Thin waxy cuticle) will lose water / transpire / evaporate water more quickly (than a thick cuticle);  [1 mark]
 • (So) will produce a measurable result in quicker time / it will be easier to measure its transpiration rate;  [1 mark]
 (ii) The shoot with ten leaves was cut from the branch under water and not in air because:

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which characteristic allows an organism to detect or sense stimuli in the internal or external environment and to make appropriate responses?
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is C.
 • Sensitivity is the ability of an organism to detect or sense stimuli in its internal or external environment and to make appropriate responses
 A  is incorrect as movement is an action by an organism or part of an organism causing a change of position or place.
 B  is incorrect as excretion is the removal of toxic material, waste products of metabolism and substances in excess from an organism.
 D  is incorrect as nutrition is the taking in of materials for energy, growth and development.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A hare and a rabbit are unable to reproduce to produce fertile offspring. 
 Which statement explains why?
options: B. they belong to different kingdoms
D. their DNA base sequences are different
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is A.
 • Hares and rabbits belong to different species, meaning that they cannot interbreed to produce fertile offspring.
 B  is incorrect as both hares and rabbits belong to the animal kingdom, so this cannot explain why they are unable to interbreed.
 C  is incorrect as living in different habitats does not prevent two organisms from interbreeding to produce fertile offspring.
 D  is incorrect as all organisms have different DNA base sequences to one another, including members of the same species, so this alone cannot explain why hares and rabbits are unable to interbreed.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram below shows a bacteria cell
  What is the function of structure Z?
options: B. absorbs light energy for photosynthesis
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is D.
 • Z = a plasmid; a ring of DNA in the cytoplasm which is separate from the main circular chromosome (labelled Y)
 A  is incorrect as bacterial cells do not contain membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria.
 B  is incorrect as chloroplasts are another example of membrane-bound organelles.
 C  is incorrect as, although bacterial cells do have a cell wall, Z is not pointing towards the cell wall.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The micrograph below shows onion root cells undergoing various stages of mitosis. A x200 magnification was used.
  Nathalie Russell via  Wikimedia Commons
 Which of the following shows the the real length of the cell indicated in the image, rounded to the nearest whole number?
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is C.
 • Convert the image size from cm to mm
 • 1 cm = 10 mm
 1.73 x 10 = 17.3
 • Convert from mm to µm
 • 1 mm = 1000 µm 
 17.3 x 1000 = 17 300
 • Note the magnification equation:
 
 • Rearrange the equation to give actual size:

  A  is incorrect as it results from converting mm to micrometres by multiplying by 100 instead of 1000, giving 8.65 μm which rounds to 9 μm.

 D  is incorrect as 86.5 μm rounded to the nearest whole number is 87, not 86.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A plant cell is placed in a concentrated salt solution. 
 Which of the following correctly describes the events that occur after this?
options: A. Water molecules will move out of the plant cell via osmosis into the salt solution. Eventually the cell will become plasmolysed.
B. Water molecules will move out of the plant cell via active transport into the salt solution. Eventually the cell will plasmolyse.
C. Water molecules will move into the plant cell via osmosis from the salt solution. Eventually the cell will become turgid.
D. Water molecules will move out of the plant cell via osmosis into the salt solution. Eventually the cell will become flaccid.
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is A.
 • The concentrated salt solution has a higher solute concentration than the plant cell, so water molecules move out of the plant cell via osmosis
 • This causes the cytoplasm to shrink and detach from the cell wall, which is called plasmolysis
 B  is incorrect as the movement of water molecules from a region of high water potential to a region of lower water potential through a partially permeable membrane is not active transport; it is osmosis.
 C  is incorrect as, in a high salt concentration water will move out of the plant cell and not into it. The cell therefore cannot become turgid in these conditions.
 D  is incorrect as continued water loss in a concentrated salt solution will ultimately lead to plasmolysis. Flaccid described the state of cells placed in a solution with the same concentration as the cell contents.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram below shows glucose molecules moving from the lumen of the intestines into surrounding epithelial cells.
  Which row correctly describes the movement of glucose shown?
 |  | type of transport
 | Against concentration gradient?
 | ATP required
 |
 | A
 | osmosis
 | yes
 | no
 |
 | B
 | active transport
 | no
 | yes
 |
 | C
 | active transport
 | yes
 | yes
 |
 | D
 | diffusion
 | no
 | no
 |
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is C.
 • The diagram shows glucose molecules moving from a lower concentration outside the cell to a higher concentration inside the cell, i.e. against a concentration gradient
 • This requires energy from respiration in the form of ATP, and uses carrier molecules in the membrane — this is active transport
 A  is incorrect as osmosis is the movement of water molecules only, not glucose. Osmosis occurs down a water potential gradient, not against the gradient.
 B  is incorrect as active transport moves particles against a concentration gradient, not with it.
 D  is incorrect as diffusion does not occur against a concentration gradient. The movement shown in the diagram is from a region of lower concentration to a region of higher concentration, so rules out diffusion.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which enzyme can catalyses the breakdown of fats into glycerol and fatty acids?
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is D
 • Lipase is the enzyme that can catalyse the breakdown of fats into fatty acids and glycerol
 A  is incorrect as proteases catalyse the break down of proteins into amino acids.
 B  is incorrect as cellulase catalyses the break down of cellulose.
 C  is incorrect as amylase catalyses the break down of starch into maltose.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A chemical test is carried out on a flax seed as follows:
 • A small sample of seed is crushed and placed in a test tube
 • Approximately 2 cm³ of ethanol is added to the test tube containing the crushed seed
 • The mixture is allowed to settle for about 3 minutes and poured into a second test tube containing water
 • A milky/cloudy layer forms at the top of the test tube
 Which of the following correctly names the test and the molecule that it tests for.
options: B. iodine solution test for starch
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is D.
 • The emulsion test is used to detect lipids in a sample
 • As the test tube contains a milky/cloudy emulsion, the flaxseeds must contain lipids which are soluble in ethanol
 A  is incorrect because a positive result of the Biuret test for proteins is a colour change from blue to lilac, not formation of a cloudy emulsion.
 B  is incorrect because a positive result of the iodine test for starch is a colour change from brown to blue-black, not formation of a cloudy emulsion.
 C  is incorrect because, while the test described does involve ethanol, it is called the emulsion test (not the ethanol test) and it detects lipids broadly, not oils specifically.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Sucrase is an enzyme that catalyses the breakdown of the sugar sucrose, but that is unable to break down another sugar, lactose.
 Which of the following correctly explains why sucrase cannot catalyse the breakdown of lactose.
options: A. Lactose is unavailable as a substrate.
B. The active site of sucrase is not complementary to lactose.
C. The active site of sucrase is not the same shape as lactose.
D. Sucrase is used up before lactose is fully broken down.
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is B.
 • Sucrase has an active site that is complementary in shape to sucrose, not lactose
 • Lactose cannot fit into the active site of sucrase, so no enzyme-substrate complex can form and the reaction cannot be catalysed
 A  is incorrect as, even if lactose were present, sucrase would still be unable to break it down.
 C  is incorrect as "same shape" and "complementary shape" do not mean the same thing. For a substrate to fit into an active site, the two must be complementary — meaning they interlock, like a lock and key. If the active site were the same shape as the substrate, they would not fit together at all.
 D  is incorrect as enzymes are biological catalysts and are not used up during reactions.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
An enzyme-controlled reaction takes place in a test tube.
 During the reaction the contents of the test tube include: water, dietary protein, protease, amino acids and hydrochloric acid.
 The graph below shows the progress of the reaction.
  Which component of the test tube contents is represented on the Y axis in the graph above?
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is C.
 • Protease enzymes in the test tube break down the dietary proteins into amino acids
 • Amino acids are the product of the reaction, and their volume increases as the reaction progresses
 A  is incorrect as hydrochloric acid is not produced during the reaction
 B  is incorrect as the concentration of protease will remain the same throughout
 D  is incorrect as the dietary protein is used up, so there would be a decrease in its volume over time

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: How is a leaf adapted for photosynthesis?
options: A. The upper epidermis has air spaces to increase surface area and allow rapid diffusion of carbon dioxide, water and oxygen into the leaf.
B. The phloem allows water transportation from the roots.
C. The palisade mesophyll is waterproof to reduce water loss, and transparent to allow sunlight absorption.
D. Palisade cells are positioned at the top of the leaf to absorb sunlight efficiently, and are packed with chloroplasts.
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is D.
 • Palisade cells are positioned at the top of the leaf where most sunlight hits
 • They are also packed with chloroplasts, which contain chlorophyll to absorb light energy
 A  is incorrect as it is the spongy mesophyll, not the upper epidermis, that contains air spaces for gas diffusion.
 B  is incorrect as water is transported from the roots by the xylem, not the phloem.
 C  is incorrect as the description of being waterproof and transparent better describes the waxy cuticle.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
To investigate the effect of light and dark conditions on gas exchange in an aquatic plant, a test tube is set up as follows:
 • The test tube is filled with hydrogencarbonate indicator solution
 • A cutting from a green aquatic plant is added
 • The tube is covered with aluminium foil and closed with a bung 
 • The tube is exposed to sunlight for 24 hours
 What result will the test tube show after 24 hours?
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is B.
 • The aluminium foil prevents sunlight from entering the test tube
 • The plant will respire but will be unable to photosynthesise
 • More carbon dioxide is released than is used up
 • This results in the hydrogencarbonate indicator solution changing colour to yellow
 A  is incorrect as no colour change will only occur in a control test tube without a plant cutting.
 C  is incorrect as the colour red in this instance indicates that photosynthesis and respiration are occurring at the same rate.
 D  is incorrect as the colour change to purple can only occur if the rate of photosynthesis is greater than that of respiration.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
In which conditions will there be poor plant growth but no yellowing of leaves?
 |  | Nitrogen availability

 | low
 | high
 |
 | C
 | low
 | low
 |
 | D
 | high
 | low
 |
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is B.
 • Nitrate ions are needed to make amino acids, and therefore proteins, so low nitrogen availability leads to poor growth
 • Magnesium ions are needed to make chlorophyll, so high magnesium availability means chlorophyll can still be produced and leaves remain green

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A new smoothie that claims to provide a balanced diet contains the following ingredients:

 |

 |

 |

 What ingredients are missing from the smoothie for it to be a balanced diet product?
options: A. calcium, carbohydrates, vitamins (C and D), fats and oils
B. carbohydrates, vitamins (C and D), fats and oils
C. vitamins (C and D) and mineral ions
D. vitamins (C and D) and calcium
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is B.
 • The product already contains:
 • protein (from soya protein)
 • mineral ions (iron, and calcium from low fat milk)
 • fibre
 • water
 • To be a truly balanced diet smoothie, it still needs carbohydrates, vitamins (C and D), and fats and oils
 A  is incorrect as the product already contains calcium in the low fat milk
 C  is incorrect as the product already contains mineral ions (calcium and iron)
 D  is incorrect as the product already contains calcium in the low fat milk, and also requires carbohydrates, fats and oils

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following describe prevention methods for rickets?
options: A. vitamin D supplementation, adequate intake of protein, adequate intake of iron.
B. vitamin D supplementation, adequate intake of calcium, avoid exposure to sunlight
C. vitamin D supplementation, adequate intake of calcium, exposure to sunlight
D. foods that are high in vitamin D, vitamin A supplementation, adequate intake of fibre
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is C.
 • Rickets is a deficiency condition, caused by a lack of vitamin D, that is characterised by soft, weak bones
 • Vitamin D supplementation ensures adequate vitamin D levels
 • Sunlight can stimulate the body to naturally produce vitamin D
 • Calcium is an essential mineral for bones and teeth
 A  is incorrect as protein and iron do not prevent rickets.
 B  is incorrect as sunlight exposure stimulates the body to produce vitamin D, so it should not be avoided.
 D  is incorrect as vitamin A and fibre do not prevent rickets.

 • Organ 2  is the stomach: a J-shaped organ that forms part of the alimentary canal
 • Organ 3  is the liver: a large organ that is not connected to the oesophagus and therefore is not part of the alimentary canal
 • Organ 4  is the pancreas: a leaf-shaped structure located close to the stomach and duodenum

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The graph below shows the change in concentration of pathogens as food passes through the stomach.
  Which of the following is the main factor that explains the shape of the curve?
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is C.
 • The pH of the stomach is between 1.5 and 3 due to the presence of hydrochloric acid
 • Pathogens cannot survive in this acidic environment
 A  is incorrect as stomach conditions are acidic, not alkaline.
 B  is incorrect as, while protease enzymes are likely to play a role in the digestion of pathogenic proteins, they are not the main factor in reducing pathogen numbers.
 D  is incorrect as, though stomach churning may aid pathogen destruction by ensuring thorough mixing of the stomach contents, it is not the main factor.

 • Tooth 2  is a molar as it has a broad grinding surface for crushing and grinding food
 • Tooth 3  is an incisor as it has a broad, chisel-like biting edge
 • Tooth 4  is a canine as it has a pointed tip

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Amylase is a digestive enzyme.
 Which of the following correctly identifies the product(s) of amylase digestion.
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is C.
 • Amylase breaks down starch to simple reducing sugars
 A  is incorrect as amino acids are the product of protease activity, not amylase.
 B  is incorrect as fatty acids and glycerol are the products of lipase activity, not amylase.
 D  is incorrect as starch is the substrate of the reaction, not the product.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A potometer is used to measure the rate of transpiration. The table below shows the results.
 | Distance travelled by bubble (mm)
 | Time (mins)

 | 17
 | 30
 |
 | 29
 | 60 
 |
