 |
 | 44
 | 120
 |
 | 51

 |
 Calculate the rate of transpiration between 30 and 120 minutes.
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is C.
 • To calculate the rate of transpiration:
 
 • Calculate the distance travelled by the bubble between 120 min and 30 min:
  = 44 - 17 
 = 27 mm
 • Calculate the time that passes between 120 and 30 mins:
 = 120 - 30 
 = 90 min
 • Calculate the rate of transpiration:

 A  is incorrect as it corresponds to dividing 44 mm by 120 mins, i.e. it is the rate of transpiration between 0 and 120 mins, not between 30 and 120 mins.

 D  is incorrect as this is the correct calculation but the wrong unit. 
 Always remember to calculate the change in distance and the change in time rather than using the raw values from the table. 
 Ensure that you include the correct units in your final answer.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following statements about the process of transpiration is correct?
options: A. water moves upwards from the roots
B. increasing wind speed decreases the rate of transpiration
C. water evaporates directly from the stomata
D. water vapour is lost from the leaves by diffusion
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is D.
 • Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from leaves, which occurs by diffusion through the stomata
 A  is incorrect as this does not describe transpiration, which is the loss of water vapour from leaves. The movement of water upwards from the roots is known as the transpiration stream.
 B  is incorrect as increasing wind speed increases the rate of transpiration.
 C  is incorrect as water evaporates from the surfaces of the mesophyll cells, not directly from the stomata.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Look at the sentences below and select the correct answer
 • The right ventricle contains ......... blood 
 • Blood from the right ventricle flows to the .........
 • The blood flows out of the right ventricle via the .........
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is D.
 • The right side of heart receives blood from the body, so it contains deoxygenated blood
 • Blood from the right ventricle travels to the lungs
 • The blood travels out of the right ventricle via the pulmonary artery

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:

B. The pulse rate decreased by more than 40% in the first two minutes of recovery.
C. The greatest decrease in pulse rate occurred in the first minute after exercise stopped.
D. The pulse rate after 3 minutes was less than half of the pulse rate immediately after exercise stopped.
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:

 • The pulse rate dropped by 40 bpm in the first minute (175 to 135 bpm), which is greater than the decrease in any subsequent minute

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following correctly lists features of a capillary?
options: A. thin walls and narrow lumen
B. valves and a large lumen
C. thick walls and a narrow lumen
D. thin walls and a large lumen
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is A.
 • Capillaries have thin walls (one cell thick) and a narrow lumen
 B  is incorrect as capillaries do not have valves; valves are found in veins 
 C  is incorrect as capillaries have thin walls, not thick walls; this description applies to arteries
 D  is incorrect as capillaries have a narrow lumen, not a large lumen; this description applies to veins

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Below are statements about the components of blood and their functions.
 • White blood cells produce antibodies and carry out phagocytosis
 • Red blood cells transport oxygen using haemoglobin
 • Platelets transport hormones and nutrients around the body
 • Plasma transports carbon dioxide and urea
 Which statements are correct?
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is C.
 • Statement 1  is correct: white blood cells defend the body against pathogens by producing antibodies and carrying out phagocytosis to engulf pathogens
 • Statement 2  is correct: red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which binds to oxygen and transports it around the body
 • Statement 4  is correct: plasma is the liquid component of blood that transports substances including carbon dioxide and urea
 Statement 3  is incorrect as it is plasma, not platelets, that transports hormones and nutrients around the body. Platelets are involved in clotting to prevent blood loss and the entry of pathogens.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Below are statements about methods of controlling the spread of disease.
 • Boiling drinking water reduces the risk of transmitting waterborne pathogens
 • Disinfecting surfaces reduces the risk of transmitting pathogens via direct contact
 • Collecting food waste in sealed bins reduces the likelihood of animals spreading pathogens
 • Treating sewage before releasing it into rivers prevents the direct transmission of pathogens between individuals
 Which statements are correct?
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is B.
 • Statement 1  is correct: boiling drinking water kills pathogens, reducing the risk of waterborne transmission
 • Statement 3  is correct: collecting food waste in sealed bins prevents animals from accessing waste and spreading pathogens
 Statement 2  is incorrect as disinfecting surfaces reduces  indirect  transmission via contaminated surfaces, not direct transmission between individuals.
 Statement 4  is incorrect as sewage treatment prevents  indirect  transmission via contaminated water, not direct transmission between individuals.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following is a correct definition for the term transmissible disease?
options: A. a disease caused by a pathogen that can be passed from one host to another
B. a disease caused by a pathogen that cannot be treated with antibiotics
C. a disease that is always transmitted through direct contact between individuals
D. a disease caused by unhealthy lifestyle choices that increase the risk of infection
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is A.
 • A transmissible disease is one caused by a pathogen that can be passed from one host to another
 B  is incorrect as transmissible diseases can be caused by a range of pathogens including viruses, which cannot be treated with antibiotics. Whether a disease responds to antibiotic treatment is unrelated to whether it is transmissible.
 C  is incorrect as transmissible diseases can be passed between hosts indirectly, for example via contaminated surfaces, food, animals or air — not only through direct contact.
 D  is incorrect as this describes a non-communicable disease. Transmissible diseases are caused by pathogens, not by lifestyle choices.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:

 • Structure 2  is a bronchus (plural bronchi): one of the two branches leading from the trachea into each lung
 • Structure 3  is the diaphragm: the large, dome-shaped muscle at the base of the thorax
 • Structure 4  is an alveolus: the small air sacs visible at the ends of the bronchioles
 The oesophagus is part of the digestive system, not the breathing system.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Below are statements about the features of gas exchange surfaces in humans.
 • Gas exchange surfaces have a large surface area to maximise the rate of diffusion
 • Gas exchange surfaces have a thick surface to prevent damage from the constant movement of air
 • Gas exchange surfaces have a good blood supply to remove gases that have diffused across the surface
 • Gas exchange surfaces are well ventilated to increase the concentration of carbon dioxide in the alveoli
 Which statements are correct?
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is C.
 • Statement 1  is correct: a large surface area increases the rate of diffusion of gases across the gas exchange surface
 • Statement 3  is correct: a good blood supply removes oxygen from the lung capillaries after it has diffused into the blood, maintaining the concentration gradient for further diffusion
 Statement 2  is incorrect as gas exchange surfaces are thin, not thick in order to maximise the rate of diffusion.
 Statement 4  is incorrect as good ventilation maintains a high concentration of oxygen and a low concentration of carbon dioxide in the alveoli, not a high concentration of carbon dioxide.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following correctly describes aerobic respiration?
options: A. a chemical reaction in cells that uses oxygen to break down nutrient molecules to release energy
B. a chemical reaction in cells that breaks down glucose without using oxygen
C. the process of breathing air into and out of the lungs to obtain oxygen
D. a chemical reaction in cells that produces energy from the breakdown of glucose
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is A.
 • Aerobic respiration is a chemical reaction in cells that uses oxygen to break down nutrient molecules to release energy
 B  is incorrect as this describes anaerobic respiration, which does not require oxygen.
 C  is incorrect as this describes ventilation, not respiration. Respiration is a chemical process occurring in cells, not a mechanical process of breathing.
 D  is incorrect as aerobic respiration  releases  energy rather than producing it. Energy cannot be created; it is released from the breakdown of nutrient molecules.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
An experiment was conducted to investigate the effect of temperature on respiration in yeast. 
 • 10 cm³ of glucose solution was added to 5 g of yeast
 • A thin layer of oil was added on top of the mixture
 • The tube was placed in a water bath for 10 minutes and a delivery tube was connected to a gas syringe
 Which of the following correctly identify control variables?
options: B. volume of carbon dioxide produced
C. amount of yeast and time
D. volume of yeast and volume of oil added
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is D.
 • Volume of yeast and volume of oil added are both control variables — they are specific, measurable quantities that would need to be kept constant to ensure a fair test
 A  is incorrect as temperature is the independent variable in this experiment, not a control variable. Glucose concentration is a control variable, but pairing it with temperature is incorrect.
 B  is incorrect as the volume of carbon dioxide produced is the dependent variable, not a control variable.
 C  is incorrect as "amount" is an imprecise term. Control variables should be described using specific, measurable quantities such as volume, concentration or mass.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which statement correctly compares aerobic and anaerobic respiration in humans?
options: A. both aerobic and anaerobic respiration produce carbon dioxide as a product
B. aerobic respiration produces carbon dioxide and water, whereas anaerobic respiration produces alcohol.
C. aerobic respiration produces lactic acid, whereas anaerobic respiration produces carbon dioxide and water
D. aerobic respiration releases more energy per glucose molecule than anaerobic respiration
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is D.
 • Aerobic respiration releases more energy per glucose molecule than anaerobic respiration
 A  is incorrect as anaerobic respiration in humans does not produce carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is only produced in anaerobic respiration in yeast.
 B  is incorrect as anaerobic respiration in humans produces lactic acid, not alcohol. This is a products of anaerobic respiration in yeast.
 C  is incorrect as the products of aerobic and anaerobic respiration have been swapped. Aerobic respiration produces carbon dioxide and water, whereas anaerobic respiration in humans produces lactic acid.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following shows the word equation for anaerobic respiration in yeast?
options: C. glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water
D. carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is A.
 • Anaerobic respiration in yeast breaks down glucose to produce alcohol and carbon dioxide
 B  is incorrect as glucose → lactic acid is the word equation for anaerobic respiration in humans, not yeast.
 C  is incorrect as glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water is the word equation for aerobic respiration.
 D  is incorrect as this is the word equation for photosynthesis.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following is a correct statement about excretion in humans?
options: A. carbon dioxide, excess water and ions are excreted by the lungs
B. urea and excess water are excreted by the kidneys
C. urea is transported from the kidneys to the bladder via the urethra
D. the bladder connects the kidneys to the urethra
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is B.
 • The kidneys excrete urea and excess water from the body
 • Ions are also excreted by the kidneys, but their omission does not make this statement incorrect
 A  is incorrect as, although carbon dioxide and some water vapour are excreted through the lungs, ions are not — they are excreted by the kidneys.
 C  is incorrect as urea leaves the kidneys in the urine, which is transported to the bladder via the ureters. The urethra connects the bladder to the exterior.
 D  is incorrect as the bladder does not connect the kidneys to anything. The kidneys are connected to the bladder via the ureters, and the bladder is connected to the exterior via the urethra.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The image below shows a neurone.
  Which of the following statements about the neurone is correct?
options: A. this is a motor neurone that carries impulses from the CNS to effectors
B. this is a relay neurone that connects sensory and motor neurones in the CNS
C. this is a sensory neurone that carries electrical impulses towards the CNS
D. this is a sensory neurone that carries electrical impulses from a receptor to an effector
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is C.
 • The position of the cell body in the middle of the axon identifies this as a sensory neurone
 • Sensory neurones carry electrical impulses from receptors towards the CNS
 A  is incorrect as this is not a motor neurone. Motor neurones have their cell body at one end, not in the middle, and carry impulses from the CNS to effectors.
 B  is incorrect as this is not a relay neurone. Relay neurones are typically located entirely within the CNS, whereas this neurone has long extensions, suggesting that it connects to structures outside the CNS.
 D  is incorrect as sensory neurones carry electrical impulses from receptors to the CNS, not from receptors directly to effectors.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: A person touches a pin. Which of the following correctly describes the sequence of events in the resulting reflex arc?
options: A. pin → receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → effector
B. pin → receptor → motor neurone → relay neurone → sensory neurone → effector
C. pin → receptor → relay neurone → sensory neurone → motor neurone → effector
D. pin → effector → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → receptor
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is A.
 • When a finger touches a pin, touch receptors detect the stimulus and a nerve impulse is sent along the sensory neurone to the relay neurone in the spinal cord
 • The relay neurone passes the impulse to the motor neurone, which carries it to the effector, causing the arm muscles to contract and withdraw the finger
 B  is incorrect as the impulse travels along the sensory neurone first, not the motor neurone. Motor neurones carry impulses away from the CNS to the effector. A helpful way to remember this is that  sensory  neurones connect to  sense  organs, such as the skin.
 C  is incorrect as the impulse travels along the sensory neurone before reaching the relay neurone, not the other way round.
 D  is incorrect as the sequence begins at the receptor, not the effector. Receptors detect stimuli at the start of the reflex arc, whereas effectors, such as muscles, produce the response at the end.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Ear length in rabbits is determined by a single gene with two alleles.
 • The long ears allele is dominant and is represented by  E
 • The short ears allele is recessive and is represented by  e
 A male rabbit that is heterozygous for ear length mates with a female rabbit with short ears.
 What is the probability that any offspring will have long ears?
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is D.
 To determine the probability that any offspring will have long ears:
 • Determine the genotypes of both parents:
 • the heterozygous male has genotype  Ee
 • the female has short ears, which is the recessive phenotype, so she must be homozygous  ee
 • Set up a Punnett square:
 |  | E
 | e
 |
 | e
 | Ee
 | ee
 |
 | e
 | Ee
 | ee
 |
 • Count the offspring with long ears: 
 • 2 out of 4 offspring have genotype Ee and will therefore have long ears
 • Express as a probability:
   =    = 50 %

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Plants respond to changes in their environment.
 Which row correctly describes the responses of a plant shoot to light and gravity?
 |  | Light
 | Gravity
 |
 | A
 | negative gravitropism
 | negative phototropism
 |
 | B
 | positive phototropism
 | negative gravitropism
 |
 | C
 | positive phototropism
 | positive gravitropism
 |
 | D
 | negative phototropism
 | positive  gravitropism
 |
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is B.
 • A plant shoot will grow away from gravity (negative gravitropism) and towards light (positive phototropism)
 A  is incorrect as growth towards light is not gravitropism and growth towards gravity is not phototropism.
 C  is incorrect as shoots grow away from gravity so cannot show positive gravitropism.
 D  is incorrect as shoots grow towards light so cannot show negative phototropism. Shoots also grow away from gravity so cannot show positive gravitropism.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following statements about antibiotics is correct?
options: A. antibiotics can be used to treat HIV
B. antibiotic resistance in humans reduces the effectiveness of antibiotics
C. antibiotics can only treat bacterial infections
D. antibiotics are an effective method of preventing the spread of STIs
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is C.
 • Antibiotics are drugs that are used to treat bacterial infections, but do not affect viruses
 A  is incorrect as HIV is a viral infection and antibiotics do not affect viruses.
 B  is incorrect as antibiotic resistance develops in bacteria, not in humans.
 D  is incorrect as antibiotics treat bacterial infections and are not an effective method of controlling the spread of STIs.

set-7/paper-3-theory-core.stem:
A student is identifying different plants found in a school garden. They take a small sample from the leaf of a plant to look at under a light microscope. 
 Fig. 1.1 shows a diagram of one of the cells observed.
  Fig. 1.1
 State the names of structures A, B and C in Fig. 1.1.
set-7/paper-3-theory-core.explanation:
• A = cell wall  [1 mark]
 • B = vacuole / permanent vacuole  [1 mark]
 • C = chloroplast  [1 mark]
 The most common error  is misidentifying the large central vacuole (B) as the nucleus. In a plant leaf cell, the vacuole is the largest structure

set-7/paper-3-theory-core.stem:
A student monitored their breathing rate before, during, and after an exercise period. The exercise period began at minute 1 and ended at minute 7.
 The results are shown in Fig. 2.1.
  Fig. 2.1
 Determine the breathing rate at minute 4 and at minute 8 in Fig. 2.1.
set-7/paper-3-theory-core.explanation:
• Minute 4 = 17 breaths per minute  [1 mark]
 • Minute 8 = 29 breaths per minute  [1 mark]

set-7/paper-3-theory-core.stem:
A student investigated the mass of water lost by a potted plant over one hour in different environmental conditions. The results are shown in  Table 3.1 .
 Table 3.1
 | Condition
 | Water lost in 1 hour (g)
 |
 | Cool and still
 | 2.5

 Water is transported from the roots to the leaves before it is lost to the atmosphere.

 [1]

 [1]
set-7/paper-3-theory-core.explanation:
(i) The tissue that transports water up the stem of plants is:
 • Xylem  [1 mark]
 (i) The name of the small openings on the underside of the leaf from which most water vapour is lost is:
 • Stomata / stoma  [1 mark]
 (iii) The name of the cells that control the opening and closing of the openings named in (ii) is:
 • Guard (cells)  [1 mark]

set-7/paper-3-theory-core.stem:
A student analysed the nutritional content of a 60 g "high-energy" snack bar. They suspected that the bar contained starch and protein.
 Describe the food tests they would use to confirm the presence of these two nutrients.
set-7/paper-3-theory-core.explanation:
• Iodine solution  [1 mark] 
 • Turns blue-black if starch is present  [1 mark]
 AND
 • Biuret reagent  [1 mark] 
 • Turns purple / lilac / violet if protein is present  [1 mark]
 The results must be linked with the correct tests for marking points 2 and 4 to be awarded.

set-7/paper-3-theory-core.stem:
A large area of tropical rainforest was cleared by an agricultural company in 2010. The rainforest was replaced with a single crop of oil palm trees. 
 Fig. 5.1 shows a bar chart of the estimated population of a native forest bird species recorded in this area between 2010 and 2020.
  Fig. 5.1 
 Describe the trend in the bird population between 2010 and 2020 and suggest why the deforestation of the rainforest has caused this change.
set-7/paper-3-theory-core.explanation:
Description of trend (maximum 2)
 • Bird population decreases
 • Population changes from 5000 to (around) 200
 • The population decrease is consistent/steady / occurs at the same rate throughout the period
 Suggested explanation (maximum 2)
 • Loss of habitat
 • Loss of nesting sites/breeding sites
 • Loss of food sources / disruption to food chain
 • Increased vulnerability to predators (due to loss of shelter)
 [3 marks]
 Award a maximum of two marks for description and a maximum of two marks for explanation, but no more than three marks in total across both sections.
 Always quote both values from the graph when describing the trend — "decreased from 5000 to 200" 
 Never just say "they die" — link it to a specific biological reason like loss of food or shelter.

set-7/paper-3-theory-core.stem:
A farmer is responsible for managing a large herd of cattle. Within the herd, some cattle naturally grow horns whilst others do not. Cattle that do not grow horns are described as polled. The allele for being polled (P) is dominant over the allele for having horns (p).
 Define the following terms.
 (i) Allele
 [1]
 (ii) Heterozygous
 [1]
set-7/paper-3-theory-core.explanation:
(i) Allele:
 • An alternative form/version of a gene  [1 mark]
 (ii) Heterozygous:
 • Having two different alleles of a gene  [1 mark]

set-7/paper-3-theory-core.stem:
A patient visited a medical clinic to receive a vaccination.
 While waiting in the clinic, the patient felt nervous about the injection. A hormone was secreted that prepared their body for a 'fight or flight' response, causing their heart rate to increase.
 (i) State the name of this hormone and the specific glands that secrete it. 
 [2]
 (ii) State one effect that this hormone has on the body, other than an increased heart rate. 
 [1]
set-7/paper-3-theory-core.explanation:
(i) The hormone and the glands are:
 • Adrenaline  [1 mark] 
 • Adrenal (glands)  [1 mark] 
 (ii) One effect other than an increased heart rate is:
 Any  one  from: 
 • increased breathing rate 
 • widened pupils / increased pupil diameter
 [1 mark]
 Accept references to increased blood glucose

set-7/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.stem:
A student investigated the effect of pH on the activity of the enzyme amylase. Amylase breaks down starch into maltose. The student used the following method: 
 • Step 1:  set up four test-tubes, each containing the same volume of starch solution and amylase
 • Step 2:  add a different pH buffer solution to each test-tube
 • Step 3:  place all four test-tubes in a water-bath
 • Step 4:  every 30 seconds, remove a drop of the mixture from each test-tube and add it to a drop of iodine solution on a spotting tile
 • Step 5:  record the time taken for the iodine solution to remain yellow-brown (i.e. the point at which no colour change occurs)
 Fig. 1  shows the thermometer reading from the water bath at the start of the experiment.
 Fig. 1
   Record the temperature shown in  Fig. 1.
set-7/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.explanation:
• 36.9 °C   [1 mark]
 Accept values between 36.88-36.9
 Units must be included

set-7/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.stem:
A researcher investigated the populations of rabbits and foxes in a woodland area over 20 years.
 Fig. 2  shows the estimated populations over this time period.
 Fig. 2
  (i) Using  Fig. 2 , state the rabbit population at year 0.
 [1]
 (ii) Using  Fig. 2 , state the fox population at year 10.
 [1]
set-7/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.explanation:
(i) The rabbit population at year 0 is:
 • 400  [1 mark]
 (ii) The fox population at year 10 is:
 • 40  [1 mark]
 When reading values from a graph, make sure you read the correct axis. Here, the rabbit population is typically shown on one axis and the fox population on another. Take care to identify which line represents which organism before reading off the value.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A scientist observes four events in an organism:
 • It takes in glucose.
 • It releases carbon dioxide produced in cells.
 • It moves away from a harmful chemical.
 • It increases in biomass over time.
 Which row correctly matches the events to characteristics?
 |  1
 2
 3
 4

 | A
 | respiration
 | excretion
 | sensitivity
 | growth
 |
 | B
 | nutrition
 | excretion
 | sensitivity
 | growth
 |
 | C
 | nutrition
 | respiration
 | movement
 | reproduction
 |
 | D
 | excretion
 | nutrition
 | sensitivity
 | growth
 |
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B .
 • 1 = nutrition : taking in glucose is taking in material for energy
 • 2 = excretion : releasing carbon dioxide produced by cells is removing a waste product of metabolism
 • 3 = sensitivity : moving away from a harmful chemical is detecting and responding to a change in the environment
 • 4 = growth : increasing in dry mass over time matches the definition of growth
 While it is possible to link statement 2 with respiration, and statement 3 with movement, the combination given by option B is the only one that is correct for all four statements.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram shows an organism.
  Which arthropod group does the organism belong to?
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C.
 • The organism has the key features of an insect: 
 • six legs
 • one pair of antennae
 • a body divided into head, thorax and abdomen
 A  is incorrect because arachnids have four pairs of legs and no antennae.
 B   is incorrect because crustaceans have more than three pairs of legs and two pairs of antennae.
 D  is incorrect because myriapods have many body segments with many legs.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A palisade mesophyll cell is found near the upper surface of a leaf and contains many chloroplasts.
 Why is this an effective adaptation?
options: A. It reduces water loss by closing stomata.
B. It allows the cell to absorb more light for photosynthesis.
C. It increases the surface area for gas exchange.
D. It allows the cell to respire at a higher rate.
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.
 • A palisade mesophyll cell is packed with many chloroplasts and is found near the upper surface of the leaf, where light intensity is highest
 • This means it can absorb more light energy for photosynthesis
 A  is incorrect because palisade mesophyll cells do not close stomata; that is the role of guard cells.
 C  is incorrect because the palisade mesophyll layer does not have a notably large surface area. Increasing surface area for gas exchange is mainly the role of the spongy mesophyll, which has large air spaces that allow gases to diffuse through the leaf.
 D  is incorrect because although the cell does respire, the key adaptation described here is for photosynthesis, not increased respiration.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
An image of a cell is 24 mm long. The actual cell length is 6 μm.
 What is the magnification?
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.
 • The cell is magnified 4000 times
 To calculate magnification:
 • Convert the units so that they match
 • There are 1000 μm in 1 mm
 24 x 100 = 24 000 μm
 • Use the formula: 
 magnification = image size ÷ actual size
 = 24 000 ÷ 6
 =  4000
 Always check that your units match before you begin calculating. If the image size is given in millimetres and the actual size is given in micrometres, convert the image size to micrometres first (multiply by 1000) before doing anything else. 
 Carrying out unit conversions at the start of your working reduces the risk of forgetting to convert at all, which is one of the most common sources of error in magnification questions.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: What is the role of water in digestion?
options: A. It increases the surface area of food for enzyme action.
B. It allows soluble food molecules to dissolve so they can be absorbed.
C. It turns insoluble food molecules into soluble molecules.
D. It provides energy for active transport.
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.
 • Water acts as a solvent, so substances can dissolve in it. This allows digested substances to be transported and absorbed
 A  is incorrect because increasing the surface area of food is the role of physical digestion (for example chewing), not water.
 C   is incorrect because large insoluble food molecules are made into small soluble molecules by chemical digestion carried out by enzymes, not water.
 D  is incorrect because water does not provide the energy for active transport.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A potato tissue sample has an initial mass of 5.0 g. 
 It is immersed in an unknown solution.  
 Its mass after 1 hour is 4.2 g. 
 Which statement is correct?
options: A. The solution had a lower water potential than the plant tissue.
B. The solution had a higher water potential than the plant tissue.
C. The plant tissue had no cell membrane.
D. The solution was distilled water.
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A.
 • The tissue  lost mass , so water left the cells by osmosis. This means the surrounding solution had a  lower water potential  than the plant tissue
 B  is incorrect because if the solution had a higher water potential, water would enter and mass would increase.
 C  is incorrect because osmosis only occurs through partially permeable membranes, which plant cells do have.
 D i s incorrect because distilled water has a high water potential, meaning water would enter and mass would increase.
 Don't mix up water potential   with the concentration of the solute. Osmosis is defined as the net movement of water molecules from a region of  higher water potential  (dilute solution) to a region of  lower water potential  (concentrated solution), through a  partially permeable membrane .

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram shows a root hair cell.
  Which row correctly matches each labelled part to its role in active transport?
 |  Structure needed for moving ions
 Structure supplying energy

 | R
 |
 | B
 | S
 | Q
 |
 | C
 | R
 | P
 |
 | D
 | P
 | Q

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A.
 • P = carrier protein:  this is the structure needed to move ions by active transport
 • R = mitochondrion:   this is the structure that releases energy through respiration
 The other answers are incorrect because  Q = ions:  these are the substances the cell takes up, and  S = cell wall:  this is the freely permeable outer layer of the plant cell.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A section of one DNA strand has the bases:
 A C T G
 What is the sequence on the opposite strand?
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.
 • In DNA, bases pair in a fixed way:  A pairs with T  and  C pairs with G
 • Therefore the initial strand pairs with its opposite strand as follows:
 A C T G
 T G A C

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Why are enzymes said to be specific?
options: A. Each enzyme can only work at one temperature.
B. Each enzyme has an active site with a complementary shape to a particular substrate.
C. The active site changes permanently after every reaction, so only one substrate can be used.
D. Each enzyme works best with substrates of the same size.
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.
 • Enzymes are specific because each enzyme has an  active site  with a shape that is  complementary to a particular substrate , so only the correct substrate fits properly
 A  is incorrect because enzymes can work over a range of temperatures, though they have an optimum.
 C  is incorrect because enzymes are not normally changed permanently after each reaction.
 D  is incorrect because specificity depends on shape and fit, not just the size of the substrate.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A student heats an amylase solution to 80 °C for 10 minutes, then cools it back to 25 °C before adding starch. 
 The reaction rate stays very low.
 What is the best explanation for this?
options: A. Cooling stops amylase from working.
B. Starch has changed shape permanently.
C. Amylase was used up before starch was added.
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.
 • Amylase is an  enzyme
 • Heating to  80 °C  likely  denatured  the enzyme. 
 • The heat breaks bonds, changing the shape of the  active site  permanently so that the substrate (starch) cannot fit
 A  is incorrect because cooling alone does not permanently stop enzymes from working.
 B  is incorrect because the problem is the enzyme, not the substrate.
 C  is incorrect because the enzyme was heated before the reaction started, so it was not used up by reacting.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Which row correctly identifies the reactants and products of photosynthesis?
 |  Reactants
 Products

 | A
 | carbon dioxide and water
 | glucose and oxygen
 |
 | B
 | carbon dioxide and glucose
 | water and oxygen
 |
 | C
 | oxygen and water
 | carbon dioxide and glucose
 |
 | D
 | glucose and oxygen
 | carbon dioxide and water
 |
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A.
 • The word equation for photosynthesis is: 
 carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen 
 • Reactants  are the starting materials in a chemical reaction, while  products  are the new substances formed as a result
 B  is incorrect because glucose is a product and water is a reactant.
 C  is incorrect oxygen is a product and carbon dioxide is a reactant.
 D  is incorrect because it shows the reactants and products of aerobic respiration, not photosynthesis.
 The substances in photosynthesis and aerobic respiration are arranged in reverse, so this can help you remember the equations. Always think about which process is building glucose (photosynthesis) and which is breaking glucose down to release energy (respiration).

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The graph shows the effect of increasing light intensity on the rate of photosynthesis. 
  Which does point A show?
options: A. Light is no longer the limiting factor.
B. Light has stopped reaching the leaf.
D. Chlorophyll has been used up.
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A.
 • If the rate stops increasing even when  light intensity continues to increase , then  light is no longer the limiting factor . Another factor must now be limiting the rate
 B  is incorrect because if light stopped reaching the leaf, the rate would decrease.
 C  is incorrect because the graph shows the rate has levelled off, not fallen to zero.
 D  is incorrect because chlorophyll is not used up in photosynthesis.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: How does physical digestion help chemical digestion?
options: A. It changes large insoluble molecules into small soluble molecules.
B. It increases the surface area of food.
C. It provides the acidic conditions needed.
D. It absorbs digested nutrients directly into the blood.
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.
 • Physical digestion breaks food into smaller pieces, which  increases the surface area  available for enzymes
 A  is incorrect because changing large insoluble molecules into small soluble molecules is chemical digestion, not physical digestion.
 C  is incorrect because acidic conditions are provided by hydrochloric acid in the stomach, not by physical digestion.
 D  is incorrect because physical digestion does not move nutrients into the blood, and absorption happens after digestion.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Which row correctly matches the enzyme to what it breaks down?
 |  enzyme
 what it breaks down

 | A
 | amylase
 | fats
 |
 | B
 | maltase
 | starch
 |
 | C
 | pepsin
 | starch
 |
 | D
 | trypsin
 | protein
 |
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.
 • Trypsin  is a  protease , so it breaks down  protein
 A  is incorrect because amylase breaks down starch, not fats.
 B  is incorrect because maltase breaks down maltose to glucose, not starch.
 C  is incorrect because pepsin is another protease that breaks down protein, not starch.
 While  pepsin  breaks down proteins in the  acidic  conditions of the stomach,  trypsin  continues to break down proteins in the  alkaline  conditions of the small intestine.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram shows villi in a healthy small intestine and in a person with coeliac disease.
  A person with coeliac disease may become undernourished even if they eat enough food. 
 Which is the best explanation?
options: A. The surface area exposed to food is reduced, which stops chemical digestion from taking place in the small intestine.
B. The damaged villi prevent enough digestive enzymes from being secreted into the small intestine.
C. The surface area of the small intestine is reduced so fewer digested nutrients are absorbed into the blood.
D. The damaged villi cause food to move through the intestine too slowly to be digested.
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C.
 • In coeliac disease, the villi become  damaged and flattened , so the  surface area of the small intestine is reduced . This means  fewer digested nutrients are absorbed into the blood , so the person may become undernourished even if they eat enough food
 A  is incorrect because reducing surface area mainly affects absorption, not the whole process of chemical digestion.
 B  is incorrect because damaged villi do not mainly prevent digestive enzymes from being secreted. 
 D  is incorrect because danaged villi will not cause the food to move slowly.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which sequence correctly shows the pathway of water through a plant?
options: A. xylem → root hair cell → root cortex cell → mesophyll
B. root hair cell → root cortex cell → xylem → mesophyll
C. root cortex cell → mesophyll → xylem → root hair cell
D. root hair cell → xylem → root cortex cell → mesophyll
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.
 • Water moves through the plant in this order: 
 root hair cells → root cortex cells → xylem → mesophyll cells
 • Root hair cells  absorb water from the soil because they are in direct contact and have a large surface area.
 • The water then passes through the  root cortex cells  to reach the centre of the root
 • Next, the water enters the  xylem , which carries water up through the root and stem towards the leaves
 • Finally, in the leaf water moves from the xylem into the  mesophyll cells , where it can evaporate during transpiration and is also used in photosynthesis

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Which environmental condition would most reduce transpiration?
 |  temperature
 humidity

 | A
 | low
 | high
 |
 | B
 | high
 | low
 |
 | C
 | low
 | low
 |
 | D
 | high
 | high
 |
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A.
 • Transpiration is reduced by  low temperature  and  high humidity
 • Low temperature  gives water molecules less kinetic energy, so evaporation from mesophyll cell surfaces is slower
 • High humidity  means the air already contains a lot of water vapour, so the diffusion gradient for water vapour leaving the leaf is smaller, reducing diffusion through the stomata
 B  is incorrect because high temperature and low humidity both increase transpiration.
 C  is incorrect because low humidity increases the diffusion gradient for water vapour.
 D  is incorrect because high temperature increases evaporation.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: How does blood exit the heart?
options: A. through arteries from the atria
B. through arteries from the ventricles
C. through veins from the atria
D. through veins from the ventricles
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.
 • Blood leaves the heart in  arteries , and it is pumped out from the  ventricles
 • The  left ventricle  pumps oxygenated blood into the  aorta , and the  right ventricle  pumps deoxygenated blood into the  pulmonary artery
 A  is incorrect because blood does not leave the heart from the atria. 
 C  is incorrect because veins carry blood towards the heart, not away from it.
 D  is incorrect because although blood leaves from the ventricles, it does not leave through veins.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram shows the blood vessels associated with the liver.
  What is the blood vessel labelled X?
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C.
 • The  hepatic vein  carries blood  away from the liver  and returns it to the  vena cava , which transports the blood back to the heart
 • In the diagram,  X leads out of the organ , which matches the position of the hepatic vein
 A  is incorrect because the hepatic artery carries oxygenated blood from the aorta into the liver, so the blood flow direction would be towards the liver.
 B  is incorrect because the hepatic portal vein also enters the liver at the bottom. It brings nutrient-rich blood from the intestines to the liver and is typically shown entering the liver alongside the hepatic artery.
 C  is incorrect because the bile duct is not a blood vessel. It carries bile away from the liver to the gall bladder or small intestine and is also located at the bottom of the liver near the vessels that enter the organ.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The following are statements about blood.
 • Red blood cells transport oxygen.
 • Plasma transports hormones.
 • Platelets destroy pathogens.
 Which statements are correct?
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.
 Statement 1 is correct  because  red blood cells transport oxygen . They contain  haemoglobin , a protein that  binds oxygen  in the lungs and carries it to body tissues.
 Statement 2 is correct  because  plasma transports hormones and other dissolved substances  around the body. These include nutrients such as glucose, waste products such as urea, carbon dioxide and ions.
 Statement 3 is incorrect  because  destroying pathogens is mainly the role of white blood cells .  Platelets  are involved in  blood clotting , helping to form a clot to prevent blood loss when a blood vessel is damaged.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Varicella zoster virus  (VZV) causes chickenpox.
 The graph shows the concentration of antibodies in the blood of a patient after vaccination against VZV.
  What most likely happened at point X to cause the increase in antibody concentration?
options: A. infection with a different pathogen
B. the vaccine took time to stimulate lymphocytes
C. antibodies produced earlier were released into the blood
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.
 • The first small rise shows the  primary immune response after vaccination , when antibodies are produced slowly and  memory cells are formed
 • When the person is  infected with VZV at X , these memory cells recognise the antigen and respond rapidly, producing  large amounts of antibodies  and causing the large second increase
 A  is incorrect because infection with a different pathogen would trigger a new primary immune response, which would be slower and smaller.
 B  is incorrect because the vaccine already stimulated lymphocytes to produce antibodies, shown by the first peak on the graph.
 C  is incorrect because antibodies are not stored and later released.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: What do the external intercostal muscles do during inhalation?
options: B. pull ribs upwards and outwards
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.
 • External intercostal muscles  contract , moving the ribs  up and out
 • This increases the  volume  of the  thorax , which decreases the  pressure  inside the lungs and  draws air into the lungs
 A  is incorrect because downward rib movement occurs during exhalation.
 C  is incorrect because muscles do not directly push air.
 D  is incorrect because mucus is produced by goblet cells, not intercostal muscles.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Why does breathing rate increase during exercise?
options: A. oxygen concentration in blood increases
B. oxygen concentration in blood decreases
C. carbon dioxide concentration in blood increases
D. carbon dioxide concentration in blood decreases
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C.
 • During exercise, muscle cells carry out  respiration at a higher rate , producing  more carbon dioxide as a waste product
 • The increased  carbon dioxide concentration in the blood is detected by the brain , which stimulates an  increase in breathing rate and depth  to remove the excess carbon dioxide
 A  is incorrect because oxygen concentration does not increase during exercise.
 B  is incorrect because although oxygen concentration in the blood may decrease slightly during exercise, breathing rate is mainly controlled by increases in carbon dioxide concentration detected by the brain.
 D  is incorrect because because carbon dioxide concentration does not decrease during exercise.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Which row correctly completes the balanced equation for anaerobic respiration in yeast? 
 C 6 H 12 O 6  →    X + Y
 |  X
 Y

 | A
 | 2C 2 H 5 OH

 | 2O₂

 |
 | D
 | C₃H₆O 2
 | C₃H₆O 4

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A.
 • Anaerobic respiration in yeast converts  glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide :
 C 6 H 12 O 6  →    2C 2 H 5 OH + 2CO₂
 You must memorise the  balanced chemical equation  for  aerobic respiration  and  anaerobic respiration in yeast .
 You should also know the  word equations  for:
 • aerobic respiration
 • anaerobic respiration in yeast
 • anaerobic respiration in muscle cells
 Remember that anaerobic respiration in  muscles  forms  lactic acid , while anaerobic respiration in  yeast  forms  ethanol and carbon dioxide.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Glucose is filtered from the blood plasma at the glomerulus. Explain why glucose is not normally found in the urine of a healthy person.
options: A. Glucose is reabsorbed back into the blood.
B. Glucose cannot pass through the filtration membrane in the glomerulus.
C. Glucose is converted into urea.
D. Glucose is broken down in the kidney before urine is formed.
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A.
 • Glucose is a small molecule and is filtered from the blood   into the nephron at the glomerulus
 • In a healthy kidney  all of the glucose is reabsorbed  from the nephron  back into the blood , so none appears in the urine
 B  is incorrect because glucose can pass through the filtration membrane in the glomerulus due to its small size. 
 C  is incorrect because glucose is not converted into urea. Urea is produced in the liver from excess amino acids during deamination.
 D  is incorrect because glucose is not broken down in the kidney.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: What is the sequence of a reflex arc?
options: A. receptor → motor neurone → relay neurone → sensory neurone → effector
B. receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → effector
C. sensory neurone→ relay neurone → receptor → motor neurone → effector
D. sensory neurone → receptor → relay neurone → effector → motor neurone
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.
 • A reflex arc follows a fixed sequence:
 • A  receptor  detects a  stimulus  (for example heat or pain) and generates a nerve impulse
 • The impulse travels along a  sensory neurone  to the central nervous system (usually the spinal cord)
 • The impulse passes across a  synapse  to a  relay neurone  within the spinal cord
 • The relay neurone passes the impulse across another synapse to a  motor neurone
 • The motor neurone carries the impulse to an  effector  (a muscles or gland), which produces the response

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which muscle action causes the pupil to become smaller in bright light?
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A.
 • In bright light, the  pupil reflex  reduces the amount of light entering the eye. The  circular muscles of the iris contract , which makes the pupil  smaller  (constricts) and therefore reduces the amount of light reaching the retina
 B  is incorrect because when the radial muscles contract, the pupil becomes larger (dilates), which happens in dim light to allow more light into the eye.
 C  is incorrect because when the circular muscles relax, the radial muscles contract as described above.
 D  is incorrect because the ciliary muscles control the shape of the lens, helping focus on near or distant objects; they do not control pupil size.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The table shows features of four body control systems.
 Which row is the nervous system?
 |  Response speed
 Carried by
 Duration of effect

 | A
 | fast
 | neurones
 | short
 |
 | B
 | slow
 | blood
 | long
 |
 | C
 | slow
 | neurones
 | long
 |
 | D
 | fast
 | blood
 | long
 |
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A.
 • Nervous control involves  electrical impulses travelling along neurones , so responses are  very fast  and usually  short-lived
 B  is incorrect because signals carried in the blood describe hormonal control, not nervous control.
 C  is incorrect because nervous signals do travel along neurones, but they are fast, not slow.
 D  is incorrect because signals carried in the blood describe hormonal control, not nervous control.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram shows a plant shoot.
  What substance is X?
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.
 • Auxin  is a plant growth hormone produced in the shoot tip. When light shines from one side, auxin becomes  unevenly distributed , moving to the  shaded side of the shoot
 • Auxin  stimulates cell elongation , so cells on the shaded side grow longer
 • This causes the shoot to  bend towards the light , which is the  phototropic response
 A  is incorrect because glucose is used in respiration and growth, but it does not control the bending of the shoot.
 B  is incorrect because chlorophyll is the green pigment used for photosynthesis; it absorbs light but does not control growth direction.
 C  is incorrect because cellulose forms the cell walls of plant cells and provides support; it does not control plant growth responses.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A new antibiotic is introduced. Initially it is very effective at killing a bacterial pathogen. After many years, the antibiotic becomes much less effective.
 Which process explains this change?
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A.
 • Natural selection  occurs when bacteria with mutations that make them resistant to an antibiotic survive treatment
 • These resistant bacteria  reproduce  and pass the  resistance genes  to their offspring
 • Over time,  the proportion of resistant bacteria increases , so the antibiotic becomes  less effective
 B  is incorrect because bacteria do not have immune systems.
 C  is is incorrect because behavioural adaptation refers to changes in animal behaviour that improve survival, such as migration or hunting strategies. 
 D  is incorrect because toxin production refers to bacteria producing harmful chemicals that damage host tissues, not antibiotics.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram shows a flower.
  Which row correctly identifies the functions of X, Y and Z?
 |  Function of X
 Function of Y
 Function of Z

 | A
 | produces pollen grains
 | receives pollen grains
 | contains ovules
 |
 | B
 | produces pollen grains
 | receives pollen grains
 | produces pollen
 |
 | C
 | receives pollen grains
 | produces pollen grains
 | contains pollen
 |
 | D
 | produces pollen grains
 | contains ovules
 | receives pollen
 |
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A.
 • The  anther  ( X ) is part of the  stamen  and its function is to  produce pollen grains , which contain the  male gametes
 • The  stigma  ( Y ) is the top of the  carpel  and its role is to  receive pollen grains during pollination . It is often sticky to help trap pollen
 • The  ovary  ( Z ) is located at the base of the carpel and  contains ovules , which hold the  female gametes . After fertilisation, the ovules develop into  seeds

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The graph shows the levels of four hormones in the blood during a 28-day menstrual cycle.
  What is hormone X?
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.
 • Luteinising hormone (LH)  shows a  sharp surge just before day 14 , which  triggers ovulation , causing the ovary to release an egg
 • This sudden peak in LH is known as the  LH surge
 A  is incorrect because FSH (follicle-stimulating hormone) increases earlier in the cycle and stimulates the development of follicles in the ovary.
 C  is incorrect because oestrogen gradually increases during the first half of the cycle as the follicle develops. 
 D  is incorrect because progesterone rises after ovulation and helps maintain the lining of the uterus in preparation for possible pregnancy.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: What carries genetic instructions from the nucleus to the cytoplasm?
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.
 • Messenger RNA (mRNA)  carries genetic instructions from the  nucleus to the cytoplasm
 • A gene remains in the nucleus, but a  copy of the gene is made as mRNA
 • The mRNA moves out of the nucleus to a  ribosome  in the cytoplasm, where it is used to assemble amino acids into a  protein
 A  is incorrect because DNA remains in the nucleus and does not leave to carry instructions to the cytoplasm.
 B  is incorrect because neurotransmitters are chemical signalling molecules used to transmit impulses between neurones, not to carry genetic information.
 C  is incorrect because ribosomes assemble proteins, but they do not carry genetic instructions from the nucleus.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: When gametes are produced, cells undergo division by
options: A. mitosis to produce genetically identical cells.
B. mitosis to produce genetically different cells.
C. meiosis to produce genetically identical cells.
D. meiosis to produce genetically different cells.
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.
 • Meiosis  is the type of cell division that produces  gametes (sperm and egg cells)
 • During meiosis, the chromosome number is  halved from diploid to haploid , and the resulting cells are  genetically different from each other
 • This genetic variation is important for  sexual reproduction
 If the question mentions  growth ,  repair  or  asexual reproduction , the process is  mitosis . Mitosis produces  genetically identical cells  and keeps the chromosome number the same.
 If the question mentions  gametes  or  sexual reproduction , the process is  meiosis . Meiosis produces haploid gametes that are  genetically different , with half the number of chromosomes as the parent cell.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Red–green colour blindness is caused by a recessive allele on the X chromosome.
 A carrier female (XᴺXᶜ) and a normal male (XᴺY) have children.
 What proportion of their sons will be colour blind?
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C.
 • Determine parent genotypes:
 Carrier female:  XᴺXᶜ
 Normal male:  XᴺY
 • Complete Punnett square:
 |  | Xᴺ
 | Y
 |
 | Xᴺ
 | XᴺXᴺ (daughter, normal)
 | XᴺY (son, normal)
 |
 | Xᶜ
 | XᴺXᶜ (daughter, carrier)
 | XᶜY (son, colour blind)
 |
 • For sons only, look at the Y column (because sons get Y from the father):
 XᴺY  (normal)
 XᶜY  (colour blind)
 • So 1 out of 2 sons ( 1/2 ) are colour blind
 A  is incorrect because one possible son genotype (XᶜY) results in colour blindness.
 B  is incorrect because 1/4 refers to the proportion of all children, not specifically to sons.
 D  is incorrect because only sons that inherit Xᶜ from the mother are colour blind.
 If a question asks only about “sons” or “daughters”, only consider the relevant row or column of the Punnett square. A helpful strategy is to identify and highlight the sons or daughters in the Punnett square before doing any calculations. This makes it much easier to avoid errors.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A desert plant has thick leaves and a waxy cuticle.
 Scientists make three statements.
 • These features reduce water loss.
 • These features are inherited characteristics.
 • These features developed because the plant needed them.
 Which statements are correct?
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B.
 Statement 1 is correct  because  thick leaves  and a  waxy cuticle  are adaptive features that  reduce water loss . These features help desert plants survive in dry environments by reducing evaporation from the leaf surface.
 Statement 2 is correct  because these features are  inherited characteristics . Adaptive features are  controlled by genes  and can be  passed from parent plants to their offspring.
 Statement 3 is incorrect  because adaptations  do not develop because organisms need them . Instead, they arise through  natural selection  over many generations. Plants that already had traits such as thicker leaves or a waxy cuticle  survived better in dry conditions  and  passed these alleles to their offspring.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which organism is a producer?
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A.
 • A  producer  is an organism that  makes its own organic nutrients , usually by  photosynthesis  using energy from sunlight
 • Grass is a plant, so it acts as a producer at the first trophic level of a food chain, converting  light energy into chemical energy  stored in organic molecules
 B  is incorrect because a rabbit is a primary consumer, obtaining energy by feeding on plants.
 C  is incorrect because a hawk is a carnivore and a higher-level consumer, obtaining energy by eating other animals.
 D  is incorrect because fungi are decomposers, obtaining energy by breaking down dead organic material.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The sequence shows the events that occurs in a lake after fertiliser runoff enters the water.
 fertiliser runoff → algal bloom → X → dissolved oxygen decreases → fish die
 What is process X?
options: D. increased nitrate absorption by plants
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A.
 • When fertilisers containing  nitrates and other nutrients  enter a lake, they cause an  algal bloom  (rapid growth of algae)
 • When many algae die as part of their natural life cycle,  decomposers  break down the dead organic material
 • During this process, decomposers carry out  aerobic respiration , which uses large amounts of  dissolved oxygen  in the water
 • This increase in respiration by decomposers causes the  dissolved oxygen concentration to decrease , which can lead to the  death of aquatic organisms  that require oxygen
 B  is incorrect because increased photosynthesis would produce oxygen, not cause oxygen levels to decrease.
 C  is incorrect because fish feeding does not cause a large decrease in oxygen.
 D  is incorrect because nitrate absorption by plants occurs earlier in the process.

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram shows the structure of a bacterium.
  Which structure is commonly used in genetic modification to produce human proteins such as insulin?
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D.
 • Plasmids  are  small circular pieces of DNA  found in bacteria that can be easily removed and modified
 • In genetic modification, a  human gene  can be inserted into a plasmid using enzymes such as  restriction enzymes  and  DNA ligase
 • The  recombinant plasmid  is then placed back into a bacterium, which  replicates and expresses the human gene to produce the protein
 A  is incorrect because it represents ribosomes, which are involved in protein synthesis.
 B  is incorrect because it represents the circular bacterial chromosome, which contains the bacterium’s main DNA.
 C  is incorrect because it represents the cell wall, which provides structural support and protection.

set-8/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
Figure 1.1 is a diagram of a cell from the pancreas that produces and secretes digestive enzymes.
  Fig. 1.1
 State the names of the structures labelled P and Q in Fig. 1.1.
set-8/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
• P  = cell membrane  [1 mark]
 • Q  = nucleus   [1 mark]

set-8/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
Fig. 2.1 shows a representation of the nitrogen cycle. 
  Fig. 2.1
 State the names of the processes labelled A, B, and C in Fig. 2.1.
set-8/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
• A = nitrogen fixation  [1 mark]
 • B = decomposition   [1 mark]
 • C = nitrification  [1 mark]
 Accept ammonification for B
 Students often confuse nitrification with nitrogen fixation; remember that:
 • fixation  is removing nitrogen from the air
 • nitrification  is converting ammonia into nitrates

set-8/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
Glucose is produced in the leaves of plants during photosynthesis. This glucose is converted into a different carbohydrate for transport.
 Name the carbohydrate transported in the phloem.
set-8/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
• Sucrose  [1 mark]
 Do not say "sugar" or "glucose" is transported; plants move carbohydrate in the form of  sucrose .
 Amino acids are not carbohydrates, so no marks will be awarded for naming these compounds.

set-8/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
Fig. 4.1 shows a blue whale, a marine mammal that has a heart weighing up to 600 kg.
  Public domain, via  rawpixel
 Fig. 4.1
 In mammals, the wall of the left ventricle is approximately three times thicker than the wall of the right ventricle.
 Explain why the muscle wall of the left ventricle is significantly thicker than the muscle wall of the right ventricle.
set-8/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
• The left ventricle pumps blood to the whole body while the right ventricle only pumps blood to the lungs  OR  the left ventricle pumps blood further than the right ventricle  [1 mark]
 • The left ventricle needs to generate higher pressure / must contract with more force  [1 mark]
 Make sure you connect the destination of the blood (whole body vs. lungs) to the requirement for a thicker wall. Avoid vague statements such as "it needs more muscle" without explaining why.

set-8/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
A volunteer participated in a study looking at the pupil reflex. Fig. 5.1 shows the change in the volunteer's pupil diameter when a high-intensity light is switched on after 0.5 seconds.
  Fig. 5.1
 Calculate the rate of pupil constriction between 0.5 seconds and 2.5 seconds.
 Show your working and provide the correct units.
set-8/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
To calculate the rate of pupil constriction between 0.5 seconds and 2.5 seconds:
 • Determine the time that has passed, i.e. the change in the Y axis:
 = 2.5 - 0.5
 = 2 seconds
 • Determine the change in pupil diameter, i.e. the change in the X-axis:
  = 8 - 2
 = 6 mm
 • Determine the change in pupil diameter per second:
 • Divide the change in diameter by the number of seconds
 = 6 ÷ 2
 =  3 mm/s
 Award marks as follows:
 • 2 (seconds)  AND  6 (mm)  [1 mark]
 • 3  [1 mark]
 • mm/s  OR  mm s -1  [1 mark]
 Award full marks for the correct answer and units in the absence of other calculations.

set-8/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
Alpha-1 antitrypsin (AAT) is a protein that protects the lungs from damage. A deficiency in this protein is a genetic condition determined by a single gene.
 Fig. 6.1 shows the inheritance of this condition in a family.
  Fig. 6.1
 Using evidence from Fig. 6.1:
 (i) Explain whether the allele for AAT deficiency is dominant or recessive.
 [2]
 (ii) Determine the probability of individuals 5 and 6 having a second child who is a carrier.
 [1]
set-8/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
(i) The allele is:
 • Recessive  [1 mark]
 • Two unaffected parents / 5 and 6 have an affected child  [1 mark]
 (ii) The  probability of individuals 5 and 6 having a second child who is a carrier is:
 • 50%  OR  0.5  OR  1/2  [1 mark]
 Where two parents with the same phenotype produce a child with a different one, this indicates that the parents are heterozygous and the condition is recessive.

set-8/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.stem:
A student investigated the effect of pH on the activity of the enzyme amylase. Amylase breaks down starch into maltose. The student used the following method: 
 • Step 1:  set up four test-tubes, each containing the same volume of starch solution and amylase
 • Step 2:  add a different pH buffer solution to each test-tube
 • Step 3:  place all four test-tubes in a water-bath
 • Step 4:  every 30 seconds, remove a drop of the mixture from each test-tube and add it to a drop of iodine solution on a spotting tile
 • Step 5:  record the time taken for the iodine solution to remain yellow-brown (i.e. the point at which no colour change occurs)
 Fig. 1  shows the thermometer reading from the water bath at the start of the experiment.
 Fig. 1
  Record the temperature shown in  Fig. 1.
set-8/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.explanation:
• 36.9 °C   [1 mark]
 Accept values between 36.88-36.9
 Units must be included

set-8/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.stem:
A researcher investigated the populations of rabbits and foxes in a woodland area over 20 years.
 Fig. 2  shows the estimated populations over this time period.
 Fig. 2
  (i) Using  Fig. 2 , state the rabbit population at year 0.
 [1]
 (ii) Using  Fig. 2 , state the fox population at year 10.
 [1]
set-8/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.explanation:
(i) The rabbit population at year 0 is:
 • 400  [1 mark]
 (ii) The fox population at year 10 is:
 • 40  [1 mark]
 When reading values from a graph, make sure you read the correct axis. Here, the rabbit population is typically shown on one axis and the fox population on another. Take care to identify which line represents which organism before reading off the value.
